title: After Breaking the Engagement, I Bought a Stunning Power-Player as My Husband for Eight Hundred Taels
author: Zhen Shang Yan Shu
synopsis:
Jin Yu, the daughter of the wealthiest merchant in Jinling, is stunningly beautiful and possesses wealth that rivals a nation.
On the day of her engagement, her fiancé, a self-proclaimed high-minded scholar, rejected her in public: "A merchant's daughter reeks of copper; how could she be worthy of the integrity of a scholar like me?"
Jin Yu laughed. She turned around and burned a priceless rare book, then pointed at a destitute, starving, yet breathtakingly beautiful scholar by the roadside:
"You. Eight hundred taels. Come with me and be my live-in son-in-law."
Everyone laughed at Jin Yu for being insane, buying a useless piece of trash who was good for nothing but his face.
Little did they know, that scholar, Chen Yinyu, was a fragile, helpless "white lotus" in front of others. When wronged, he would only hide behind Jin Yu and whimper: "Wife, they are so fierce, I’m scared..."
Yet, behind the scenes, he was a ruthless, top-tier mastermind—possessing a photographic memory and a strategy for every contingency!
He helped her deal with toxic relatives, crushed her vicious ex, and expanded the Jin family's business across all thirty-six provinces of the Great Jing!
Later, in the Golden Palace, the top-ranking scholar Chen Yinyu rejected the Emperor's offer of marriage.
He knelt before the throne, looking innocent and frank: "Your subject has a weak stomach; I can only survive on the Jin family's handouts for the rest of my life."
The entire court: ...Is that your reason for filling the national treasury to the brim?
(Warning: The male lead is a top-tier "green tea," a master actor, soft only toward the female lead, and ruthless to everyone else!)

chapters.title: Publicly Breaking the Engagement, a Classic Trope
chapters.content:
Spring, the fifteenth year of Jinghe.

Outside the city of Jinling, Liufang Garden was hosting a literary gathering famous throughout the Jiangnan region.

Within the garden, willows swayed and wine cups floated along the winding streams. A group of self-styled elegant scholars, dressed in simple and refined Confucian robes, were either reciting poetry, playing the zither, or sipping tea, their faces masks of aloofness and self-restraint.

Jin Yu’s arrival instantly shattered this carefully crafted elegance.

She was dressed today in gold-woven cloud-mist brocade, with large, blooming peonies embroidered in peacock feather thread along the hem of her skirt. As she moved, the shimmering colors were dazzling enough to blind the eyes.

Her hair was adorned with extreme luxury: a gold-inlaid kingfisher feather hairpin, a pigeon-blood red gemstone pin, and a mutton-fat jade flat hairpin. With every light step she took, they emitted a crisp and extravagant tinkling sound.

Following behind her was a maid holding a sandalwood box, inside which lay a rare ancient book—a manuscript of "Guangling San" written by a master calligrapher of the previous dynasty.

This item was priceless; she had exhausted all her efforts to acquire it from a fallen nobleman for thirty thousand taels of silver.

She hadn't come today to pretend to be cultured; she had come to give her fiancé, Xun An, a man of great talent, a surprise.

Ever since Jin Yu entered the venue, the whispering around her had not ceased.

"Tsk, the eldest daughter of the Jin family is here again. Truly... vulgar beyond measure."

"Reeking of copper. I don't know what Brother Xun An sees in her."

"What else could it be? Naturally, he’s eyeing the Jin family’s immense wealth!"

Jin Yu turned a deaf ear to these sour remarks. With a smile of certainty on her lips, she walked straight through the crowd toward the "Yongfeng Terrace," the highest point of the gathering.

Her fiancé, Xun An, was standing there.

Xun An wore a washed-out cyan Confucian robe. He stood tall with a refined face, engaged in high-minded discussion with several famous scholars of Jinling.

When he saw Jin Yu, a flash of impatience and disgust crossed his eyes, but it was immediately replaced by an inexplicable excitement.

This was the moment he had been waiting for.

Jin Yu stepped forward gracefully and personally presented the sandalwood box. Her voice carried a hint of excitement she hadn't even noticed herself: "Xun An, this is the rare manuscript of 'Guangling San' I found for you. I hope you win the top spot in next month's provincial examination."

A collective gasp echoed around them.

A rare manuscript of "Guangling San"! That was a treasure that could not be bought even with money!

Everyone expected Xun An to accept it with wild joy, but instead, he recoiled as if he had been burned by something filthy.

Standing on the third step, he looked down at Jin Yu, his voice ringing out clearly across the entire Liufang Garden.

"Miss Jin, please forgive me, but I cannot accept this."

The smile on Jin Yu's face stiffened slightly.

Xun An continued in a tone of deep, pained regret: "We scholars should stand in the world with integrity and pass down a clean reputation! You reek of copper and are covered in gaudy jewels; your heart has long been blinded by worldly possessions. How could you possibly understand our reverence for the wisdom of the sages?"

He spoke righteously, as if he were a pine tree standing proudly in the snow.

"Such a rare, world-renowned manuscript is nothing but a toy for you to flaunt your wealth! In my eyes, it is the continuation of culture and a symbol of integrity!"

"Today, in front of all the famous scholars of Jinling, I, Xun An, must say—"

He took a deep breath. "I, Xun An, am ashamed to associate with merchants! I am breaking off this engagement!"

Silence fell over the garden.

All eyes were fixed on Jin Yu—some filled with sympathy, some with schadenfreude, but most waiting to see her cry and make a fool of herself.

In the corner of the crowd, several merchants dressed in silk with shrewd eyes were exchanging knowing glances with the manager of the Liu family firm.

Jin Yu stood there quietly, the color draining from her face inch by inch.

She did not cry, nor did she make a scene. Instead, in the deathly silence, she let out a low laugh.

"Heh... hehe..."

The laughter was crisp, yet carried an indescribable sense of mockery and chill.

Xun An felt a shiver run down his spine at her laughter and frowned, scolding, "What are you laughing at? Am I not right?"

Jin Yu raised her eyes, her usually bright and spirited gaze now piercingly sharp. "I’m laughing at you, Master Xun."

She took a step forward, forcing the man on the steps to meet her gaze: "Your so-called integrity—is it to live comfortably off the Jin family’s silver, stay in the villa provided by the Jin family, and use the connections the Jin family paved for you, all while acting as if the Jin family’s money dirties your hands and stains your reputation?"

"You..." Xun An’s face turned the color of liver. He hadn't expected Jin Yu to expose these things in public and, for a moment, didn't know how to argue back.

Jin Yu didn't give him the chance. She lifted her chin, her smile even colder: "Three years ago, your family was destitute, and you couldn't even afford the travel expenses to the capital for the exams. It was my father who saw your plight, set up this engagement, and funded your studies. For these three years, which part of your food and clothing wasn't paid for by the Jin family? Now that you feel your studies have achieved some success, you can't wait to trample on the Jin family’s face to earn your so-called high-minded reputation?"

"You... you are spouting nonsense!"

Xun An was humiliated and angry, left with only pale excuses. "I have long since settled my debts with your Jin family!"

"Settled?" Jin Yu sounded as if she had heard the greatest joke in the world.

She turned abruptly and barked at her maid, who was already frozen in shock: "Light it!"

The maid trembled. "Eldest Miss, this... this is worth thirty thousand taels of silver!"

"I said light it!" Jin Yu’s voice was devoid of warmth.

The maid dared not disobey again. With trembling hands, she lit a fire starter and brought it to the sandalwood box.

"No!" a book-loving scholar cried out in horror.

A flash of greed and reluctance crossed Xun An’s eyes, but to maintain his "integrity," he could only watch.

The flames roared to life, instantly consuming the ancient book filled with elegance.

The scent of ink turned into a charred stench in the blaze, and the priceless manuscript became a handful of flying ash in the blink of an eye.

The firelight reflected on Jin Yu’s resolute face. As she watched the flames, it was as if she were burning away her own foolish devotion of the past three years.

She turned and declared to the ashen-faced Xun An, word by word:

"Since Master Xun feels that copper stinks and that my Jin family is unworthy of your integrity."

"Then fine. Today, I, Jin Yu, will use this 'stinking' copper to buy a husband in this city of Jinling who is a hundred times better than you!"

The moment these words were spoken, the crowd erupted in an uproar!

Jin Yu didn't even look at their reactions. She turned directly to a plump woman waiting in the crowd—the most famous matchmaker in Jinling, Mother Wang—and gave her order.

"Mother Wang, I’ll give you one stick of incense's time."

She pulled a thick stack of banknotes from her sleeve and slapped them into Mother Wang’s arms. A rough glance showed at least a thousand taels.

"Go, go to the street right now and drag me a man!"

"There is only one requirement: he must have a clean background, and his face must be a hundred times better-looking than this great scholar Xun’s!"

"As long as he is willing to marry into the Jin family, this thousand taels is your reward! His settlement fee will be calculated separately!"

Mother Wang’s eyes lit up at the sight of the banknotes, and she was nearly bursting with joy. She replied repeatedly, "Oh, my dear Eldest Miss! Just leave it to me! I guarantee I’ll find you someone more handsome than Pan An!"

With that, she lifted her skirt and rolled out of Liufang Garden as fast as a meatball.

All the scholars in the garden were stunned.

Buy... buy a husband?

What a shocking and scandalous act!

Xun An’s face had turned from liver-colored to a deep, bruised purple. He felt as if he had been stripped naked and thrown into the middle of a busy market.

Jin Yu was using the most direct and brutal way to tell him: The integrity you are so proud of is not even worth as much as a handsome face in my eyes!

Time ticked by, and the atmosphere in the garden became bizarrely tense.

Jin Yu stood there with her arms crossed, waiting as if for a good show to begin.

In less than the time it took for a stick of incense to burn, Mother Wang returned.

She was panting, her face full of joy, dragging a thin, tall figure behind her.

"Eldest Miss! Eldest Miss! I found him! Look at this quality, this build—I guarantee you’ll be satisfied!"

Mother Wang pushed the person behind her forward as if presenting a treasure.

The man stumbled and nearly fell. When he steadied himself and looked up, the noise in the entire Liufang Garden seemed to have been pressed on pause.

He was... an exceptionally handsome man.

He wore a washed-out, coarse mourning robe. His clothes were tattered and stained with mud.

His frame was thin and tall, his face appearing somewhat haggard from long-term hunger, and his complexion was a cold, almost translucent white.

Yet, none of this could hide the face that could only be described as stunning.

His eyebrows were like distant mountains, his eyes like cold stars. The bridge of his nose was as high and straight as if carved from jade, and his lips were pale, yet they curved into a heart-stopping arc.

He was like a snow lotus growing out of the mud—clean, cold, and possessing a fragile, shattered quality, yet hidden deep within those eyes was a fire that refused to be extinguished.

Xun An prided himself on his own handsome looks, but compared to the man before him, he suddenly felt like an unrefined lump of clay.

Jin Yu’s eyes lit up instantly. As a seasoned connoisseur of beauty, she was satisfied with this face to the extreme.

She walked down the steps, one by one, until she stood before him.

The surrounding air seemed to freeze. Xun An stared fixedly at the man, the jealousy in his eyes almost turning into tangible blades.

Jin Yu, however, couldn't be bothered to spare him even a glance.

She walked up to the destitute scholar and, with a slender, jade-like finger, gently lifted his chin.

"What is your name?"

The man lowered his eyes, his long lashes casting shadows beneath them. His voice was clear and cold, with a hint of hoarseness.

"Chen Yinyu."

Jin Yu nodded in satisfaction, her red lips parting slightly as she asked the earth-shattering question.

"You—are you for sale?"

chapters.title: You’ll Have to Pay More
chapters.content:
As soon as these words were spoken, the entire scene fell into a deathly silence.

Everyone looked like a chicken whose neck had been throttled, their eyes wide, staring at Jin Yu in disbelief.

They had heard of buying and selling goods, land, and even slaves.

But to ask a living, breathing scholar on the street if he was "for sale"—this... this was simply unheard-of absurdity!

Xun An’s complexion shifted from a liver-like purple to an ashen blue; he was so angry he felt as if his lungs might burst.

This was an insult!

This was the most naked, blatant insult to him and to all the scholars in the world!

He glared at Chen Yinyu, waiting for him to fly into a rage, waiting for him to flick his sleeves and storm off, waiting for him to use the integrity of a scholar to trample Jin Yu’s face into the dirt!

However, Chen Yinyu’s reaction exceeded everyone’s expectations.

He was not angry; there wasn't even a ripple of emotion.

Those eyes, cold as a frozen pool, slowly lifted, his long lashes fluttering like butterfly wings.

His gaze drifted past Jin Yu toward a spot not far outside Liufang Garden.

There, a man in a short jacket was wringing his hands anxiously, standing beside a flatbed cart that held a thin wooden coffin.

That was Boss Wang from the coffin shop in the east of the city, waiting to collect his money so he could lay his mother to rest.

Chen Yinyu’s gaze lingered on the coffin for a moment; the grief and resolve that flashed in the depths of his eyes were too quick for anyone to catch.

When he turned his gaze back to Jin Yu, his eyes had returned to the stillness of an ancient well.

He looked at the thick stack of banknotes in Jin Yu’s hand, then at her face, which was so vivid it was almost aggressive.

Then, his thin lips parted, and he uttered a few words.

"You want to buy me?"

"You’ll have to pay more."

Boom!

The crowd exploded.

Everyone thought they had misheard!

Not only did this man not refuse, but he was actually... raising the price on the spot?!

The muscles in Xun An’s face twitched uncontrollably, and he nearly lost his footing. He had anticipated countless possibilities, but never this one!

"You... you refined scoundrel!"

Xun An pointed at Chen Yinyu, trembling with rage. "You have completely disgraced all the scholars in the world! For the sake of mere pelf, you would abandon your integrity and shame!"

He spoke with stern severity, attempting to use the cudgel of morality to nail Chen Yinyu to the pillar of shame.

Yet, Chen Yinyu wouldn't even spare him a glance. It was as if the only thing left in his world was the woman before him, who radiated the scent of money.

Completely ignoring Xun An’s roar, he began to quote his price to Jin Yu.

"My mother’s body is not yet cold; to lay her to rest requires fifty taels of silver."

His voice was calm, as if he were discussing the most mundane business.

"You have just been rejected in marriage and are feeling stifled; you need someone by your side to hold your ground, accompany you for meals, and do your bidding. That is fifty taels per month."

"That Master Xun," he glanced with the corner of his eye at the fuming Xun An, "seems to be pestering you incessantly and will surely be a nuisance in the future. To fend off this rotten peach blossom for you, that is one hundred taels per month."

With every word he spoke, Jin Yu’s eyes grew brighter. By the end, she was ready to clap her hands and laugh out loud.

Heavens!

What a treasure of a man!

Look at this clear logic, this precise needs analysis, this professional standard of itemized pricing!

He knew exactly what she needed. This wasn't just buying a vase or an ornament; this was buying a stress-free, efficient solution!

In Jin Yu’s eyes, any problem that could be solved with money was not a problem at all.

Her heart settled, and she gave a clear, sharp cry: "Deal!"

Without another word, she pulled another stack of banknotes from her sleeve and, without even looking at them, stuffed them into Chen Yinyu’s arms along with the previous ones.

"Is this enough?"

The stack of banknotes was thick and heavy.

Chen Yinyu lowered his eyes, his long, slender fingers pinching the notes, and began to count them one by one in front of everyone.

His movements were not fast, but they held a strange sense of rhythm. That composure and focus caused the surrounding clamor to quiet down.

"Eight hundred taels."

He finished counting and arrived at an accurate figure. He then looked up at Jin Yu and stated calmly, "According to the previous quote, this amount is enough to buy out all of my time for the next four years."

Jin Yu was thoroughly pleased by his "strictly business" demeanor. She waved her hand with heroic flair: "I’m not buying four years; I’m buying your whole life!"

"Enter my Jin family, be my live-in son-in-law. You are mine in life, and you shall be my ghost in death! These eight hundred taels are your settlement fee!"

Upon hearing this, Chen Yinyu’s hand holding the banknotes paused slightly.

He looked deeply at Jin Yu, as if confirming the weight of her words.

Jin Yu met his gaze frankly, her eyes firm, without a hint of a joke.

Finally, Chen Yinyu nodded.

"Very well."

He carefully folded the thick stack of banknotes and tucked them into his chest, his movements as if he were placing the destination of his remaining life.

Only after doing all this did he finally turn around and look squarely at the nearly insane Xun An.

"Brother Xun."

His voice remained cold, but with a hint of sharpness that was hard to detect.

"You are noble, you look down on worldly wealth, but do not stand in the way of me burying my mother."

He straightened his thin, lean back, his words ringing with conviction.

"The *Classic of Filial Piety* says: 'Our body, hair, and skin are given by our parents; to not damage them is the beginning of filial piety. To establish oneself and practice the Way, to make a name for oneself in later generations, and thus bring glory to one's parents, is the end of filial piety.'"

"I am currently unable to establish myself, and I have no path to practice the Way. I can only first fulfill the duty of a son and let my mother be laid to rest."

"I am selling myself to bury my mother; what wrong is there in that?"

His words were resonant, instantly trading the label of "greedy" for the halo of "utmost filial piety"!

Xun An was rendered speechless, his face turning the color of a pig’s liver. He stammered for a long time, unable to utter a single word.

Indeed, of all virtues, filial piety comes first.

The man was selling himself to bury his mother—what great filial piety! What right did an outsider have to point fingers here?

The eyes of the surrounding crowd changed instantly.

From initial contempt, they turned to sympathy, and even a touch of admiration.

Jin Yu looked at Chen Yinyu, the appreciation in her eyes nearly overflowing.

Not only was his face handsome, but his tongue was sharp, and he could instantly seize the moral high ground!

These eight hundred taels were well spent!

"Mother Wang!" Jin Yu, in high spirits, called out to the matchmaker standing to the side, who was already stunned. "Bring the brush and ink!"

Mother Wang awoke as if from a dream and hurriedly pulled the prepared stationery and a marriage contract from her bag.

Jin Yu took the brush and wrote her name with a flourish on the contract, then specifically added a few clauses at the end.

"First, after marrying into the family, you must uphold male virtue and not linger in houses of pleasure."

"Second, you may not take concubines; I am the only one in the back courtyard."

"Third, in all things, put me first and obey your wife."

After writing, she handed the contract and the brush to Chen Yinyu.

Chen Yinyu didn't even look at the clauses; he picked up the brush and wrote the three characters "Chen Yinyu" neatly beside Jin Yu’s name, then pressed his thumbprint.

The handwriting was elegant and proud.

The contract was sealed!

The moment the brush touched the paper, Chen Yinyu’s entire aura changed.

He set down the brush and bowed deeply to Jin Yu, his movements as standard as if he had practiced them a thousand times.

Then, he looked up and addressed Jin Yu with a natural, submissive tone, using the brand-new title.

"Wife."

chapters.title: Inspecting the Goods! This Money Was Well Spent
chapters.content:
The wheels of the Jin family carriage were rimmed with high-quality iron-pear wood, and one could barely hear a bump while traveling on the bluestone road.

Chen Yinyu sat in the corner of the carriage, eyes closed, seemingly unconcerned with anything outside. However, his slightly trembling eyelashes betrayed his far-from-calm heart.

Soon, the carriage stopped in front of a magnificent mansion.

"Young Miss, Son-in-law, we have arrived home."

The coachman’s voice came through.

Chen Yinyu opened his eyes and followed Jin Yu off the carriage.

Even though he had been prepared, his breath hitched imperceptibly the moment he saw the main gate of the Jin residence.

The vermilion-lacquered gate was inlaid with pure copper beast-head knockers, two majestic stone lions stood taller than he was, and the servants sweeping the entrance were all dressed in fine cotton cloth.

And that was just the outside.

Stepping into the Jin residence, it was a world of its own.

The gaps between the bluestone slabs on the ground seemed to be filled with gold dust, shimmering with fine, dazzling light under the setting sun.

The air was filled with a faint, expensive scent of sandalwood, overpowering the fragrance of all the flowers and plants.

Pavilions and towers, carved beams and painted rafters, the glazed tiles flowed with color in the sunset, resembling the dwelling of immortals.

Chen Yinyu walked along, his expression calm, but in his heart, he had already estimated the value of the mansion.

The conclusion was: immeasurable.

The loyal old steward, Wang Quan, came to greet them. He first bowed respectfully to Jin Yu, then cast a look of extreme complexity at Chen Yinyu behind her.

His young mistress had actually... bought a man to be a live-in son-in-law!

And she did it in front of the whole city!

Wang Quan’s heart was pounding. He leaned toward Jin Yu and lowered his voice: "Miss, this... this man’s background is unknown, is he reliable? I hope he isn't a swindler..."

Jin Yu waved her hand with complete indifference, her tone as casual as if she were discussing a newly purchased piece of porcelain.

"Just an ornament. As long as it looks good, that’s enough."

She cast a sidelong glance at Chen Yinyu, who stood with his eyes lowered and gaze averted. Her voice was just loud enough for the person behind her to hear.

"If it’s not useful, I can always return it."

Chen Yinyu’s forward stride faltered imperceptibly, but he immediately resumed his pace, as if he hadn't heard the stinging remark at all.

Jin Yu instructed, "Uncle Wang, take him to the 'Yuqing Pavilion.' Find someone to help him bathe and change, and bring him to see me once he’s cleaned up."

"Yes, Miss."

Wang Quan accepted the order. Despite his lingering doubts, he respectfully gestured for Chen Yinyu to follow.

"Sir, please follow me."

Hot water had already been prepared; the massive white jade tub was scattered with medicinal herbs and flower petals to soothe the muscles and invigorate the blood.

Two pretty maids stood to the side with their hands folded, ready to step forward and serve.

Chen Yinyu said only a single, cool sentence: "I will do it myself."

He dismissed the maids and, left alone, shed his dusty, worn Confucian robe and stepped into the tub.

The warm water instantly enveloped his body, washing away the fatigue and dust of his journey.

Half an hour later, when he emerged from behind the screen dressed in the cloud-patterned red robes that Jin Yu had ordered prepared, the maids waiting outside all gasped in unison.

If the Chen Yinyu from before was a piece of unpolished jade covered in dust, then the man before them now was a rare treasure that, once wiped clean, suddenly radiated peerless brilliance.

The red robe was as vibrant as fire, making his already cold, pale skin look even more like snow. His long, ink-black hair hung loosely over his shoulders; his brows and eyes were like a painting, his lips naturally flushed without the need for rouge.

He stood before the large dressing mirror and looked quietly at his own reflection.

The man in the mirror had sharp, piercing eyes and a profound gaze—there was no trace left of the meek and submissive demeanor he showed others.

He slowly curled his lips into a meaningful smile.

Night fell.

After finishing all the business matters for the firm, Jin Yu strolled leisurely toward the Yuqing Pavilion.

She wanted to see exactly what kind of "merchandise" her eight hundred taels of silver had bought.

Pushing open the door, a refreshing scent of tea greeted her. Chen Yinyu was sitting by the table, brewing tea for her.

He had changed out of the striking red robe and was wearing a moon-white casual gown. His long hair was loosely held up by a jade hairpin. In the candlelight, the contours of his profile were soft and handsome, like a freehand landscape painting.

Hearing the door open, he looked up and offered Jin Yu a faint smile.

"You’ve returned, my lady."

Jin Yu gave an "un" sound, walked straight to the head seat, and sat down. Without ceremony, she picked up the tea he had just brewed, but did not drink it.

Like the most fastidious antique dealer, she began her "inspection" process.

"Lift your head."

Chen Yinyu obediently raised his chin, revealing the long, elegant lines of his neck.

Jin Yu reached out two fingers to pinch his jaw, applying just enough pressure to force his mouth slightly open.

"Good teeth."

She then grabbed his hands and examined them carefully. His fingers were long and slender with distinct knuckles; there was a thin layer of calluses on his palms—the mark of years of holding a brush, not the rough calluses of manual labor.

"The hands are passable, too."

Jin Yu released him and leaned back in her chair, her eyes carrying a hint of playfulness.

"Tell me, besides being good-looking, what else are you good for?"

She had expected Chen Yinyu to spout some pedantic nonsense like "I can read" or "I can write."

To her surprise, Chen Yinyu set down his teacup, stood up, walked behind her, and reached out to knead her shoulders with just the right amount of pressure.

His fingers had the perfect temperature, and his strength landed precisely on her sore acupoints, instantly soothing the body she had kept tense all day.

Jin Yu narrowed her eyes in comfort, her satisfaction with this "commodity" rising a few notches.

Just as she was drifting toward sleep, a warm breath accompanied by a low, magnetic voice brushed against her ear.

"My lady, what service do you require tonight?"

Chen Yinyu leaned down slightly, his warm breath hitting Jin Yu’s sensitive earlobe, sending a faint shiver through her.

"Company for conversation, or..."

He deliberately drew out the final syllable, the suggestive implication in his words self-evident.

"...warming the bed?"

Jin Yu’s eyes snapped open!

She grabbed the hand Chen Yinyu had on her shoulder and pulled him in front of her. The distance between them closed instantly, close enough to see their reflections in each other's eyes.

Chen Yinyu’s gaze was damp, like a startled young deer—innocent and pitiful—yet the words he spoke were bold to the extreme!

Jin Yu stared at him for a long moment, then suddenly laughed.

This was no little white rabbit; this was a little fox wearing a rabbit skin!

"Heh, you’re quite quick on the uptake."

She thought to herself: Buying such an obedient, sensible, and interesting beauty for eight hundred taels is far better than keeping that self-important master, Xun An!

This money was well spent!

Jin Yu let go of his hand and tossed a silk quilt from the wardrobe by the bed onto the daybed by the window.

"Tonight, you sleep there."

Her tone was flat and brooked no argument.

"Yes, my lady."

Chen Yinyu had no objections; he picked up the quilt and obediently walked toward the daybed.

Jin Yu watched his submissive back, the thrill of controlling everything putting her in an excellent mood.

However, while the Jin residence was peaceful, a tavern in the south of the city presented a different scene.

Xun An was downing cup after cup of bitter wine, his face so gloomy it seemed ready to drip water.

The discussion from a nearby table drifted into his ears, word for word.

"Have you heard? The eldest daughter of the Jin family bought a live-in son-in-law today!"

"Tsk tsk, I saw the scene! She bought a scholar, some guy named Chen Yinyu. He’s so handsome, he looks like Pan An!"

"Isn't that the truth! Compared to that Master Chen, the previous one, Xun An, is like heaven and earth! No wonder the eldest Miss Jin didn't fancy him. Master Xun has lost miserably this time!"

"Bang!"

Xun An slammed his wine cup onto the table, shattering the porcelain.

"Chen Yinyu... Jin Yu..."

He gritted his teeth as he spat out the names, a cold, venomous glint flashing in his eyes.

You pair of wretches dare to humiliate me like this? He would not let this go!

Three days later was the Flowing Cup Poetry Gathering, an event all the scholars in the city looked forward to. All the prominent literati and refined gentlemen in the city would attend.

At the gathering, in front of everyone, he would expose Chen Yinyu’s vanity and greed, and make Jin Yu, that merchant woman reeking of copper, the laughingstock of the entire city!

chapters.title: Rumors Spread, the Green Tea Strategist Goes Online
chapters.content:
The next morning, Jin Yu was awakened by a faint tickling sensation.

She opened her sleepy eyes and met a pair of focused, earnest pupils.

Daylight filtered through the window lattice, casting a soft glow that outlined the profile of the person before her, making him look even more refined and ethereal.

Chen Yinyu was sitting on the edge of the bed, holding a delicate eyebrow pencil, carefully drawing her brows.

It was clearly his first time doing such a thing; his movements were clumsy and stiff. His fingers gripping the pencil were taut, his expression as serious as if he were reviewing state affairs.

Jin Yu didn't move, leaning lazily against the pillow and enjoying this rare moment of leisure.

The air was filled with the clean, crisp scent of soap from his body, mixed with a hint of ink—it smelled very pleasant.

"Your hands are quite unpracticed," she remarked, deliberately critiquing him.

Chen Yinyu’s movements paused, his long eyelashes fluttering slightly. His voice was soft and tinged with nervous sweetness: "It is Yinyu’s clumsiness that has disturbed your rest, my lady."

As he spoke, he moved to pull away.

"Who told you to stop?" Jin Yu grabbed his wrist. As their skin touched, she could feel how thin his wrist was and his slightly cool body temperature.

She closed her eyes lazily: "Continue."

"...Yes."

Chen Yinyu stared at her steadily for a few seconds, a hint of a smile that no one else could detect flashing deep in his eyes, before he returned to his meek and submissive expression, continuing his clumsy yet incredibly earnest task of drawing her brows.

Jin Yu calculated silently in her heart.

Eight hundred taels to buy an eye-pleasing ornament that could also warm the bed, and now, she had unlocked the eyebrow-drawing service.

Hmm, this deal wasn't a loss—it was actually a bargain.

Just as she was enjoying this "value-added service," a flurry of hurried footsteps sounded outside the door, accompanied by the anxious shouts of the steward, Wang Quan.

"Miss! Miss, it's bad! Something terrible has happened!"

With a "bang," the door was flung open.

Wang Quan didn't care about propriety anymore. His old face was flushed red, his forehead covered in beads of sweat, and he rushed in, gasping for air.

He immediately saw the man by the bed drawing his mistress's brows and choked for a moment, but he was quickly pulled back to reality by more urgent matters.

Jin Yu slowly sat up, her face darkening at being disturbed: "Uncle Wang, is the house on fire this early in the morning?"

Seeing this, Chen Yinyu very perceptively put down the eyebrow pencil and retreated to the side, standing with his hands folded and eyes lowered, minimizing his presence as much as possible.

"Miss, it really is a disaster!"

Wang Quan stamped his feet in anxiety, "Outside... it's spreading like wildfire!"

"Spreading what?" Jin Yu picked up a robe and draped it over her shoulders, unconcerned.

In the business world, what kind of storms hadn't she seen? It was just a few rumors.

Wang Quan said with a mournful face, "Everyone outside is saying... that you used the Jin family's power to forcibly seize a man! They say... that Master Chen was a clean, upright scholar who had to sell himself to bury his mother, but you forcibly bought him as a slave and forced him to be your live-in husband!"

His voice grew quieter as he spoke, stealing glances at the expressions of Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu.

The rumor was fabricated with vivid detail, painting Jin Yu as a lawless, bullying merchant woman, while Chen Yinyu was cast as a tragic, peerless "little white flower" forced into submission.

Jin Yu’s expression turned cold, inch by inch.

This wasn't just simple gossip; this was a blatant attempt to smear the reputation of the Jin family!

A merchant family valued reputation above all else. Once the label of "using power to bully others" was pinned on them, who would dare do business with the Jin family in the future?

This tactic was truly vicious!

"Xun An."

Jin Yu squeezed these two words through her teeth.

Aside from that insecure yet arrogant hypocrite, she couldn't think of anyone else who would use such low-down, dirty tactics.

"Miss is wise!"

Wang Quan quickly agreed, "I sent people to investigate. The news first started spreading from those teahouses in the south of the city that Xun An frequents!"

"Good, very good!"

Jin Yu laughed out of extreme anger and slammed her hand on the table. "Gather all the servants in the manor, bring clubs! Today, I want to see whether his mouth is harder, or my club is!"

She had always been a woman of her word. Before the words even left her lips, she had already stood up, her brows filled with a murderous aura.

Daring to touch her purse was the same as touching her lifeline!

"Yes!" Wang Quan received the order and turned to go summon the men.

But at that moment, a slender figure quietly blocked Jin Yu's path.

Chen Yinyu reached out and gently tugged at her wide sleeve—the force was light, yet impossible to ignore.

Jin Yu stopped in her tracks and looked down at him impatiently. "What are you doing? Scared?"

She assumed he was trying to persuade her to let the matter drop.

Chen Yinyu, however, looked up. Those beautiful eyes were filled with clear, limpid worry, like a pool of spring water stirred by a breeze—innocent and pure.

"My lady."

He spoke softly, his voice gentle and warm.

"Smashing the teahouse is easy, and venting one's anger for a moment is satisfying."

"But if we confirm our reputation for 'bullying others with power' because of this, wouldn't we be falling right into the trap set by the person behind this?"

"When that time comes, the power of public opinion will be like a thousand mouths melting gold and a thousand tongues destroying bones. Who would dare trust the Jin family's business in the future?"

Every word he spoke was clear and logical, precisely dissecting the pros and cons. Every syllable hit the points Jin Yu cared about most.

The raging fire in Jin Yu's heart was mostly extinguished by his few gentle, soft-spoken words.

She sat back down in her chair and frowned. "Then what do you suggest? We can't just let them slander us like this!"

Chen Yinyu's eyelashes lowered slightly, masking the flash of cold light in his eyes.

He smiled softly, his tone carrying a sense of certainty, as if he had everything under control: "Since Xun An wants to use public opinion to kill, then we... shall use public opinion to kill him back."

Jin Yu raised an eyebrow, signaling him to continue.

"He has molded Yinyu into a victim to win the world's sympathy, thereby attacking you and the Jin family. This is his display of weakness."

"If we storm over there aggressively, it will be a case of the strong bullying the weak, which will only make the rumors spread even more wildly."

"Therefore, we must also display weakness."

"Display weakness?" Jin Yu was puzzled.

"Yes."

Chen Yinyu nodded. "Three days from now is the Orchid Pavilion Poetry Gathering. All the scholars and refined gentlemen of the city will be there, and Xun An will surely be among them. Please, my lady, take Yinyu with you."

Jin Yu understood his meaning instantly. He wanted to turn the tide of public opinion at the poetry gathering in front of all the scholars.

But she still had some doubts: "Can you handle it? That bunch of scholars are sharper with their tongues than ten people combined."

Upon hearing this, Chen Yinyu showed no cowardice; instead, he smiled shyly, his expression as clean as a child who knew nothing of the world.

He lowered his head slightly, his voice as light as a feather brushing against the heart.

"Yinyu is slow of speech; I cannot out-argue them."

"But..."

He lifted his eyes, the rims turning slightly red, shimmering with moisture, enough to make one's heart tremble.

"Yinyu knows how to cry."

Jin Yu: "..."

She looked at this man who had said "I know how to cry" with such a straight face, and for a moment, she didn't know how to react.

What kind of secret weapon for victory was this?

Relying on tears to drown the opponent?

Although she felt this method was absurdly ridiculous, looking at Chen Yinyu's "pitiful and touching" yet cunningly hidden expression, Jin Yu nodded in spite of herself.

"Fine. I want to see how you cry your way into a brilliant future."

She decided to take a gamble, and the stake was the "military advisor" she had bought for eight hundred taels of silver.

Having received Jin Yu's approval, Chen Yinyu immediately resumed his actions.

He turned toward the wardrobe and began to carefully select his "battle armor" for the "battlefield" three days later.

Jin Yu watched him with great interest.

She saw him pass over rows of bright, luxurious silk garments, and finally, from the very corner, he pulled out a simple, plain, cyan-colored Confucian robe.

The cyan fabric was plain, even carrying a sense of age from being washed many times.

He held the robe up against himself. The moon-white inner garment set off the cyan, making his frame look even thinner and his temperament colder, as if a gust of wind could blow him over.

Jin Yu understood instantly.

This wasn't just choosing clothes; this was clearly crafting a "victim" persona!

She looked at Chen Yinyu's harmless profile, the corners of her lips curling upward uncontrollably.

This little fox in a rabbit's skin was becoming more and more interesting!

chapters.title: Prelude to the Poetry Gathering, The Little White Rabbit Enters the Wolf Pack
chapters.content:
On the third day of the third lunar month, the Shangsi Festival, it was the perfect time for the "winding stream" poetry gathering.

The Jin family's carriage rolled through the city, almost crushing the spring scenery beneath its wheels, and stopped at the entrance of the Orchid Pavilion gathering outside the city.

The carriage curtain was lifted, and a soft cloud-brocade shoe adorned with an Eastern pearl stepped out first.

Following that, Jin Yu bent down and emerged.

Today, she wore a wide-sleeved silk dress with a pattern of golden peonies and intertwined branches. The hundred butterflies embroidered in gold thread on the hem were so lifelike that they seemed ready to flutter away with her every step.

Her hair was piled high, and a nine-tailed golden phoenix hairpin with dangling pearls swayed, making her bright and imposing face appear even more dazzling. Her noble aura was so overwhelming it almost eclipsed the gentle spring light.

Behind her, Chen Yinyu followed closely.

In stark contrast to Jin Yu's radiant brilliance, he wore only that cyan Confucian robe she had watched him select—the one washed until it was somewhat faded.

The cyan was so plain it was almost dull, which only served to highlight his cold, pale skin and thin frame, his brows and eyes carrying a fragility that could not withstand the wind and rain.

He kept his head slightly lowered, his long eyelashes casting a faint shadow beneath his eyes. He looked exactly like a young wife who had been forcibly dragged out by a wealthy woman to see the world, suffering all sorts of grievances yet daring not to speak.

The two walked one after the other—one as flamboyant as fire, the other as cold as water. This highly impactful combination instantly attracted the attention of everyone present.

The Orchid Pavilion was already crowded with guests.

The stream gurgled, and soft mats were laid out on both banks. Scholars and refined guests gathered in twos and threes, either engaging in high-minded discussions or reciting poetry in low voices.

In the crowd, an elderly man with white hair and a refined face sat at the head; he was the judge of this poetry gathering, the famous Confucian scholar—Master Li.

He held a scroll in his hand, his expression serious, his gaze like a torch as he scanned every junior present.

However, when Jin Yu appeared with Chen Yinyu, the originally elegant and harmonious atmosphere seemed to have been pressed on pause by an invisible hand.

All conversation ceased abruptly.

Countless gazes—some disdainful, some curious, some pitying—shot toward them, like countless fine needles pricking their skin.

After a brief, deathly silence, whispers rose like a tide.

"Look, that's Jin Yu, the merchant's daughter of the Jin family! I heard she spent money to buy a man as a live-in son-in-law!"

"Tsk tsk, the world is truly going downhill. Look at the one behind her; he looks like a decent man, but what a pity—he chose to debase himself, sacrificing the integrity of a scholar for money."

"Shh, keep it down! Look at him, thin as a bamboo pole, with such a look of grievance. I wonder how much torture he's endured? Truly pitiful..."

Jin Yu remained expressionless, her long nails almost digging into her palms.

She had expected this scene, but hearing these filthy words with her own ears still ignited a nameless fire in her heart.

Pitiful?

The Jin family provided him with the best food and drink; how was this pretty boy pitiful?

Just then, a particularly harsh voice rang out from the center of the crowd, carrying undisguised contempt and hostility.

"I wondered who had such a grand entrance; so it is the eldest Miss Jin."

The crowd looked toward the sound and saw Xun An in white, holding a folding fan, standing out like a crane in a flock of chickens, surrounded by a group of students.

His upright face wore a hypocritical smile, but his eyes were like poisoned blades, shooting straight at Jin Yu, then falling lightly on Chen Yinyu with even greater disdain.

He deliberately raised his volume to ensure everyone present could hear:

"This is a refined place for scholars to meet and exchange poetry. It is one thing for the wealthy Miss Jin to be ignorant of the rules, but to bring a lowly house slave in here—does that not sully the purity of this Orchid Pavilion and offend our eyes?"

Xun An emphasized the words "house slave" heavily. As soon as he finished, a chorus of mocking laughter erupted from the surroundings.

Xun An's words were not only an insult to Chen Yinyu but also nailed Jin Yu to the pillar of shame as "crude, vulgar, and bullying."

Jin Yu's face darkened instantly, cold light flashing in her phoenix eyes. She was about to speak—

She was best at using silver to shatter others' pride and using facts to shut their mouths!

However, before she could speak, her sleeve was tugged by a very light force.

Jin Yu was startled and looked down.

She saw that Chen Yinyu had shrunk behind her like a frightened rabbit.

He revealed only his clear, panicked eyes, his long eyelashes seemingly still hung with morning dew, wet and glistening, making one's heart tighten.

The hand clutching her sleeve had prominent knuckles, turning slightly white from the effort, and his fingertips were trembling slightly.

This appearance perfectly embodied the definition of "too frail to take care of oneself."

Jin Yu took a deep breath, swallowing the "shut your damn mouth" that had been on the tip of her tongue.

Good, very good.

The show has started, has it?

She saw Chen Yinyu's lips quiver, and a trembling, aggrieved voice, thick with a nasal tone, whispered in her ear:

"My lady..."

"There are so many people here, and they... they don't seem to like us."

His voice was as light as a mosquito's hum, yet it carried a magic that could instantly strike the softest part of one's heart.

"Yinyu... has Yinyu embarrassed you?"

"Should we... should we just go back? Please? Yinyu doesn't want you to be pointed at by so many people because of me..."

The voice carried three parts fear, three parts self-reproach, and four parts of crumbling grievance, as if he might burst into tears at any second.

Jin Yu: "..."

However, before she could react, the atmosphere around them had already quietly shifted.

The voices that had been pointing at Jin Yu had faded away without her noticing.

Especially the official's wives who had come to watch the fun with their husbands; their expressions had completely changed.

"Oh my, this little scholar looks far too pitiful..."

"Indeed. Look at how terrified he is, his face is as pale as a sheet. He’s so handsome, it’s no wonder the Jin family’s young lady is fond of him."

"That Xun An is truly something else, refusing to forgive even when he has the upper hand. How could he be so harsh to such a beautiful boy? It’s simply lacking in grace!"

"Exactly! He is, after all, the Jin family’s son-in-law. Calling him a 'house slave' at every turn is truly an insult to his status as a scholar!"

The justice of good looks was on full display at this moment.

Once Chen Yinyu’s striking, beautiful face was clouded with terror and grievance, its lethality increased exponentially.

The hostility originally directed at Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu had, because of his "little rabbit" performance, silently shifted toward the aggressive Xun An.

Xun An clearly sensed the subtle change in the atmosphere, and his expression immediately turned sour.

He had not expected that his full-force strike would feel like hitting cotton, only to bring a wave of criticism upon himself.

And the culprit behind all this—the "kept man" he despised the most—was currently hiding pitifully behind a woman, using his innocent eyes to solicit sympathy from everyone.

Even Master Li, who sat at the head of the table with an air of natural authority, noticed the commotion.

Watching Xun An’s eager-to-please, acerbic demeanor, he frowned ever so slightly.

Though talented, he lacked the capacity to tolerate others; he was arrogant and impetuous—not the behavior of a gentleman.

In his heart, Master Li had silently given Xun An’s character a very low score.

chapters.title: Grateful for the Lady's Kindness, Serving Her for the Rest of My Days
chapters.content:
Xun An’s venom-soaked eyes stared fixedly at Chen Yinyu. Seeing him cowering like a quail behind Jin Yu, the jealousy and contempt in his heart burned like a wildfire.

His meticulously planned humiliation had been neutralized by this pretty boy’s few words of weakness? It had even made him, Xun An, the villain without grace in the eyes of the crowd?

Preposterous!

Xun An’s eyes darted, the hypocritical smile on his face deepening. He paced forward, waving his folding fan, and adopted a tone of pained regret.

"Brother Chen, why be so timid?"

He deliberately slowed his speech. "In the years when we were classmates, you were the student the Master often praised for your spiritual insight. Though your family was poor, you once possessed a spine of steel."

"Now... sigh, never mind. To each their own, one cannot force these things."

"But today at the Orchid Pavilion Gathering, with all the worthies present, it is a grand event for us scholars to exchange knowledge. Since Brother Chen has come, surely your hands are itching to show your skill?"

This sounded like he was offering a way out, but in reality, it was constructing a higher scaffold for an execution.

Xun An looked around and said loudly, "Why not ask Brother Chen to compose a poem on the spot? It would allow us to see whether the Jin family’s vast wealth has raised a canary or a Qilin talent!"

"Let everyone judge just how much a scholar’s integrity is worth!"

As soon as these words were spoken, the crowd erupted.

This was no longer a provocation; it was nakedly roasting Chen Yinyu over a fire!

Ask him to compose a poem?

If he performed well on an occasion like this, it might be fine.

But if he performed poorly, it would be self-inflicted humiliation, cementing his reputation as someone who "bowed for money and lacked true learning."

Moreover, with Xun An, the champion of last year’s poetry gathering, standing there as a standard, who would dare to easily make a fool of themselves?

The surrounding students, eager for a spectacle, immediately began to jeer.

"Brother Xun is right! Give us one! Give us one!"

"Exactly, let us broaden our horizons and see the literary talent of the Jin family’s son-in-law!"

"Don't hide behind a woman! If you're a man, stand out!"

The shouts, growing louder by the second, were like countless hands trying to drag Chen Yinyu out from Jin Yu’s protection, throwing him into the public eye and stripping away the last layer of his dignity as a scholar.

Jin Yu’s face was now as cold as frost.

She pulled Chen Yinyu closer, her phoenix eyes filled with malice as she swept them over the gloating faces.

"My husband is unwell; it is not convenient for him to compose poetry today."

Her voice was cold and clear, carrying an indisputable authority.

"Whoever dares to make another sound, the Jin family will cut off the supply of all silk and fabric to their household!"

"I want to see if your tongues are harder, or if the winter clothes of your female relatives are more important!"

Simple, brutal, and effective.

Once the "money power" was unleashed, the noisy crowd instantly quieted down.

Some students from less affluent families thought of their wives and daughters at home, their faces turning awkward as they sheepishly shut their mouths.

Seeing this, Xun An was green with rage. This Jin Yu was simply vulgar! She couldn't go three sentences without mentioning money; she was covered in the stench of copper, polluting this elegant place!

Just as Jin Yu was about to say more, Chen Yinyu reached out from behind her and gently pressed her hand.

His fingertips were icy and trembling slightly, but the pressure was impossible to ignore.

"My lady..."

Chen Yinyu looked up, his eyes, always misted with moisture, fixed unblinkingly on her.

His expression was complex.

There was fear, unease, and supplication, but beneath those layers of fragility, Jin Yu caught a glimpse of... a calmness that put her at ease.

As if he were saying: Trust me.

Jin Yu’s heart skipped a beat, and the raging fire in her chest inexplicably dimmed by a third under his gaze.

Chen Yinyu let go of her hand, took a deep breath, and as if gathering all the courage of his life, he stepped out from behind her, trembling.

He was already slender, and now, under the wolf-like gazes of the crowd, he appeared even more fragile.

He walked to the desk by the stream, and the attention of the entire room focused on him.

Even Master Li, who had been resting with his eyes closed at the head of the table, slowly opened them, his gaze carrying a hint of scrutiny.

Chen Yinyu picked up the wolf-hair brush.

He dipped it in ink and held his wrist suspended over the snow-white rice paper, but he hesitated to write.

Time ticked by, second by second, and the air around them seemed to freeze.

A cruel smile curled the corners of Xun An’s mouth—can't write it, can you?

Trash!

Just as everyone thought he would embarrass himself and throw down the brush in defeat, the trembling tip finally touched the paper.

The scratching sound of the brush was exceptionally clear in the silent Orchid Pavilion.

Characters appeared on the paper one by one. The handwriting... was actually elegant and powerful, showing great character.

The crowd stretched their necks, and even Jin Yu subconsciously held her breath.

Could it be... was he really going to stun them all and write a masterpiece to slap their faces?

Soon, the four-line poem was finished.

A student standing nearby couldn't help but read it aloud in a low voice.

"Though I lack a belly of silk and brocade..."

"I am fortunate to have hot rice and soup..."

"Grateful for the lady's kindness..."

"I shall serve her in her finery for the rest of my days."

By the last line, the student’s voice was filled with irrepressible laughter.

When the words fell, there was a deathly silence in the Orchid Pavilion.

Everyone stared at the poem, stunned as if struck by lightning.

This is... a poem?

Isn't this just a few lines of plain, colloquial speech?!

One second.

Two seconds.

"Hahahahahaha—!"

It was unclear who started it, but a deafening roar of laughter erupted instantly!

The laughter was filled with undisguised contempt, disdain, and mockery.

"My god! This is called a poem? My three-year-old child speaks more fluently than this!"

"Belly of silk? Hot rice and soup? It’s killing me! Just how hungry is he!"

"Serve her in her finery? Hahaha, he has some self-awareness! He knows he’s just a plaything to serve a woman!"

Xun An laughed the most wildly; he was bent over, tears streaming from his eyes.

He snatched the paper, holding it high as if displaying a trophy.

"Everyone! Everyone, come and admire the masterpiece of our great scholar Chen!"

He pointed at Chen Yinyu, laughing until he was out of breath.

"A dog with a broken spine! I’ve finally seen a living one today!"

"Chen Yinyu, oh Chen Yinyu, not only have you disgraced all us scholars, I think you’ve even disgraced your late mother who raised you through such hardship!"

Amidst the sharp, mocking laughter, Chen Yinyu kept his head down, saying nothing.

Seeing him like a dead dog, Xun An felt even more satisfied.

He wanted to trample this man into the mud so he would never rise again!

"I truly feel it was a waste for your mother to die so early!"

"If she knew in the afterlife that you were kneeling and wagging your tail like a dog for a woman just for a bite to eat, she would probably... be so angry she’d crawl out of her coffin!"

These words were like a poisoned dagger, cruelly thrust into his deepest wound.

The surrounding laughter stopped abruptly; everyone felt that Xun An had gone too far.

One does not attack a person's parents; that is the bottom line of human decency.

"Snap—!"

A crisp, snapping sound rang out abruptly, making everyone’s heart tremble.

They followed the sound.

Chen Yinyu’s wolf-hair brush had snapped cleanly in two; the top half of the handle fell to the ground with a dull thud.

He kept his head down, and no one could see his expression.

His hand, gripping the broken brush, had knuckles turned white from the force, veins bulging, no longer trembling in the slightest.

Jin Yu’s heart tightened; she knew Xun An had touched his only reverse scale.

However, to everyone’s surprise, Chen Yinyu did not fly into a rage, nor did he argue back.

He simply, slowly, and silently crouched down, his gaze falling on the poem draft that Xun An had contemptuously thrown to the ground.

The paper with the clumsy doggerel was being stepped on by a foot, stained with dust and crumpled into a ball.

He reached out and used two fingers to carefully pick the paper up from the dirt.

He gently brushed off the dust and slowly, bit by bit, smoothed out the crumpled paper.

When he looked up again, everyone gasped.

His eye sockets were already so red they looked like they might bleed. A crystal-clear tear hung precariously on his long lashes, trembling and struggling, but stubbornly refusing to fall.

He looked up at Xun An with those bloodshot eyes filled with endless sorrow.

There was no anger, no resentment in that gaze—only a dead, impenetrable grief.

However, only Jin Yu, who was closest to him, caught a fleeting, heart-stopping glint deep within that thick, impenetrable sorrow.

It was not weakness, nor was it resignation; it was a trace of... calculation.

The entire Lanting Pavilion fell deathly silent.

Those who had mocked him earlier now felt their faces burning, as if they had been slapped by an invisible hand.

They suddenly felt that they were just as repulsive as the aggressive Xun An!

chapters.title: A Counterattack, Everyone Does It for Money
chapters.content:
In this deathly silence, a roar suddenly exploded!

"Enough!"

Everyone turned to look at the source of the sound, only to see Master Li, who had been sitting at the head of the table with his eyes closed, seemingly detached from the world, suddenly stand up.

His beard and hair bristled, his old eyes wide with fury as he glared at Xun An and slammed his hand heavily onto the desk in front of him!

"Disgraceful! Simply disgraceful!"

Master Li was trembling with rage, pointing a finger at Xun An’s nose, his voice sharp and severe: "Though the poem is crude, every word and line reveals his gratitude toward his wife. This is the heart of an innocent; what fault is there in that?"

"It is you, Xun An!"

The Master's voice rose sharply, laden with profound disappointment and heartache: "As a scholar, you do not seek to hone your learning, but instead take pleasure in sharp-tongued malice, tearing open others' scars and insulting their late mothers!"

"Have you fed all your study of the sages to the dogs? How is this behavior any different from a street ruffian? I am ashamed to be associated with you!"

These words were spoken with great weight, each one like a blade, scolding Xun An until he was utterly humiliated.

The surrounding students were struck dumb, no longer daring to show even a hint of mockery, and lowered their heads, fearing they might be caught in the Master’s wrath.

Xun An’s complexion shifted instantly from a flush of triumph to a liver-like purple.

He had never imagined that Master Li, who always valued integrity above all else, would publicly shame him for the sake of a few plain words from a live-in son-in-law!

"Master, please calm your anger!"

Xun An was both shocked and furious, but he dared not talk back, so he forced down his humiliation and bowed to defend himself, "Student... student was only frustrated that he did not live up to expectations!"

He put on a look of deep distress, his words earnest: "Brother Chen was once one of us, but now he has stooped to such degradation, bowing for five pecks of rice. Student was expressing pity for him, and more importantly, upholding the integrity and dignity of us scholars!"

These words sounded high-minded and righteous, as if his earlier malicious remarks had all been for the sake of the public good.

Had it been anyone else, they might have been fooled by his glib tongue.

But just then, a faint, trembling voice, as if it had suffered a great injustice, spoke up softly.

"Young Master Xun..."

It was Chen Yinyu.

He had stood up straight at some point, still clutching the crumpled manuscript in his hand.

"The integrity... and dignity you speak of... Yinyu does not understand."

"Yinyu only remembers that when the Jin family sent a matchmaker to your residence to propose, you, Young Master Xun, rejected it to the matchmaker's face."

Xun An’s eyelids twitched violently, and a sense of foreboding rose in his heart.

Chen Yinyu continued in that soft, innocent tone, speaking slowly: "You said you were a pillar of the righteous, a future backbone of the nation; how could you associate with the daughter of a merchant reeking of copper?"

When these words were spoken, many nodded secretly, feeling that Xun An had shown backbone.

Xun An also straightened his back, a look of pride appearing on his face.

However, Chen Yinyu’s next sentence was like a poisoned soft blade, piercing precisely into his heart.

"But you turned around and told the matchmaker... if the Jin family were willing to provide three thousand taels of silver and throw in the newly opened 'Moxiang Study' shop in the west of the city as a dowry, you might be able to... 'struggle' a bit and consider it?"

As soon as these words were out, the whole place was in an uproar!

Everyone’s gaze snapped toward Xun An, filled with shock, suspicion, and contempt.

Three thousand taels of silver?

And a shop?

This wasn't being high-minded; this was clearly holding out for the highest bidder!

"You... you are spouting blood!"

Xun An’s face turned deathly pale in an instant, his finger trembling as he pointed at Chen Yinyu, like a cat whose tail had been stepped on.

Only he and the matchmaker had known about this at the time. Even if Jin Yu had found out later, she could never have told Chen Yinyu, an outsider!

How could he know it so clearly?!

Chen Yinyu seemed frightened by his harsh shout, shrinking back and leaning closer to Jin Yu, his voice sounding even more aggrieved.

"Yinyu dares not lie... my wife told me these things during casual conversation."

He paused, as if trying hard to recall, and continued to twist the knife slowly.

"My wife also said that the month before last, you borrowed fifty taels of silver from the Jin family’s accounts under the pretext of your 'mother being ill,' and you have yet to return it."

"Last month, you hosted your fellow students at the 'Spring Breeze Pavilion,' and you signed it to the Jin family’s account, totaling twelve taels and three qian."

"And..."

"Enough!"

Xun An let out a terrified shriek, completely losing his composure.

He stared fixedly at Chen Yinyu, his eyes full of disbelief.

How could this man know these old, rotten details so clearly, down to the very last fraction?

That woman, Jin Yu, had actually whispered all these things to him in bed?!

Watching Xun An’s ghost-struck expression, a cold, triumphant smile finally flickered deep in Chen Yinyu’s eyes.

He raised his sleeve to gently wipe away a perfectly timed tear from the corner of his eye and sighed softly.

"Yinyu married into the family for five taels of silver to bury my mother and survive. You, Young Master Xun, wanted three thousand taels of silver for a bright future and to live better."

He looked up, his clear eyes staring straight into Xun An’s panicked gaze:

"We are all doing it for money; there is no difference. Why is it that you can take it, but I cannot?"

"Could it be that Young Master Xun’s silver is fragrant and can uphold integrity, while Yinyu’s silver is foul and only fit to break one's spine?"

This series of soul-piercing questions was like a string of loud slaps, striking hard across Xun An’s face!

The way everyone present looked at him changed completely; it was a naked, contemptuous mockery, the way one looks at a clown.

So the so-called "high-minded scholar" was nothing but a hypocrite who cursed the smell of money while trying to bleed the Jin family dry!

"I... I didn't..."

Xun An’s lips trembled as he tried to defend himself, but he found his throat gripped by an invisible hand, unable to utter a single word.

His pride-and-joy eloquence had collapsed in the face of Chen Yinyu’s seemingly weak, yet soul-piercing, questioning!

The entire Lanting Pavilion was so quiet you could hear a pin drop.

Just as Xun An was being roasted over the fire, wishing he could crawl into a hole in the ground, a cold, somewhat lazy female voice broke the suffocating silence.

"So, you were just complaining that the money wasn't enough."

Jin Yu had already stood in front of Chen Yinyu, shielding him completely behind her.

She crossed her arms, her phoenix eyes narrowed, looking at him as if he were a buffoon.

"You should have said so earlier. Why go through such a long-winded circle? Aren't you tired?"

Before the words had even faded, she performed an action that made everyone’s eyes nearly pop out of their heads.

She calmly and unhurriedly pulled a stack of... banknotes from her bosom.

Not one, not two, but a whole stack!

The banknotes were all from the "Four Seas" Bank, the brand-new paper printed with golden embossed patterns, and the top one clearly bore the large characters "One Hundred Taels."

At a rough glance, there was at least a thousand taels!

Under everyone’s shocked gaze, Jin Yu casually flicked the stack of banknotes, and with a "slap," tossed them lightly onto the table in front of Xun An.

The banknotes scattered, covering the table like snowflakes, dizzying to behold.

"Is this enough?"

Jin Yu looked down at Xun An, whose face had turned liver-colored, a cold, mocking sneer curling the corner of her mouth.

"If it's not enough, I'll add more. Take this money as a reward for shutting your mouth. From now on, stay away from my husband. If I ever hear you utter another word from that dog's mouth..."

Her voice turned suddenly cold, carrying a bone-chilling murderous intent: "I will make sure you never speak again for the rest of your life."

chapters.title: Time to Settle the Bill, the Black-Hearted Lotus is Exposed
chapters.content:
Xun An’s face burned with pain, and the surrounding gazes were like poisoned steel needles, pricking him densely all over.

Humiliation.

Unprecedented humiliation!

Money! It was money again!

What else could this woman do besides throw money around!

Xun An’s body trembled violently, his fists clenched so tightly that his nails dug into his palms, nearly drawing blood.

He glared at Jin Yu, his eyes wishing he could tear her apart.

However, Jin Yu only looked back at him from above with contempt, as if looking at an insignificant ant.

Behind her, Chen Yinyu remained in that frightened-deer posture, half his body hidden under Jin Yu’s protection, revealing only a pair of wet eyes, looking timidly at everything.

"Disgraceful... simply disgraceful!"

Master Li shook his head in heartache, his cloudy old eyes filled with disappointment.

He was disappointed not just by Xun An’s greed and hypocrisy, but by the scholar’s integrity being so nakedly trampled by money.

He let out a long sigh and waved his hand wearily at Xun An.

"You... leave."

"From this day forward, the Lanting Poetry Gathering does not welcome you."

This light sentence was like Mount Tai crushing down, completely declaring the death sentence for Xun An in the circle of righteous scholars.

Expelled by the head of the academy himself, his reputation was thoroughly ruined!

"Master! I..." Xun An tried to make a final struggle.

But when he met Master Li’s eyes, filled with disgust and finality, all his excuses were stuck in his throat.

He knew everything was over.

Amidst the contempt and mockery of the entire room, Xun An stumbled away like a stray dog, nearly crawling as he fled Lanting Pavilion.

His retreating figure was wretched, no longer possessing a shred of the high spirits he had arrived with.

The farce ended there.

Master Li watched the direction in which Xun An had disappeared, then turned to look deeply at Chen Yinyu, who was still shielded by Jin Yu, his expression complex.

This boy appeared weak, but his resilience and the ruthlessness of his methods far exceeded that of ordinary people.

One could not tell if this was a blessing or a curse.

...

"Let's go."

Jin Yu couldn't even be bothered to look at the group of stunned students again; she grabbed Chen Yinyu’s hand and turned to leave.

At this moment, she felt as if she had just won a resounding victory, and even her gait carried the high-spirited air of a "victorious rooster."

The crowd automatically parted a path for her, their expressions of awe replacing their previous disdain.

Chen Yinyu followed her obediently, his steps small and delicate, maintaining that same fragile posture of someone who had suffered a great grievance and was in need of protection.

It wasn't until the two of them boarded the luxurious carriage—lined with thick white fox fur and scented with ambergris in the corner—that they were finally cut off from the outside world.

The moment the carriage curtain fell, the triumphant smile on Jin Yu’s face hadn't yet fully faded.

She looked at Chen Yinyu, who was still sitting in the adjacent seat with his head bowed, his shoulders trembling slightly as if he were still lingering in fear. A rare feeling stirred in her heart... guilt?

After all, today’s incident was caused by her; he had taken the hit on her behalf.

Jin Yu cleared her throat, attempting to offer some clumsy comfort in a tone that wasn't too stiff:

"Um... today, I’ve wronged you."

"When we get back, I’ll have the kitchen stew a bowl of blood bird's nest to help you calm your nerves, and... and I’ll add a chicken leg for you?"

She racked her brains, but could only come up with such a simple form of compensation.

However, the tearful, grateful look she expected did not appear. The person beside her stopped trembling.

Chen Yinyu slowly raised his head. Where was there any trace of grievance or fear on that breathtakingly beautiful face?

His eyes were still slightly red, but those clear, limpid pupils were calm, even carrying a hint of scrutiny.

He leisurely took a clean, plain white handkerchief from his sleeve, but instead of wiping the corners of his eyes, he meticulously wiped his own long, slender, fair fingers.

It was as if he had just touched something filthy.

The elegant yet detached movement left Jin Yu stunned. What... what was going on?

Under Jin Yu’s dumbfounded gaze, Chen Yinyu finished wiping his hands, folded the handkerchief neatly, and tucked it back into his sleeve.

Then, he made a gesture that shocked Jin Yu even more.

He reached out his hand toward her.

"My lady."

His voice had returned to its usual coldness, devoid of any softness or trembling.

"The act is over. Shouldn't we settle the payment?"

Jin Yu’s brain "buzzed," short-circuiting for a moment.

Pay... payment?

Seeing her lack of reaction, Chen Yinyu pushed his hand forward a bit more and explained with great patience:

"As we agreed, playing the part of a loving couple in front of others to maintain your reputation costs ten taels of silver per month."

"Today’s event was an emergency, so it should be treated as a rush job, which warrants an extra fee."

He paused and began to calculate item by item.

"First, the base performance fee. I performed beyond expectations, portraying the image of a humiliated yet forbearing husband for love with great vividness. That should be twenty taels."

"Second, the tears. This is an additional service, a high-level technique. Ten taels per drop. I shed three drops just now, so that’s thirty taels."

"Finally," he raised those beautiful eyes to look directly at Jin Yu, "being pointed at and called a 'broken-spined dog' by Xun An caused me severe psychological trauma. For emotional distress, I won't ask for much—let's just say fifty taels, my lady."

"That totals one hundred taels. Cash or on credit? If on credit, there will be a one-percent interest rate."

The carriage fell into a dead silence.

Jin Yu’s eyes widened as she stared at the man before her like he was a monster. The string in her brain labeled "common sense" had completely snapped.

This... was this still that helpless little white flower? This was clearly a black-hearted lotus that had gained sentience!

It took a long while for Jin Yu to recover from her petrified state.

Instead of getting angry, she let out a "pfft" and started laughing.

Then, she burst into uncontrollable laughter.

"Hahahahahaha!"

She laughed until she was swaying back and forth, tears almost coming to her eyes. "You... you really are a... talent!"

Once Jin Yu had laughed enough, she reached into her bosom, pulled out a heavy brocade pouch, and tossed it into Chen Yinyu’s lap with a "thud" without a second thought.

"There’s two hundred taels here. The extra is your bonus!"

She realized she had truly found a treasure.

Love and affection were the most ethereal things, and the easiest to betray.

On the contrary, this relationship based on clear pricing and settled accounts made her feel an unprecedented sense of security and stability.

She loved this kind of person who was clear-headed, perceptive, and focused entirely on "money"!

"I just love this greedy streak of yours!"

Jin Yu crossed her legs and said with great bravado, "Keep up the good work, follow me, and I guarantee you'll have the best food and drink!"

Chen Yinyu weighed the money pouch, tucked it into his sleeve with satisfaction, and gave a slight nod to Jin Yu, his expression perfectly serious.

"Many thanks for your generosity, my lady. Customer satisfaction is my pursuit."

Jin Yu looked at his business-like demeanor, finding it more and more pleasing, and the smile on her lips never faded.

She discovered that she was starting to quite like this "transaction."

The carriage returned to the Jin residence with a light pace.

As soon as they stepped off the carriage, the steward, Wang Quan, hurried over to meet them, his expression grave.

"Eldest Miss, Young Master, you’ve finally returned."

"What’s wrong?" Jin Yu asked.

Wang Quan glanced at Chen Yinyu, hesitated, and finally bowed to report: "Eldest Miss, the wedding attire you ordered for the Young Master has arrived. The embroiderer’s craftsmanship is top-notch."

He changed the subject, lowering his voice: "It’s just... there are some unfavorable rumors outside the estate."

"They say that Xun An was humiliated at the Lanting Poetry Gathering and, unable to swallow his anger, has vowed to bring people to... to block the gate on the day of your wedding. He wants to prevent the Young Master from entering and make the Jin family lose all face!"

Jin Yu’s expression turned cold instantly. This Xun An was truly like a ghost that wouldn't leave!

Just as she was about to lash out, she heard a soft chuckle from Chen Yinyu beside her.

Jin Yu turned to look.

She saw Chen Yinyu leisurely taking the pouch of silver he had just received from his sleeve, placing it in his palm, and tossing it up and down playfully.

The silver made a crisp, pleasant clinking sound inside the brocade pouch.

He raised his eyes to look at the bustling street outside the gate, a flash of icy, piercing coldness crossing his clear, cold pupils.

"Since I’ve taken the money, I’ll make sure this wedding goes through!"

chapters.title: Ten Miles of Red, A Roadblock is Also a Spectacle
chapters.content:
The eighteenth of March, an auspicious day for weddings.

The entire Jiangnan Prefecture was immersed in a dream of extravagant wealth. The Jin family’s "ten miles of red" was literally a ten-mile stretch of red fabric laid out.

High-quality cloud brocade extended from the gates of the Jin residence all the way to the newly purchased mansion of the Chen family—dazzlingly, arrogantly red.

Leading the way were 108 dowry chests, all crafted from golden nanmu wood and wrapped in gleaming brass corner protectors.

The chests were unlocked, left open to nakedly flaunt the dazzling array of treasures inside.

The first chest was filled with neatly stacked gold bars, reflecting a light in the morning sun that was almost blinding.

The second chest contained East Sea pearls the size of pigeon eggs, round and plump, their luster almost spilling out of the chest.

Further back were solid, uncarved pieces of top-grade mutton-fat jade, small mountains of various gemstones, and countless rare antiques, famous calligraphy, and paintings...

The onlookers, who hadn't seen such a display in their entire lives, stretched their necks, their eyes almost popping out of their sockets.

"My heavens, are they marrying off a daughter or the God of Wealth?"

"Did the Jin family empty their entire treasury? How much money is this?"

"I finally understand what 'the smell of money' means. Can you smell it? The air is filled with the sound of silver clinking!"

The discussions, gasps, and intakes of breath merged into a symphony dedicated solely to money.

At the end of this clamor, a magnificent white steed trotted forward at a steady pace.

The man on its back was dressed in cloud brocade as red as a burning fire.

The shade of red was hand-picked by Jin Yu, dyed nine times with the most precious madder root—intense, like congealed blood, or clouds burning across the horizon.

The fabric was embroidered with intricate, swirling cloud patterns in gold thread, and with his every movement, it seemed as if flowing light danced across his sleeves.

His dark hair was tied high with a white jade hairpin, revealing a face that could topple kingdoms.

It was none other than Chen Yinyu.

Today, he had shed his usual coldness and detachment; his snow-white, handsome face, set against the red attire, revealed a hint of bewitching beauty.

His brows and eyes were as picturesque as ever, only the corners of his eyes were stained with a faint crimson from the festive atmosphere, like a peach blossom petal fallen in the snow.

His thin lips were slightly pursed, and though he wore no expression, it made people feel as if he were harboring deep affection in his eyes.

"My god... is this the Jin family’s new son-in-law?"

"He’s even better-looking than the people in paintings..."

The young women on the roadside were mesmerized, their floral handkerchiefs and fresh flowers instinctively thrown toward him.

Chen Yinyu didn't dodge, letting the fragrant items land on him and then be gently shaken off by the horse’s movement.

His gaze remained fixed straight ahead, toward that golden, magnificent direction.

[This outfit is really expensive. The treasure of the Cloud Brocade Workshop, three hundred taels of silver. I can't afford to pay for it if I ruin it; I must wear it carefully.]

Chen Yinyu calculated with no ripples in his heart.

However, this grand wedding procession came to an abrupt halt when it reached the gates of the Jin residence.

The festive sound of the suona horns stopped abruptly, and the atmosphere turned eerie.
