The gate of the Jin residence, wide enough for eight horses to ride abreast, was blocked by several broken tables and rotten chairs.

Xun An sat in a grand armchair in the center, wearing a washed-out Confucian robe that formed a stark, jarring contrast to the wealth and red of the street.

He sat with his legs spread wide, looking like a "chief examiner," with a dozen equally poor, failed scholars behind him, along with some street thugs who clearly had nothing better to do.

This group struck the pose of "examiners," wearing malicious sneers on their faces, blocking the path of the entire wedding procession.

When the steward, Wang Quan, saw this, his heart skipped a beat.

He hurried forward, his face plastered with a smile, pulling a large handful of wedding candies and red envelopes from his robes to stuff into Xun An’s hands.

"Oh, isn't this Young Master Xun! Come to have a cup of wedding wine on this joyous day and share in the luck!"

"Slap!"

Xun An raised his hand and knocked everything in Wang Quan’s hands to the ground. Copper coins and candies rolled everywhere, making a crisp yet jarring sound.

Wang Quan’s smile froze on his face.

Xun An suddenly stood up, his voice not too loud, yet clear enough for everyone around to hear, as he shouted:

"The Jin family chooses a son-in-law without regard for character, looking only at his looks—truly a bizarre tale in our Jiangnan Prefecture!"

"We scholars value integrity above all else! Today, I, Xun An, represent the literati of Jiangnan to test this bridegroom and see if he is even qualified to enter the Jin family’s gates!"

He stood on the moral high ground, exploiting the loophole in the local wedding custom of "blocking the door" to turn a hooligan’s provocation into a refined affair among scholars.

Inside the bridal sedan, Jin Yu heard the commotion outside, her nails digging into her palms in anger.

This Xun An is truly like a rock in a latrine—stinking and hard!

She wanted to "whoosh" open the curtain and step out to pelt this ungrateful wretch with silver banknotes.

However, a hand covered in wrinkles held hers down firmly.

"Miss, you mustn't!"

The matchmaker was sweating profusely, whispering urgently, "According to the rules, a bride’s feet must not touch the ground when leaving the house; it’s bad luck!"

Jin Yu ground her teeth in frustration, yet she was bound by these damned rules, forced to swallow her rage while listening to Xun An continue his clamor outside.

"Chen Yinyu!"

Xun An’s gaze locked onto Chen Yinyu, who was on horseback, like a venomous snake, his voice filled with gleeful mockery.

"We were classmates, after all. If you cannot complete this couplet to open the door..."

He pointed to a small side door used by servants, a door only high enough for a dog to crawl through.

"...then you can crawl through that dog hole! After all, a live-in son-in-law isn't worthy of walking through this vermilion main gate!"

Insult!

This was a naked, public insult in front of the entire city!

Everyone’s eyes were fixed on Chen Yinyu—some with sympathy, some with schadenfreude, but most just there to watch the spectacle.

Right under the spotlight of the crowd, Chen Yinyu moved.

He dismounted with elegant grace, his expensive red robes not showing a single wrinkle.

He didn't even look at Xun An first; instead, he raised his hand slightly toward the Jin family guards behind him, signaling them to remain calm.

His effortless demeanor made it seem as if he were the master in control of the situation, not a groom being harassed.

Only then did he slowly and methodically straighten his wide sleeves and walk step by step toward Xun An.

He was half a head taller than Xun An, looking down at him with a faint smile on his face.

That smile was cold and detached, yet carried an inexplicable sense of pressure.

"Brother Xun wishes to test my literary talent?"

Chen Yinyu tilted his head slightly, his voice clear and resonant, like jade striking jade.

"Coincidentally, my wife gave me a handy piece of stationery the day before yesterday. Today is a perfect time to try it out."

chapters.title: An Abacus Against Poetry, the Scholars’ Faces Slapped Swollen
chapters.content:
Stationery?

As soon as these words were spoken, the group of scholars behind Xun An burst into laughter, as if they had heard the greatest joke in the world.

"Stationery? Don't tell me he’s going to pull out some rare manuscript from a previous dynasty or a priceless inkstone to pretend he’s cultured?"

"As a live-in son-in-law climbing the social ladder, is he even worthy of the word 'stationery'?"

The mockery on Xun An’s face deepened. He crossed his arms, waiting to watch the show.

He wanted to see what kind of shocking "stationery" this soft-boned man who relied on his looks could pull out from those priceless red robes.

The surrounding townspeople also held their breath, craning their necks in curiosity.

Under the gaze of the crowd, Chen Yinyu’s hand finally emerged slowly from his wide cloud-brocade sleeve.

However, what he held was neither brush, ink, paper, nor inkstone, nor any rare jade artifact.

It was an abacus.

A small, exquisite abacus that was bright enough to dazzle the eyes.

The frame of the abacus was crafted from pure gold, flowing with a breathtaking, opulent luster in the sunlight.

The beads were not made of wood or common stone, but carved from top-quality Hetian white jade—round, translucent, and warm.

Gold and jade combined; the two diametrically opposed qualities of vulgarity and elegance were perfectly fused in this small abacus, creating an arrogant, unreasonable air of nobility.

This was one of the wedding gifts Jin Yu had given him a few days ago, with the excuse: "If a worker wants to do his job well, he must first sharpen his tools. You’ll be managing my private treasury from now on; how can you do that without a good abacus?"

*[She’s right; this abacus is indeed much smoother to use than the boxwood ones in the manor.]*

A pragmatic thought flashed through Chen Yinyu’s mind.

But as soon as this "stationery" appeared, the scene went deathly silent, followed by an eruption of thunderous, mocking laughter.

"Hahahaha! An abacus! He actually brought out an abacus!"

"Am I seeing this right? He calls this stationery? Is he trying to challenge us to a math contest?"

"The stench of copper! Reeking of copper! Decency is swept away! It is absolutely disgraceful!"

The scholars laughed until they were doubled over, tears streaming down their faces.

They thought Chen Yinyu had reached the end of his rope and had been driven insane.

Xun An laughed so hard he couldn't straighten up. He pointed at Chen Yinyu and shouted to the surrounding crowd: "Everyone, look! This is the husband chosen by the eldest daughter of the Jin family! His mind is filled with nothing but gold and silver calculations—how vulgar! He’s asked to complete a couplet, and he pulls out an abacus. This is a profound humiliation to our Jiangnan literati!"

A sharp-featured scholar behind him caught the hint, cleared his throat, and recited in a shrill voice:

"Regardless, you must still complete this couplet today. We’ll lower the requirements—here is the first line. If you can match the intent of the second line, we’ll let you pass!"

He shook his head, his face filled with undisguised malice, and recited loudly:

"A pair of jade arms pillowing a thousand men, half a pair of vermilion lips tasted by ten thousand guests!"

As soon as this was said, those who understood the implications had their expressions change instantly.

This was no couplet; it was clearly taken from lewd poetry used to describe courtesans in brothels!

Using it here was malicious to the core!

This was not just insulting Chen Yinyu; it was a veiled jab at the Jin family business, implying they were nothing more than "servants" earning dirty money!

Vicious!

Base!

Even the onlookers sensed something was wrong and frowned.

Wang Quan was trembling with rage, his fists clenched, ready to rush forward and argue.

Inside the sedan, Jin Yu’s breath hitched, a chill running from the soles of her feet to the top of her head.

She could endure being called vulgar or money-grubbing, but she would never tolerate anyone slandering the century-old reputation of the Jin family!

Xun An! You have a lot of nerve!

Just as the atmosphere froze to the freezing point and everyone expected Chen Yinyu to fly into a rage or be shamed into silence, he simply listened quietly, his handsome face devoid of any extra expression.

He merely lifted the gold and jade abacus, his fair, slender fingers resting on the jade beads.

Then, amidst the suspicious and uncertain gazes of everyone, he began to move the beads.

"Click-clack—"

"Click-clack, click-clack—"

The crisp sound of jade beads colliding was exceptionally clear in the sudden silence, like a sudden downpour of rain tapping on everyone’s hearts.

His fingers moved so fast they were almost a blur. Those hands that usually held a brush to write were now flying across the abacus, possessing a dazzling, hypnotic beauty.

Everyone was stunned. What... what was he doing?

Xun An’s smile froze on his face, and an ominous premonition arose.

Chen Yinyu, while rapidly moving the beads, spoke in a calm, cold, and measured tone.

His voice was not loud, but every word clearly reached everyone’s ears.

"A pair of jade arms pillowing a thousand men... based on the average price of a premium room at the Yuelai Inn in Jinling Prefecture, at five hundred wen per night, a thousand men would be five hundred guan."

"Half a pair of vermilion lips tasted by ten thousand guests... this line should describe the business of a tavern or teahouse. Based on the minimum tea fee at the Jiangnan Spring Teahouse, at ten wen per guest, ten thousand guests would be one hundred guan."

"Click!"

With the final crisp sound, his fingers stopped.

The whole world seemed to go quiet, leaving only his clear, resonant voice.

Chen Yinyu raised his eyelids, his gaze falling calmly on the sharp-featured scholar who had recited the couplet, and slowly announced a figure.

"The first line 'a thousand men' and the second line 'ten thousand guests'—added together, the total turnover is six hundred guan."

He paused, a faint curve appearing at the corner of his mouth.

"Although this couplet is flowery in language, its intent is far too meager; it doesn't even amount to half a day’s revenue from the businesses under my wife’s name."

"My good sir," he turned to Xun An, his eyes as cold as ice, "the 'thousand men and ten thousand guests' in your first line sound grand, but the total turnover doesn't even add up to the spare change of any random Jin family shop."

"This perspective..."

Chen Yinyu shook his head slightly, letting out a sigh of pity.

"...is too small."

Perspective... too small?

Xun An and the group of scholars were struck as if by lightning, their minds buzzing into a blank void.

The couplet they were so proud of, filled with sharp wit and humiliation, had actually... actually been calculated by the other party using the most vulgar abacus into... a business transaction?

And a business transaction with a "very small perspective" at that?

This was even more brutal than slapping them in the face in public!

This was a dimensionality strike!

He had taken the literary elegance they prided themselves on, pinned it to the ground, and ground it into the dirt with the measure of money!

Before they could recover from this massive shock, Chen Yinyu’s voice rang out again, this time addressed to the townspeople.

"You have all studied the words of sages for half a lifetime, full of talk about benevolence and morality, yet you cannot even calculate the cost of daily necessities."

"You look down on merchants, yet you do not know that the livelihood, food, clothing, and shelter of everyone in this city are tied to the hands of merchants."

His voice suddenly rose, carrying an unprecedented sharpness and pride.

"The sage said: The people are the most important, the state comes next, and the ruler is the least."

"To allow the people to be well-fed and clothed—that is the true Great Way!"

"Reading dead books and composing sour poetry—what use is that to the country or the people?"

His gaze was like a sword, piercing straight at Xun An.

"So, it is not that I, Chen Yinyu, cannot provide a matching couplet, but rather that your opening line is simply not worthy of having my wife’s golden abacus clicked even once!"

"Because—"

He held the gleaming golden abacus high. Under the sunlight, the light reflected from its gold frame and white jade beads was so piercing that all the scholars could barely keep their eyes open.

"The most useless thing of all is the scholar! Not worth a single tael of my wife's gold!"

As soon as these words were spoken, the entire scene fell silent.

A few moments later, someone among the onlookers finally reacted, slapping their thigh and roaring with laughter.

"Good!"

"Well said!"

This cry of "Good" was like a spark, instantly igniting the entire crowd!

"The son-in-law is right! Being able to earn money is the only truth that matters!"

"Exactly! We commoners don't understand your fancy literary jargon; we just know that because the Jin family opened their shops, we have work to do and food to eat!"

"These poor scholars only know how to wag their tongues. They’re nearly starving themselves, yet they look down on Miss Jin!"

"The Jin son-in-law is standing up for us commoners! That was damn satisfying to hear!"

The tide of public opinion reversed completely in an instant!

Those who had originally been watching for the sake of entertainment were now all ignited by Chen Yinyu’s "down-to-earth" remarks.

They might not understand obscure literary allusions, but they understood money, they understood the necessities of life, and they understood who was truly helping them live a better life!

For a time, cheers, applause, and shouts of approval rang out, almost loud enough to blow the roof off the Jin mansion.

Xun An and the scholars behind him were struck pale by this tsunami of sound, swaying as if they might collapse.

They were completely bewildered. How could this happen?

Their meticulously prepared literary duel, the dignity of the scholars they relied upon for survival—how could it all be smashed to pieces by an abacus?

Chen Yinyu hadn't followed their rules at all!

He had dragged them into the field he was most familiar with—a field they despised and knew nothing about—and then crushed them completely in a way they couldn't even comprehend!

Xun An stared fixedly at Chen Yinyu. The blood had drained from his handsome face, his lips trembling, unable to utter a single word.

He had lost again. Lost utterly, lost completely, lost without a shred of dignity left.

chapters.title: Eating Soft Rice with Hard Pride, I Kneel to My Providers
chapters.content:
But Xun An was not reconciled!

He still had one last straw to grasp, a shackle that no man of this era could break free from—a man's dignity!

"Chen Yinyu!"

Xun An roared with all his might, his voice so shrill it seemed to pierce the eardrums.

"How dare you stand there and spout such heretical nonsense!"

He pointed a trembling finger directly at the tip of Chen Yinyu’s nose, his face twisted with jealousy and looking particularly hideous.

"You were raised reading the books of sages, yet now you are content to marry into a merchant family and bow to a woman as your master!"

He seemed to have grasped his final hope. "At the wedding ceremony, you will have to kneel to your bride! A man’s knees hold gold; one kneels only to heaven, earth, and parents, yet you are going to kneel to a woman!"

"Where is your dignity?! Where is the backbone of a scholar?!"

This question was like a thunderclap, instantly suppressing the roaring crowd.

The entire scene fell into a deathly silence.

Yes, this question was sharper and more piercing than any couplet before it.

It was a pain that any man, especially a scholar, found impossible to avoid and most ashamed to mention.

Marrying into a wife's family was already a disgraceful act, and kneeling to a wife was to trample a man's face into the dirt.

All eyes focused on Chen Yinyu once again.

This time, it wasn't the mockery of watching a show, but a gaze filled with a trace of pity and scrutiny.

They wanted to see how this sharp-tongued young man would defend such a "great humiliation."

They waited to see him overcome with shame, waited to see him fly into a rage.

However, Chen Yinyu’s reaction once again exceeded everyone’s expectations.

Facing Xun An’s predatory gaze and deafening accusations, he simply stood there.

He didn't even raise an eyelid.

He lowered his gaze slightly, as if observing the cloud-brocade patterns on his magnificent red robe, or perhaps as if brushing off non-existent dust.

That composure and calm formed a stark, glaring contrast to Xun An’s hysteria.

"Dignity?"

After a long while, Chen Yinyu spoke slowly. He raised those shimmering peach-blossom eyes, his gaze landing calmly on Xun An, as if looking at a clown.

"Brother Xun, hearing the word 'dignity' from your mouth is truly ironic."

"You borrowed money from classmates to buy books and haven't repaid it yet. Did you think of dignity then?"

"To seek recommendations from famous masters, you bowed and scraped before the powerful, wagging your tail for pity. Did you think of dignity then?"

"You coveted the Jin family's wealth, and when your marriage proposal was rejected, you grew resentful and began slandering a woman here. Is this your dignity?"

With every word Chen Yinyu spoke, Xun An’s face turned a shade paler.

These words were like sharp daggers, precisely slicing open the skin he had disguised with "nobility," exposing all the filth, corruption, and ugliness within to the broad daylight!

Xun An opened his mouth, but couldn't say a word, leaving only the sound of rapid, ragged breathing.

But Chen Yinyu had no intention of letting him off.

He took a step forward, his clear, resonant voice carrying across the entire long street.

"I, Chen Yinyu, come from a poor background. I have no other skills, save for a face that is decent to look at and a talent for study that has not gone to waste."

"The eldest daughter of the Jin family saw fit to choose me, willing to offer a thousand gold pieces to take me as her husband, providing me with fine clothes and food, and promising me a stable life."

He met everyone's gaze openly, a faint smile even curling the corners of his mouth. There was no shame in that smile; instead, it carried a kind of righteous pride.

"I kneel to my providers, to the benefactor who has promised me a worry-free future, and to the woman I have married in a proper, public ceremony."

"And you, Xun An? You kneel to the powerful families that can help you rise to the top in one step, to the dirty steps you use to climb over others!"

His voice rose sharply, every word landing like heavy gold and stone, ringing with power!

"I eat 'soft rice' openly and honestly. I don't steal, I don't rob, I don't cheat, and I don't swindle!"

"You eat 'soft rice' but still insist on setting up a memorial archway to your own nobility. You want the Jin family's money, and you want the face of a scholar! You want it all—aren't you tired?"

"Xun An, tell me," he tilted his head slightly, his eyes filled with a trace of pure curiosity and innocent cruelty, "between the two of us, who is truly the one without dignity?"

"BOOM—!"

The crowd exploded!

If using an abacus to counter a couplet was a victory through surprise, then this "soft rice manifesto" was truly shocking!

To speak of "eating soft rice" so refreshingly, so righteously, and so... convincingly!

Inside the bridal sedan, Jin Yu gripped the golden apple in her hand tightly, her knuckles turning white from the force.

Through the gap in the sedan curtain, she could clearly see the man’s straight, upright back.

He was clearly lean and slender, yet at this moment, he stood like a mountain, shielding her from all the wind, rain, and filthy words.

She had expected him to be angry, to defend himself, to use obscure allusions to protect his fragile self-esteem.

She never expected him to simply flip the table, wearing the humiliating label of "matrilocal son-in-law" with the arrogance of a king being crowned.

This man... his tongue is truly poisonous.

But... I really like it.

The corners of Jin Yu’s mouth lifted uncontrollably, the smile in her eyes nearly overflowing.

The commoners outside didn't have so many twists and turns in their thoughts; they only felt satisfied!

"Well said! Miss Jin is so rich, what’s wrong with giving someone a meal of soft rice? I’d like to eat it too!" A butcher selling pork waved his greasy fist, shouting until he was hoarse.

"Exactly! Brother Xun, stop being so sour. You’re just jealous that he looks better than you and managed to marry Miss Jin!"

"You have no talent yourself and can't stand to see others doing well. Bah! What kind of scholar are you!"

The mocking jeers and cheers were like red-hot branding irons, searing into Xun An’s nerves.

He was finished. He was completely finished.

After this, Xun An would become the laughingstock of the entire Jiangnan Prefecture. Before, it was only embarrassing among the literati, but this time it was different—there were so many commoners here.

The talent he was so proud of, the dignity he guarded so fiercely, had been trampled into worthlessness by Chen Yinyu in the most humiliating way possible today.

Boundless hatred and despair instantly swallowed all his reason. In those bloodshot eyes, only a frantic desire for destruction remained.

If the literary way didn't work, then he would use force!

If dignity was gone, then no one should have any face left!

"AH—!"

Xun An let out a roar, pointing hideously at the wedding procession, using his last bit of strength to issue the command.

"Smash it!"

"Smash the bridal sedan! This wedding... no one is going to finish it!"

Before the words had even faded, several thugs in the crowd who had been silent until now changed their expressions.

Fierce light shone in their eyes; they were the backup plan Xun An had paid for, ready to act if the literary duel failed!

The burly man in the lead gave a sinister laugh, violently pushing aside the commoners in front of him. Like a beast released from a cage, he and his gang of thugs overturned the tables and chairs blocking the way, rushing toward the bright red, eye-catching bridal sedan like a foul, muddy torrent!

The onlookers screamed in terror and scrambled backward. The scene instantly spiraled out of control!

chapters.title: Playing the Victim to Protect the Wife, This Is a Murder
chapters.content:
Although the Jin family servants had some martial arts training, they were caught off guard by this group of desperate thugs and their formation fell into chaos.

Moreover, no one had expected such an event today. After all, this was the Jin family; to dare to cause such a scene was practically a death wish.

In the chaos, the burly man drew closer and closer to the sedan.

Ten steps.

Five steps.

Three steps!

A hideous grin hung on his face, and his fan-sized hand was already raised high, about to rip open the sedan curtain embroidered with mandarin ducks!

Behind that curtain was the Jin family’s sole heir, the richest person in all of Jiangnan Prefecture!

If she were truly humiliated in public by such filthy scum, the Jin family’s reputation and Jin Yu’s honor would be utterly destroyed!

In the blink of an eye, no one noticed that Chen Yinyu, who had always been considered a weak scholar, moved.

No, he didn't move.

He simply let out a perfectly timed exclamation at the very moment the burly man was about to touch the bridal sedan curtain.

For the first time, that peerlessly handsome face wore a look of utter panic, as if he had been terrified out of his wits by the violence before him.

His body tilted, as if he had completely lost his balance, and he plummeted straight down from his tall horse like a kite with a broken string!

"Son-in-law!"

Wang Quan, the butler of the Jin manor, felt his heart skip a beat.

Yet, this seemingly wretched fall contained a precision and ruthlessness that no one else could perceive.

Chen Yinyu’s body traced an arc in the air. When he landed, he made no dull thud; instead, using the momentum of his roll, he slid silently to the front of the bridal sedan.

He landed exactly in the path the burly man was bound to take.

The man hadn't even spared a glance for this scholar, and with a sinister grin, he prepared to step right over him.

But the very moment he lifted his foot, Chen Yinyu, who appeared to be sprawled limply on the ground, flicked his sleeve lightly.

His toe tapped the ground with lightning speed, striking the man’s knee—the exact, vulnerable pressure point!

It was a highly fragile joint of the human body!

"Agh!"

The burly man felt a piercing numbness in his knee. His leg gave way, and his massive frame uncontrollably collapsed forward onto his knees.

At the very moment he fell, Chen Yinyu lunged forward, seemingly in a panic to dodge, but in reality, he struck his elbow hard and precisely just below the man’s left ribcage!

*Crack—*

A faint, crisp sound was perfectly masked by the surrounding screams.

Everything happened with extreme speed. To everyone else, all they saw was:

The beautiful, weak-as-a-kitten son-in-law falling in a panic from his horse, colliding with the rushing thug, and then collapsing weakly before the bridal sedan door.

That was all.

Yet, what happened in the next second made everyone present drop their jaws.

Chen Yinyu was seen clutching his chest, collapsing delicately at the sedan entrance. His already fair face drained of all color in an instant, turning as pale as paper.

His eyes were tightly shut, his long eyelashes trembling slightly, and beads of cold sweat rolled down his temples.

He opened his mouth, as if using every ounce of his remaining strength, and let out a thin, yet piercing, shriek—

"Murder! Help!"

"In broad daylight! An assassination in the middle of the street!"

"Save me! Someone is trying to murder the son-in-law of the richest man! They're trying to kill for money!"

The cry was heart-wrenching, enough to make the listener grieve and the onlooker weep.

That indignation, that despair—it was more vivid and moving than the lead actor of the city’s most famous theater troupe.

The entire scene fell into a deathly silence. Everyone was stunned by this sudden turn of events.

One moment it was just a wedding disturbance, a verbal spat between scholars; how did it turn into a shocking case of street assassination and attempted murder for gain in the next?!

With that shout, the nature of the incident had completely changed!

What kind of family was the Jin family? They were the top taxpayers in Jiangnan Prefecture!

Attempting to murder the family of a major taxpayer—if this charge stuck, it would alarm the imperial court and result in the execution of one's entire clan!

The few constables who had been watching the show with their arms crossed turned deathly pale.

They had all, to some extent, taken "tributes" from the Jin family; they could no longer play deaf and dumb.

The head constable drew his saber and roared, "Audacious scoundrel! How dare you commit violence and injury in broad daylight! Seize him!"

"Protect the Jin family's son-in-law!"

The constables charged forward like wolves and tigers.

Those thugs and ruffians were nothing but a rabble; they could bully commoners, but how could they be a match for government officials?

In a few swift moves, they were all pinned to the ground, wailing and crying for their parents.

Two constables grabbed the terrified Xun An and held him fast.

Xun An’s mind was a blank slate. He couldn't understand how things had devolved to this point.

He had only wanted to wreck the wedding, humiliate Jin Yu, and make Chen Yinyu lose face!

How did it become an assassination?

"It wasn't me! I didn't!"

Xun An finally snapped back to reality, struggling desperately and screaming at the top of his lungs, "It was him! He fell on his own! He’s faking it!"

But who would believe him?

What the crowd saw was Chen Yinyu’s bloodless face, his body twitching as he clutched his chest, and his breathing so weak it seemed he might stop at any moment.

Then they looked at Xun An’s twisted, ferocious face born of jealousy, and his accomplices groaning on the ground.

The truth was already self-evident in everyone’s minds.

"Take them away! Bring them all to the yamen for strict interrogation!" The head constable waved his hand, giving Xun An no chance to argue.

In the chaotic crowd, the bright red bridal sedan remained quietly in place, like an isolated island in a storm.

Inside the sedan, Jin Yu slowly lowered the golden apple in her hand. Through the tiny gap in the curtain, she had taken in everything that happened outside.

Chen Yinyu lay there, his frame slender, his snow-white inner robes stained with dust, his dark hair spread messily on the ground, looking as fragile as a piece of porcelain about to shatter.

He acted so convincingly.

Jin Yu’s mind was perfectly clear.

From the angle of his fall from the horse, to the trajectory of his slide, to that scream—every detail was calculated.

This man was not only sharp-tongued, but his heart had more holes than a sieve.

However...

Jin Yu’s gaze fell on the way he had positioned himself to guard the sedan entrance.

He could have easily dodged. With his seemingly clumsy but actually precise movements, he could have avoided the reckless thug without a scratch.

But he didn't.

He chose to fall before her sedan in the most "weak," yet most effective way possible.

He used his own body to build a barrier for her—one that looked fragile, yet was impenetrable.

He blocked all the chaos, danger, and malice outside.

At this moment, Jin Yu’s heart, which was accustomed to measuring everything in terms of money and profit, felt as if it had been gently, yet firmly, struck by something.

It felt a bit sour, a bit numb, and also... a bit warm.

She watched the man still "struggling for his life" on the ground, even his breathing filled with theatricality, and the corners of her mouth curled up uncontrollably.

chapters.title: The Wedding Ceremony, Money Well Spent
chapters.content:
As Xun An and his band of cronies were dragged away in a wretched state.

The long street, which had been tense and chaotic just moments ago, was left with nothing but a mess and guests staring at each other in bewilderment.

Everyone’s eyes were fixed on the man lying before the bridal sedan, looking like a white lotus flower ravaged by wind and rain.

Wang Quan, the Jin manor butler, scrambled over, his voice choked with sobs: "Son-in-law! Son-in-law, hold on! Quick! Go fetch the best doctor in the city!"

However, before his hand could touch the hem of Chen Yinyu’s robe, he saw the "dying" man’s long eyelashes flutter, and he slowly opened his eyes.

There was not a trace of pain in those clear peach-blossom eyes; instead, they held a perfectly measured confusion, as if he had just awakened from a nightmare.

"Hmm?" Chen Yinyu blinked weakly, braced himself against the ground, and stood up with fluid grace.

He first brushed the dust off his robes and smoothed his slightly disheveled hair. The entire process was seamless and elegant, as if the person twitching on the ground just now wasn't him.

Wang Quan’s hand froze in mid-air, his mouth hanging open wide enough to fit an egg.

Chen Yinyu turned his head and flashed a bright, sunny, and harmless smile at the stunned Wang Quan and the guests.

That smile was like a spring breeze, melting the ice and snow, instantly dispelling all the gloom from just moments ago.

He cleared his throat and announced in a clear voice: "The auspicious hour has not passed. Continue the music, continue the dance!"

"..."

The entire scene fell into a bizarre silence once more.

This... he’s fine now?

Was that look of someone about to depart this world just a collective hallucination?

Only Jin Yu, inside the bridal sedan, saw the faint smile at the corner of her lips deepen.

Good heavens, his speed at changing faces was faster than her accountant using an abacus.

He was truly a man worth the heavy price she paid; his professional ability was top-notch.

The wedding procession set off again in an extremely strange atmosphere. The gongs and drums sounded once more, but they carried a certain absurdity of having survived a disaster.

The vermilion, gold-gilded gates of the Jin manor were already wide open. Inside, red carpets were laid out, stretching all the way to the brightly lit, festive main hall.

Jin Wansan sat high in the hall, his round face blooming like a rich, prosperous peony.

He wasn't unaware of the farce on the street, but he didn't care.

The process didn't matter; only the result did.

As long as this marriage was completed, the Jin family’s face would be saved, and his daughter’s reputation would be preserved.

As for whether this son-in-law lived or died... oh wait, as long as he could finish the ceremony, he was a good son-in-law!

"The bride and groom have arrived—!"

Following the master of ceremonies' high-pitched chant, Jin Yu, supported by the matchmaker, stepped into the wedding hall side-by-side with Chen Yinyu, who was dressed in red.

With her phoenix crown and ceremonial robes, her jade ornaments jingled.

Jin Yu walked with steady steps. Even though the red veil covered her face, her aura of authority—the power to decide life and death—remained undiminished.

Chen Yinyu followed half a step behind her, his posture tall and straight. Under the bright candlelight of the hall, his peerlessly handsome face looked even more dazzling than a celestial being.

The guests gasped in admiration, saying that although Chen Yinyu was a live-in son-in-law, his face alone brought glory to the Jin family.

"First bow to heaven and earth—!"

"Second bow to the high hall—!"

The proceedings went smoothly.

Jin Wansan watched his daughter and son-in-law kneeling before him, grinning from ear to ear, nodding repeatedly.

"Husband and wife bow to each other—!"

Finally, it was the last bow.

Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu stood facing each other and slowly bent down.

The heavy phoenix crown and the exquisite headpiece drew close in the air, the red tassels and dark hair intertwining.

Just as their foreheads were about to touch, a cold yet playful voice came, kept extremely low so that only they could hear.

"Good job protecting the carriage just now. Nice acting."

Jin Yu’s voice betrayed no emotion. "A reward of one thousand taels of silver."

Chen Yinyu’s movement, as he was about to bow, paused slightly.

He slowly raised his eyes. Beneath his long lashes, those peach-blossom eyes suddenly shone with an astonishing brilliance, as if countless fragments of gold were flickering and dancing within them.

That was not because of love, but because he heard the sound of money.

His lips curled into a pleased arc, and he replied in a whisper: "I thank you for your grace, my master."

Before the words had even faded, he bowed down abruptly!

"Thud—!"

A loud bang shook the entire wedding hall, making the floor seem to tremble three times over.

Chen Yinyu had knocked his head solidly and unreservedly against the bluestone floor, which was covered only by a thick red felt carpet!

All the guests gasped in unison.

My goodness! What deep affection! What overwhelming excitement!

A typical couple’s bow is merely a light gesture, stopping at the point of courtesy, yet this new son-in-law of the Jin family had performed a full prostration!

That loud thud wasn't just hitting the floor; it was hitting with his heart!

Many of the female guests’ eyes turned red on the spot, moved beyond measure.

Only Jin Yu, beneath her red bridal veil, felt her mouth twitch violently.

This man... for the sake of money, is he willing to throw his head away too?

After Chen Yinyu raised his head, he looked radiant and spoke in a clear, loud voice to Jin Yu—though in reality, he was pledging his loyalty to Jin Wansan, who sat in the seat of honor, and to all the guests in the hall:

"My wife is magnanimous! I, Yinyu, shall never fail you in this life!"

Jin Wansan, watching from above, was delighted and clapped his hands, laughing: "Good! Very good!"

This son-in-law is sensible! He knows the way!

The farcical wedding ceremony finally concluded, and as the night deepened, the noise dissipated.

In the resplendent bridal chamber, the dragon-and-phoenix candles burned quietly, and the air was filled with a faint, sweet fragrance.

Jin Yu sat on the edge of the bed, which was covered in a quilt embroidered with mandarin ducks. She finally took off the pure gold phoenix crown that had nearly broken her neck, letting out a long sigh of relief.

After a whole day of turmoil, even her iron-willed body was starting to wear thin.

As she massaged her aching neck, a pair of distinctively knuckled hands approached, carrying a basin of steaming water.

Chen Yinyu placed the wooden basin steadily at her feet, then crouched down. With practiced ease, he removed her embroidered shoes and gently placed her delicate, beautiful feet into the warm water.

The temperature was just right, instantly dispelling the exhaustion that had permeated her body.

Chen Yinyu rolled up his sleeves, revealing a glimpse of his fair, slender wrists. His long, strong fingers massaged her calves and ankles with just the right amount of pressure.

The sensation was indescribably comfortable.

Jin Yu leaned against the headboard, watching the man before her.

In the candlelight, he kept his eyes lowered, his long eyelashes casting a silhouette, his expression focused and earnest.

The shrewd, calculating "tea-flavored" aura he usually carried seemed to have been steamed away by the warm vapor, leaving only a reassuring, docile quality.

From that desperate "fall" on the street, to that earth-shattering "knock" in the wedding hall, and now this meticulous service...

Jin Yu watched Chen Yinyu’s busy back, and for the first time, she spoke without a tone of command or transaction, as if by some strange impulse.

"Thank you for today."

Chen Yinyu’s massaging motion came to a sudden halt. He stopped and slowly looked up.

A moment later, he suddenly smiled.

That smile was not as bright and flamboyant as it had been during the day; instead, it was like a clear spring under moonlight—clean and gentle.

"I take people's money, I resolve their troubles," he said softly. "It is only right."

He spoke those cold, transactional terms with a tone of natural, doting care.

Jin Yu’s heart was struck again by that strange feeling.

It didn't hurt, but it felt numb, a sensation that spread through every fiber of her being.

The atmosphere in the bridal chamber became somewhat subtle at that moment.

The candlelight flickered, the faint fragrance drifted, and a romantic sentiment quietly sprouted in the air.

Just as Jin Yu felt her cheeks growing warm and wanted to say something to break the silence—

"Knock, knock, knock!"

A series of urgent knocks on the door acted like a basin of cold water, instantly extinguishing all the romantic ambiance.

From outside the door came Wang Quan’s anxious voice, suppressing his anger:

"Eldest Miss! It’s bad!"

"The Second Master is here. I heard there’s an urgent wedding account with a major discrepancy, and he wants you to go over it with him tomorrow."

Jin Yu’s expression turned cold in an instant. The last trace of warmth in her eyes vanished, replaced by the sharpness and coldness typical of a merchant.

On her wedding night, her second uncle, Jin Wansi, had come knocking with a so-called "urgent account."

This wasn't about checking accounts; this was clearly an attempt to intimidate her!

Chen Yinyu had already stood up and picked up a soft towel to meticulously dry the water droplets from Jin Yu’s feet.

Only after doing this did he look up at the closed door.

"The Second Uncle is in such a hurry?"

"It seems this account isn't a small problem, but a very big one."

chapters.title: The Tea-Serving Conflict, the Second Uncle’s Intimidation
chapters.content:
On her wedding night, Jin Yu ultimately did not let Wang Quan let her second uncle, Jin Wansi, inside.

"Tell him to get lost."

Those were her exact words through the door—crisp and decisive, without a hint of hesitation.

"Tell him, according to the rules of the Jin family, the first three days of marriage are for avoiding bad luck, and no business should be conducted. Even if the sky were falling, he can wait until after the tea-serving ceremony to talk to me!"

Wang Quan, having received his orders, straightened his back instantly. He mimicked her words perfectly, even capturing the full force of the word "lost," successfully causing Jin Wansi to puff out his cheeks in rage and storm off.

Inside the room, the hot water that was meant for washing had long since gone cold.

Chen Yinyu silently took the basin away and replaced it with a pot of warmed calming tea.

He didn't say anything more, as if the farce outside had nothing to do with him.

After serving his "patron," he sat under the lamp and quietly began to read a book.

The flickering candlelight cast his slender figure onto the wall, creating an illusion of peaceful, timeless serenity.

Jin Yu leaned against the headboard, watching him, and had to admit that this man possessed a strange ability.

He could instantly make the most tense atmosphere turn peaceful.

It was as if, as long as he was there, the greatest trouble was nothing more than a breeze outside the window, unable to stir up even the slightest ripple.

The night passed in silence.

...

The next morning, as the sky began to brighten, the main hall of the Jin residence no longer held the festive air of the day before.

Although the red silk and "double happiness" characters were still hanging, the atmosphere was as cold as the dead of winter.

On a huanghuali wood armchair sat Jin Wansi in the center, with a group of elders from the Jin family’s collateral branches standing behind him.

Everyone wore a solemn expression, their eyes critical, looking like a group of underworld judges waiting to pass sentence on a prisoner.

The air was thick with the tension of a storm about to break.

Jin Yu had changed out of her elaborate wedding dress into a pomegranate-red brocade gown with gold-thread embroidery. Her long hair was loosely pinned up, adorned only with a gold-and-kingfisher-feather hairpin. As she walked, she shimmered with a compelling, noble air.

Her expression was indifferent, as if she hadn't noticed the "trial" awaiting her.

Chen Yinyu followed at her side, half a step behind.

He wore a bamboo-green robe today, which made his skin look as white as snow and his features as delicate as a painting.

He kept his eyes slightly lowered, hiding all his sharp edges, as docile as a harmless rabbit.

The two walked into the main hall side-by-side, where the servants had already brought out hot tea.

"Father, Second Uncle, elders," Jin Yu nodded slightly, as a greeting.

Jin Wansi sat in the seat of honor, looking at his daughter and then at the impossibly handsome son-in-law beside her. He wore an awkward smile, wanting to smooth things over but not knowing where to start.

Still, the formalities had to be observed.

Jin Yu served tea to Jin Wansi first, who accepted it happily and even gave her a thick red envelope.

Then it was Chen Yinyu’s turn.

He held the celadon teacup respectfully, walked to Jin Wansi, bent down, and offered it with both hands.

"Second Uncle, please have some tea."

His voice was clear and gentle, his posture humble to the extreme.

However, Jin Wansi didn't even bother to lift his eyelids. He leisurely picked up his own teacup, gently blew the foam away, and simply refused to reach out to take the cup from Chen Yinyu’s hands.

Time ticked by, second by second.

Chen Yinyu remained holding the teacup, frozen in mid-air.

His arm was steady, without a hint of trembling, but his overly pale complexion and tightly pressed lips revealed an unspeakable vulnerability and grievance.

The hall was so quiet you could hear a pin drop.

Everyone’s gaze was focused on Chen Yinyu, filled with scrutiny, contempt, and a touch of schadenfreude as they watched the show.

Jin Wansi finally took a sip of tea before speaking slowly, his voice not loud, but every word was cutting.

"The Jin family has strict rules."

"Not just any stray cat or dog can walk through our doors."

"Since you’ve entered, you must know your place and understand the hierarchy."

"As an outsider who climbed into the Jin family on the strength of your face, you should keep your tail tucked in the future. Don't think you've truly become a master."

This speech was less of a lesson and more of a naked humiliation!

Jin Wansi’s face had turned the color of a pig’s liver, and he tried to speak several times, only to be glared back by Jin Wansi.

Chen Yinyu’s long eyelashes trembled, as if he had suffered a great blow, and the hand holding the teacup began to shake slightly.

Just then.

A fair, slender hand reached out and took the cup directly from Chen Yinyu’s hand.

Not accepted—taken.

Jin Yu expressionlessly placed the teacup on the table beside Jin Wansi with a "clack."

A few drops of tea splashed out, hot enough to make Jin Wansi pull his hand back abruptly.

"Second Uncle is getting on in years and your hands and feet aren't as nimble as they used to be, so your niece will help you."

Jin Yu’s tone was as flat as if she were commenting on the nice weather.

"This tea was served by the new son-in-law. Whether you drink it or not is your business."

"But the tea leaves of the Jin family were bought with money. If you don't want to drink it, don't let it go cold and waste it."

Her words were cold and hard, leaving no room for sentiment.

You want to talk about rules? I’m better at following rules than you are, and the rules of my Jin family are—don't waste money!

Jin Wansi’s face turned black instantly. He knew this niece had been sharp-tongued since she was a child, and typical intimidation wouldn't work on her.

He sneered, no longer pretending.

"Good! A sharp-tongued head of the Jin family indeed!"

He slammed his hand on the table, and the servant behind him immediately brought forward a thick ledger.

Jin Wansi grabbed the ledger and slammed it onto the center of the table with a loud bang!

"Jin Yu! Don't think I don't know what you're planning!"

"Look at this! These are the expenses for your wedding! You spent money like water, emptying out all the cash in the public treasury!"

"Now look, the silk shops in the south are waiting for us to pay for goods, the shipping fleet in the east is waiting for us to settle freight costs, and there isn't even a thousand taels of silver left in the accounts!"

"Are you going to drag the entire Jin family down just to support a pretty boy?!"

The mask was off!

This was his true purpose today!

The Jin family were merchants by trade, valuing cash flow above all else. With the massive expenses of the wedding, the accounts were empty; this was Jin Yu’s most vulnerable moment.

He chose to strike now to deliver a fatal blow!

"Uncle, you are joking."

Jin Yu’s expression turned cold. "Every expense for the wedding is recorded. It is impossible for it to shake the foundation of the Jin family."

"Impossible?" Jin Wansi acted as if he had heard the greatest joke in the world. "See for yourself!"

He pointed at the ledger, his voice rising sharply.

"To help you fill this hole and keep outsiders from laughing at our Jin family, I paid out of my own pocket, using my own private savings to cover the costs!"

"It is all clearly recorded here: 30,000 taels for wedding banquet ingredients! 50,000 taels for silk and gifts! And another 20,000 taels to grease the palms of the guests!"

"A total of 100,000 taels of silver! Jin Yu, I paid this money for you, for the entire Jin family! You must give me an explanation today! Pay me back immediately!"

"Otherwise, I will take this ledger to the ancestral hall and let all the elders judge! Let’s see how you’ve been running this family! Let’s see if you intend to squander the family business passed down by our ancestors just for an outsider!"

His tone was harsh and severe, pinning labels like "spendthrift" and "traitor" onto her.

The surrounding relatives from the branch families began to whisper, their eyes filled with doubt and dissatisfaction.

"It’s true, it’s inappropriate for a woman to manage the household..."

"Spending so much money on a man, what kind of behavior is that!"

"Wansi is doing this for the good of the family..."

In an instant, Jin Yu became the target of public criticism.

Wang Quan stood to the side, sweating profusely. He knew the Second Master was forcing a coup to seize power!

After all, Jin Wansan had no sons, so he had to hand the businesses over to Jin Yu, making her the head of the family.

Since taking over, Jin Yu hadn't made any mistakes and had even brought signs of prosperity to the Jin family. But a woman being the head of the family was never going to be fully accepted.

The most dissatisfied of all was Jin Wansi. He had always felt his brother should have given the position of family head to him.

However, Jin Wansan was merely weak-willed; although he often sighed that Jin Yu wasn't a man, he never had the intention of giving the family business to an "outsider."

Jin Yu took a deep breath, suppressing the anger in her heart.

She stepped forward, picked up the ledger, and flipped through it quickly. Her heart sank.

The accounts were done flawlessly.

Every expenditure had a name and evidence, even the signatures and seals of the suppliers.

There were no flaws to be found in such a short time.

Having just finished the wedding, she was exhausted and drained, unable to immediately dive into the kind of high-concentration audit work required.

Jin Wansi watched her increasingly grim expression, his triumph barely contained.

He pressed on: "Well, niece? With this in black and white, what else do you have to say?"

"Either pay the money back, or... hand over the family seal. You choose!"

The atmosphere in the main hall was heavy to the extreme.

Jin Yu’s fingers, gripping the ledger, turned white from the pressure. She was trapped in an unprecedented predicament.

Just at this tense, hair-trigger moment, a timid voice, filled with uncertainty and a hint of ingratiation, drifted from behind her.

"Uncle... elders..."

Everyone looked toward the sound and saw Chen Yinyu, who had been standing there like a piece of background furniture, had walked up to Jin Yu.

He bowed slightly, his face filled with trepidation, like a startled fawn.

"This... this ledger looks so thick, Miss... oh, no, my wife is tired, I’m afraid she won’t be able to finish reading it for a while."

He glanced cautiously at Jin Wansi, then quickly lowered his head and whispered:

"Could... could the nephew-in-law... help take a look?"

"When I was at the academy, I... knew a thing or two about arithmetic."

As soon as these words were spoken, the entire room was stunned for a moment, followed by an explosion of raucous laughter.

Jin Wansi pointed at Chen Yinyu and said to the crowd, "Listen to him! Listen! A penniless scholar who only knows how to recite dead books dares to say he understands our merchant accounts? This is the funniest joke I’ve heard all year!"

The other elders shook their heads, their disdain growing even stronger.

"Truly ignorant of the heights of the world!"

"Has he studied himself stupid?"

After laughing for a long time, Jin Wansi suddenly felt this was a perfect opportunity to humiliate Chen Yinyu and, by extension, strike at Jin Yu.

He waved his hand, his face wearing a playful expression like a cat toying with a mouse.

"Fine! Go ahead and look!"

He slammed the ledger onto the table in front of Chen Yinyu, making the teacups jump.

"I’ll say this now!"

"If you can find a single cent of discrepancy in this ledger, I, Jin Wansi, will kneel and apologize to you on the spot!"

"But if you can’t find anything..."

His eyes turned suddenly vicious and cruel, and he said, word by word:

"Then take off these clothes and roll out of the Jin family gates naked!"

**

chapters.title: Quantum Speed-Reading, Playing the Fool to Catch the Prey
chapters.content:
The main hall of the Jin residence was deathly silent, with only Jin Wansi’s vicious and malicious words echoing between the pillars.

Everyone’s gaze fell on Chen Yinyu—some with mockery, some with disdain, and some with the excitement of waiting for a good show.

Jin Yu’s heart sank, and she instinctively moved to shield Chen Yinyu behind her.

This man was bought by her; he was her person.

One must respect the owner before beating the dog. Jin Wansi’s words were not just humiliating Chen Yinyu, they were a hard slap to her face as the new head of the family!

However, just as she was about to step forward, her wrist was gently held by a cool hand.

It was Chen Yinyu.

He still kept his head slightly lowered. No joy or anger could be seen on his breathtakingly beautiful face. He gave Jin Yu an almost imperceptible shake of his head.

His eyes seemed to say: *Wife, don't worry, leave it to me.*

Jin Yu’s steps faltered.

She looked into Chen Yinyu’s eyes, which were as calm as an ancient well, and her heart inexplicably settled.

She was crazy.

She must be crazy.

To actually believe that this weak scholar could solve the deadlock before them.

Seeing the two "exchanging glances," Jin Wansi’s anger burned even hotter. He kicked out, sending the other two spare ledgers beside the table flying.

The three thick ledgers tumbled and landed at Chen Yinyu’s feet, kicking up a cloud of dust.

"Look!"

Jin Wansi pointed at the ledgers on the floor, his voice booming, his face ferocious.

"Don't say your uncle didn't give you a chance! Three ledgers! I'll give you plenty of time to look!"

"When you're done, get out!"

The branch relatives whispered to each other, their sneers undisguised.

"That pretty boy must be scared stupid."

"Does he really think he’s omnipotent after reading a few sage books? The tricks in merchant accounts are deep; can he even understand a single word?"

"Yu really was blind this time, finding such a piece of trash who only adds to the trouble!"

Amidst the noise and contempt, Chen Yinyu moved. He ignored everyone and slowly crouched down.

His slender fingers were well-defined, like fine mutton-fat jade.

He gently brushed the dust off the covers of the ledgers, picked them up one by one, held them in his arms, stood up, and walked to an empty table nearby to sit down.

Jin Yu’s heart tightened. She couldn't help but walk over, tugging his sleeve, and whispering: "You..."

She wanted to say, *Don't force yourself, I'll pay the money, I'll just accept the loss.*

But the words died on her lips, blocked by an assuring look from Chen Yinyu.

His gaze was very quiet, very deep, like the surface of a lake without ripples in the dead of night, reflecting the stars in the sky.

He said nothing, simply placing the first ledger gently on the table.

Then, he turned to the first page.

The hall went quiet instantly. Everyone watched him as if he were a fool.

Chen Yinyu’s fingers glided lightly over the pages, his gaze sweeping from top to bottom.

Immediately after, there was a "swish."

The first page was turned.

The speed was so fast that one had to wonder if he had even seen a single character on it.

Before anyone could mock him, a second "swish" rang out.

The third, the fourth...

At first, everyone thought he was just putting on a show, but gradually, everyone’s expressions changed.

Chen Yinyu’s page-turning speed grew faster and faster!

The sound of the pages turning, "swish-swish-swish," went from sporadic to a continuous, rolling wave of sound.

It was like an autumn wind sweeping through fallen leaves, or the tide washing over a beach.

The sound echoed in the terrifyingly silent hall, striking everyone’s heart, causing an inexplicable sense of trepidation.

His eyes seemed not like eyes, but like mirrors, responsible only for reflecting the content of the pages into his mind.

Ten lines at a glance—no, a page at a glance!

His focus was absolute, as if the entire world consisted only of him and the ledger before him, and all the clamor of the outside world was cut off from him.

The sneer on Jin Wansi’s face froze. He stared fixedly at Chen Yinyu, his brows knitted into a knot.

"Playing tricks!"

He couldn't help but sneer, trying to break the eerie atmosphere.

"Flipping through like that, can you see a single ghost-drawn symbol? Boy, don't waste everyone's time here!"

Chen Yinyu turned a deaf ear. In his world, countless numbers, entries, and seals were flowing by at high speed.

Jin Yu was also stunned.

To be honest, she also felt this was completely unreasonable.

But when she saw Chen Yinyu’s peerlessly handsome profile, saw the small shadow cast by his long, curled eyelashes under his eyelids, and saw his thin lips pressed tight in extreme concentration...

For some reason, an inexplicable sense of trust welled up.

Mainly... he looked so handsome when he was serious.

Forget it!

It was already at this point anyway; could it get any worse?

She took a deep breath, her cold gaze sweeping across the room.

"Let him look!"

"Even if he can't find anything, I, Jin Yu, will pay the 100,000 taels!"

"My people, even if it's just for show, are not for you to point fingers at!"

The statement was overwhelmingly domineering, protective to the extreme!

The main hall fell into silence once more, time slipping away quietly amidst the sound of pages flipping rapidly.

From the faint light of dawn until the sun was high in the sky, half an hour passed in silence.

When Chen Yinyu finished the last page and closed the third thick ledger, fine beads of sweat had already seeped onto his temples.

His complexion was several shades paler than before; clearly, this high-intensity, overloaded memorization had taken a massive toll on his energy.

He closed the book, slowly shut his eyes, took a long breath, and exhaled slowly.

Seeing this, Jin Wansi could no longer suppress the smugness on his face.

He stood up with a "whoosh," walked triumphantly toward Chen Yinyu, and looked down at him.

"Finished reading?"

"How was it, my good nephew-in-law? Did you find anything?"

"If you can't find anything, isn't it time to fulfill the bet?"

"Someone!" he shouted loudly. "Prepare to... change the clothes for our new son-in-law!"

Before the words had even faded, several burly servants had already rubbed their hands together and surrounded him, their faces full of mocking laughter.

Jin Yu's expression turned icy in an instant, her hand already reaching for the short whip at her waist.

The atmosphere in the entire hall was tense to the extreme.

Just at this critical moment, Chen Yinyu suddenly opened his eyes.

In that instant, it was as if a flash of lightning had streaked through his deep pupils.

Those eyes, which had always been timid and docile, now became as sharp as blades, their edge fully exposed!

It was the look of someone who had seen through all the fog and discerned every scheme!

He raised his head to meet Jin Wansi's triumphant gaze.

The corners of his mouth slowly curled into a cold arc, three parts mocking and seven parts knowing.

"Second Uncle."

He spoke softly; the voice was not loud, but it reached the ears of everyone present clearly.

"These accounts are truly 'well' done."

chapters.title: The Human Ledger
chapters.content:
Jin Wansi was stunned, then burst into an even more rampant laugh.

"Hahahaha! Good? Of course it's good! I made these accounts myself, how could they not be good?"

He puffed out his round belly, pointed at Chen Yinyu's nose, his face full of fat quivering.

"What, my good nephew-in-law, did you find some trick? Do you think the ink on one of the entries isn't handsome enough, or that one of the pages wasn't cut squarely?"

The several distant relatives behind him also joined in the laughter, looking at Chen Yinyu as if they were watching a clown who didn't know his own limitations.

Jin Yu's heart was in her throat again. What on earth was this man trying to do?

Did he really think that by flipping through books at that absurd speed, he could find the tricks that an old fox like her Second Uncle had hidden in the ledgers?

However, Chen Yinyu ignored Jin Wansi's mockery.

He didn't even look at the ledger again, just lowered his eyelids slightly, his long eyelashes casting a shallow shadow on his pale face, his voice clear and cold, without a ripple.

"Page three, line five."

His voice was not loud, but it had a strange penetrating power, making the entire noisy main hall go quiet instantly.

"Purchased five hundred catties of top-grade red candles, unit price two taels of silver. Second Uncle, although I am not a businessman, I know that even the most top-tier tribute red candles on the market cost no more than five mace per catty."

He paused, slowly raising those shimmering peach-blossom eyes, his gaze like a sword, piercing straight at Jin Wansi.

"Are these red candles of yours made of gold?"

As soon as these words were spoken, the whole hall was shocked!

The smile on Jin Wansi's face froze instantly, as if he had been doused with a basin of ice water, a flicker of imperceptible panic flashing in the depths of his eyes.

All the relatives present, every single one of them, were stunned.

He... he actually remembered?!

And, remembered so accurately! Even the page and line numbers were perfectly correct!

How is this possible!

Those were three thick ledgers, and he only used half an hour!

Jin Yu was even more shocked beyond measure; she subconsciously covered her mouth, her beautiful eyes full of disbelief.

She herself was an expert at playing with abacuses and ledgers, so she naturally knew what a terrifying ability it was to accurately pick out this one entry from a vast sea of items in such a short time!

Jin Wansi was an old hand after all; the panic lasted only a moment. He immediately flushed red and argued forcefully: "What do you know! Those were special tribute candles prepared for the government, made with spices shipped from the Western Regions, so the price is naturally expensive! What would a poor scholar like you know about the world!"

"Oh? Western Region spices?"

Chen Yinyu did not give Jin Wansi any chance to breathe. His speaking speed suddenly increased, like pearls falling onto a jade plate, crisp and dense.

"Then may I ask Second Uncle, page seven, purchased three hundred bolts of silk, recorded as 'Suzhou Embroidery Cloud Brocade,' why is it that what was received in the warehouse was ordinary Huzhou coarse cloth? The price difference between these two is surely much more 'fragrant' than your 'Western Region spices,' right?"

"Page ten, renovation of the South Courtyard warehouse, labor costs falsely reported for thirty people, construction period calculated for an extra month! Is Second Uncle planning to renovate the warehouse into an imperial palace?"

"Page fifteen, purchase of banquet wine, for the same batch of 'Daughter Red,' you recorded the cost three times! Does Second Uncle think our Jin family's money was blown in by the wind, and can be spent three times for every penny?"

"Page twenty-two..."

"Page thirty-seven..."

Chen Yinyu's voice grew faster and colder!

Every entry he reported was like a loud slap, fiercely striking Jin Wansi's face.

At first, Jin Wansi tried to stiffen his neck and argue a few words.

But Chen Yinyu's speed was simply too fast; one by one, item by item, the evidence was conclusive, the details clear, leaving him no room to interrupt or refute!

He was like a clown stripped of his clothes, all his dirty tricks exposed nakedly in the light of day!

The entire main hall was deathly silent.

Everyone was stunned by this scene, which could be called a miracle.

Was this still that submissive, easily bullied son-in-law? This was clearly a human-shaped ledger spirit wearing a beauty's skin!

His brain was even more precise than the old abacuses the accountants had used for over a decade!

Speaking of abacuses...

Chen Yinyu's gaze swept lightly and landed on an empty rosewood table nearby, where a large sandalwood abacus used by the accountants was placed.

He took a long stride and walked over slowly.

Amidst the suspicious and uncertain gazes of the crowd, his slender, jade-like fingers rested lightly on the abacus.

The next second!

"Clatter—!"

A sound of abacus beads colliding, as dense as a sudden rainstorm, suddenly resounded throughout the hall!

His left hand remained behind his back, and using only his right hand, his five fingers flew, moving so fast they almost left afterimages!

Those heavy sandalwood abacus beads seemed to be endowed with life at his fingertips, flying up and down, colliding fiercely!

"Click! Click! Click! Click!"

Every impact was like a heavy hammer, fiercely striking the chests of Jin Wansi and all the clansmen with ulterior motives!

While Chen Yinyu was moving the abacus at a dazzling speed, he continued to report the accounts without stopping.

"Additionally, tea purchases were marked up by thirty percent, totaling three hundred and twenty taels!"

"Transportation and porterage fees were falsely inflated by fifty percent, totaling five hundred and seventy taels!"

"Antiques and calligraphy were replaced with inferior goods, a price difference of one thousand two hundred taels!"

His voice intertwined with the rapid sound of the abacus, completely drowning Jin Wansi!

Jin Wansi's complexion had changed from the initial mockery to astonishment, then to deathly pale, and finally to a dull gray!

He was trembling all over, cold sweat soaking his luxurious silk clothes, his lips quivering, but he couldn't say a single word.

It's over.

Everything is over.

The fake accounts he thought were seamless were as fragile as a thin sheet of paper in front of this scholar who looked like he couldn't even truss a chicken!

How on earth did he do it?!

Is he even human?!

Jin Yu was completely dumbfounded.

She stared blankly at the man standing in front of the abacus, his expression focused, as handsome as a god.

Sunlight filtered through the window lattice, plating him with a faint golden glow. Those flying fingers, that cold profile, those lips that had become even paler due to extreme mental exhaustion...

All of this formed a highly impactful image, deeply branded into her heart.

She had always thought she had bought just a pretty ornament, a tool to anger Xun An and shut the mouths of the gossiping public.

But she never expected.

She... had actually bought a peerless treasure!

"Snap!"

Chen Yinyu's right index finger lightly pressed the last abacus bead, and the storm-like sound of the abacus stopped abruptly.

The whole world went quiet instantly.

Chen Yinyu slowly raised his head, his bottomless eyes reflecting Jin Wansi's bloodless face.

He parted his thin lips, his voice calm without a ripple, yet carrying the power of a judgment.

"Red candles, silk, labor, wine, tea, transportation, antiques... in total, thirty-seven errors and omissions, with a total false report of three thousand eight hundred and fifty taels, seven mace, and three candareens."

He smiled slightly, "Second Uncle, if all this money were exchanged for those 'gold-made' red candles of yours, I'm afraid it could light up half of Jinling City."

"Thump!"

Jin Wansi's legs went weak, and he collapsed into the grand armchair, his face like gold paper, gasping for air.

The hall was deathly silent; you could hear a pin drop.

All the relatives were like they had been hit by a freezing spell, each of them with their mouths wide open, their faces full of shock and fear.

Three thousand eight hundred and fifty taels! This was not a small sum! It was enough for a well-off family to live comfortably for several lifetimes!

What audacity this Jin Wansi had! What a black heart!

After a brief silence, the main hall suddenly erupted into irrepressible exclamations and discussions!

"My god! Over three thousand taels!"

"This... this is simply digging up the roots of our Jin family!"

"You can know a person's face but not their heart; I never expected that Second Uncle, who usually looks honest, would be so ruthless!"

And more gazes were cast with awe toward Chen Yinyu; this man had completely overturned all their perceptions of the words "son-in-law" and "scholar."

Jin Wansi listened to the surrounding murmurs and felt the scornful, angry gazes directed at him. His aged face shifted from pale to red, from red to purple, and finally turned as black as ink.

Shame, panic, and fury—various emotions intertwined and collided within his chest, eventually erupting into a fit of hysterical madness!

He sprang up from his chair, pointed at Chen Yinyu’s nose, and let out a beast-like roar.

"You... you are slandering me!"

"What right does an outsider like you have to audit the Jin family’s accounts! This is defamation of your elders! This is treasonous!"

Seeing his verbal battle end in a miserable defeat, he had completely torn off his mask, ready to resort to shameless bullying!

"Someone, come here!"

Jin Wansi, acting like a madman, pointed at Chen Yinyu and bellowed.

"Bring out the family law!"

"Drag this glib-tongued, elder-slandering scoundrel out and beat him to death!"

chapters.title: The Fatal Evidence
chapters.content:
Before his voice had even faded, the burly, loyal henchmen behind Jin Wansi grinned hideously and surrounded them.

They had long since found this frail, pretty-faced man an eyesore. Now that they had their master's order, they flexed their muscles, their knuckles cracking with "pop" sounds.

Jin Yu’s heart sank, and a towering rage surged from her chest straight to her head!

"How dare you!"

She shouted sharply. Before the henchmen could even get close, she grabbed the celadon teacup beside her and smashed it fiercely onto the floor!

"Crash—!"

With a crisp sound, the fine official-kiln porcelain shattered into pieces on the smooth bluestone floor, fragments scattering everywhere!

The clamor in the main hall fell silent instantly; everyone was stunned by this sudden turn of events.

Jin Yu stood up abruptly, strode in front of Chen Yinyu, and spread her arms, shielding him firmly behind her like a mother leopard protecting her cub.

Her bright, captivating phoenix eyes were burning with a raging fire, and her cold, piercing gaze shot straight at Jin Wansi.

"Touch my man?"

Her voice was not loud, but every word was like tempered ice, carrying an indisputable arrogance and majesty.

"Just try it!"

Jin Wansi was so shaken by her terrifying aura that he subconsciously took half a step back.

He had never seen Jin Yu like this!

Was this still the niece who only knew how to fiddle with an abacus? This was clearly a vengeful deity in a true rage!

"You’ve rebelled! You’ve rebelled! You little wench..." Jin Wansi roared, his bluster masking his inner fear.

However, before he could finish, a rhythmic and heavy sound of footsteps came from outside the hall.

Steward Wang led a team of Jin family guards armed with staves, flooding in like a tide, instantly surrounding Jin Wansi and his incompetent henchmen.

These guards had all been promoted by Jin Yu herself and were fiercely loyal to her. At this moment, their faces were grim and their eyes unfriendly, waiting only for Jin Yu’s command to beat these people who dared to disrespect the son-in-law until they couldn't find their teeth.

The disparity between the two sides was clear at a glance.

The atmosphere in the main hall was stifling to the extreme.

Just at this critical moment, a light chuckle broke the deadlock.

"My lady, do not be angry."

Chen Yinyu reached out his slender, slightly cool hand and gently grasped Jin Yu’s trembling wrist.

His voice remained as gentle and refined as ever, seemingly carrying a power to soothe the heart.

Jin Yu turned back to meet his deep, pool-like eyes. The concern and worry visible within them miraculously calmed the rage in her heart.

Chen Yinyu gave her a reassuring smile, then turned to face the livid Jin Wansi once more.

He leisurely pulled a few neatly folded sheets of paper from his wide sleeves.

"Second Uncle, don't be impatient."

He flicked the papers against his fingertips, producing a crisp sound. "The accounts are only a minor matter."

Chen Yinyu curled his lips slightly, but the smile did not reach his eyes; it carried a chilling, heart-stopping coldness.

"Here, there is a major matter."

Jin Wansi looked at the papers in his hand, his eyelids twitching wildly, and an extremely ominous premonition rose in his heart.

He didn't know what they were, but his intuition told him that those things were even more lethal than the fake account book from earlier!

Chen Yinyu did not keep them in suspense.

He didn't even look at the content on the papers, but lowered his eyes and began to recite in a steady, unhurried tone.

"The third year of Jinghe, the fifth day of the third lunar month, at night, in the Heaven-grade private room of the Zui Xian Lou."

"Second Uncle conspired with Liu Fu, the manager of the Liu Family Trading Firm, regarding a batch of silk from the Jin Family’s Southern Goods Store."

Jin Wansi’s pupils contracted sharply!

The Liu family!

How could he know?!

Chen Yinyu seemed not to notice his instantly pale face and continued to recite in that calm, emotionless tone.

"Second Uncle promised to help the Liu family pass off inferior goods as superior, a 'civet cat for a crown prince' scheme. Once successful, the Liu family was to pay a thirty-percent kickback."

"Furthermore, Second Uncle promised that once you took charge of the Jin family, you would 'transfer' the most profitable shop in the south of the city to the Liu family at thirty percent of its market value..."

"Boom!"

Jin Wansi felt as if something had exploded in his brain!

It’s over!

It’s all over!

He had handled this matter with extreme secrecy; besides himself and Liu Fu, it was impossible for a third person to know!

This Chen Yinyu... how on earth did he find out?!

"You... you... slanderer! Forgery! This is a forgery!"

Jin Wansi was completely unhinged. He pointed at Chen Yinyu, roaring with a hoarse voice, spittle flying everywhere.

"What evidence do you have?! You want to slander me with empty words?!"

"Evidence?"

Chen Yinyu smiled lightly, a trace of pity in his expression, as if watching the final struggle of a clown.

He raised his hand and clapped twice.

"Clap! Clap!"

The crisp sound of applause echoed.

Steward Wang understood immediately, turned, and shouted toward the door: "Bring him in!"

Soon, two guards brought in a thin young man dressed in the attire of a waiter.

As soon as the waiter entered and saw Jin Wansi, he trembled all over and immediately buried his head low.

When Jin Wansi saw the man's face clearly, the last trace of blood drained from his own.

It... it was that waiter from Zui Xian Lou!

"Second Uncle, do you still recognize this person?" Chen Yinyu’s voice echoed eerily.

"On the night of the fifth of the third month, it was he who served tea to you and Manager Liu outside the private room."

The waiter was pressed to his knees by the guards. Under Chen Yinyu’s encouraging gaze, he mustered his courage, lifted his head tremblingly, and pointed at Jin Wansi, shouting with a tearful voice: "I... I recognize him! It’s this master! That night, I heard with my own ears... heard them talking about a 'civet cat for a crown prince,' and... and something about a thirty-percent kickback..."

A witness!

He even had a witness!

The material evidence was the flawed account book, the motive was the dirty deal recorded in the letter.

Now, even a living witness stood right before them!

The chain of evidence was completely closed!

Jin Wansi could no longer hold himself up. His legs went weak, and he collapsed to the floor like a pile of mud, making strange "ho-ho" sounds in his throat, like a fish out of water.

He knew he was completely finished.

Colluding with outsiders to harm the family’s interests was an unforgivable felony in any clan!

The clansmen in the main hall now looked at Jin Wansi not with scorn, but with bone-deep hatred and anger.

A traitor! He was simply the scum of the Jin family!

Jin Yu looked coldly at Jin Wansi, who was sprawled on the floor. On that once-arrogant, fat face, there was now only despair and deathly gray.

She walked slowly to him, looking down at him from above, her voice devoid of any warmth.

"Second Uncle."

"Betraying the family, colluding with outsiders, emptying out the family business, and attempting to usurp the position of the head of the house."

With every word she spoke, Jin Wansi’s body twitched.

"According to our Jin family’s clan rules, what should be done?"

Jin Yu’s voice echoed in the empty main hall, carrying the weight of a judgment.

Just then, a hoarse and powerful cough suddenly came from behind the tightly closed screen in the main hall.

"Ahem!"

Everyone turned their heads to see the heavy carved sandalwood screen being slowly pushed open from the inside.

Jin Wansan hadn't left after all. He had just walked away, and everyone assumed he had snuck off as usual.

After all, the struggle between Jin Yu and Jin Wansi was a common occurrence, and Jin Wansan always acted as if it had nothing to do with him.

But they didn't know that Jin Wansan had never left; it was just that Jin Yu had never suffered a major loss, so he hadn't needed to appear.

chapters.title: Cleaning House, Taking Control of the Accounts
chapters.content:
Seeing his father return, Jin Yu felt a slight stir in her heart, but she remained calm on the surface.

She knew her father wasn't indifferent; he just couldn't be bothered with small matters.

But once someone touched the foundation of the Jin family and encroached upon his most cherished money bag, this old man, who looked like a Maitreya Buddha, would instantly transform into a tiger protecting its food.

Jin Wansan’s gaze swept across the room. His eyes, which were usually narrowed, were now flashing with sharp light, carrying the oppressive aura of someone who had long held power.

He didn't look at Jin Yu, nor at Chen Yinyu, and didn't even spare a glance for the terrified clansmen.

Instead, he fixed his gaze directly on Jin Wansi, who was sprawled on the floor.

"Second brother."

Jin Wansan’s voice was very calm, revealing neither joy nor anger.

Jin Wansi shuddered, as if injected with a burst of strength. He scrambled over, hugged Jin Wansan’s legs, and wailed loudly.

"Big brother! Big brother, you must uphold justice for me! This little beast... no, Chen Yinyu, he is slandering me, he forged the evidence, he is trying to sow discord between us brothers and seize our Jin family’s assets!"

Jin Wansi cried incoherently, attempting one last struggle.

Jin Wansan lowered his eyes, looking at his own younger brother who was covered in tears and snot. The cowardly, conciliatory look he had worn earlier was gone; he seemed like a different person.
