At the docks, torches crackled and popped, illuminating the entire area as brightly as day.

Squads of government soldiers, holding long spears, patrolled back and forth with expressionless faces, their boots making dull "patter" sounds on the waterlogged wooden planks.

On the perimeter of the soldiers stood a group of even fiercer men.

They were the Liu family’s thugs—all of them thick-necked and broad-shouldered, their shirts open to reveal tattoos, their eyes scanning every corner with vicious intent, looking just like a pack of vicious guard dogs.

The officials and bandits were in league, and the security was so tight that not even a bird could fly in.

Chen Yinyu hid behind a pile of discarded crates, taking it all in.

He took a deep breath, suppressed the waves of emotion in his heart, adjusted the crooked goatee on his face, hunched his back, and stepped out from the shadows.

He did not dodge at all; instead, he limped toward the most heavily guarded main entrance.

"Stop! Who goes there!"

Two of the Liu family’s thugs immediately crossed their long staffs, blocking his path, their eyes filled with malice.

Chen Yinyu stopped immediately, his face piling up with a humble and fawning smile, looking exactly like an accountant who had spent years reading people's expressions.

He pulled a ledger, wrinkled from the rain, from his bosom, held it high, and spoke in a Mandarin dialect with a heavy southern accent: "Officers, officers, I’m an accountant newly hired by the yamen to count the cargo. Look, here are the travel permits and the ledgers."

His accent was crucial.

To handle this inspection, the government had indeed temporarily drafted a group of clerks skilled in arithmetic from other regions, and their accents were varied.

One of the thugs stepped forward and rudely snatched the ledger and permit. He flipped through two pages, and seeing that they were indeed stamped with the government’s red seal, three parts of his suspicion vanished.

But he still had no intention of letting him through. Instead, he poked Chen Yinyu’s chest with his staff and asked viciously: "Counting cargo this late? Can't it wait until tomorrow?"

Chen Yinyu hunched his back even lower, his face displaying a perfectly measured look of awkwardness and trepidation: "Officers, you don't understand. The higher-ups are pressing hard, saying this shipment is of vital importance. The count must be verified tonight, and it has to be sealed and put into storage by tomorrow morning. I am only following orders, and I hope you two gentlemen can make things a little easier for me."

As he spoke, he unobtrusively slid two small pieces of silver from his sleeve and, with a quickness born of practice, pressed them into the palms of the two thugs.

The silver was small, but it felt cold and heavy in their hands.

The two thugs exchanged a glance, and the fierce look on their faces softened significantly.

One of them weighed the silver in his hand and muttered vaguely, "You know how to play the game."

The other waved the long staff in his hand and barked impatiently, "Get in! Be quick about it, don't wander around, and if you get into trouble, you're on your own!"

"Yes, yes, thank you, officers, thank you!"

Chen Yinyu nodded and bowed repeatedly, like a pardoned dog, then hurried inside with his back hunched.

The interior of the wharf was even more chaotic. Soldiers and thugs were busy moving crates of cargo off the ships; no one noticed the addition of a sallow-faced, wretched-looking accountant.

Chen Yinyu held his ledger, pretending to wander around a few ships, and soon locked onto the Jin family’s *fuchuan* (flat-bottomed junks).

The massive "Jin" sign on the hulls looked particularly glaring under the firelight.

The area around these ships was guarded more heavily than anywhere else.

He did not approach rashly but circled to the rear of the fleet, where the light was dim, with only a few oil lamps flickering precariously in the wind.

He heard a series of heavy, creaking friction sounds, accompanied by suppressed gasps, coming from the bottom of the cargo hold of the largest ship.

*So, there is something fishy going on.*

Chen Yinyu’s heart sank.

He scanned his surroundings and, taking advantage of a gap in the patrol, darted forward with the agility of a civet cat, slipping silently into the shadows of the *fuchuan*.

He pressed himself against the cold hull and found an inconspicuous vent, leaning in close.

A thick, fragrant scent of tea mixed with a strange, briny, fishy odor drifted into his nostrils.

Peering through the gap in the vent, he saw the scene in the bottom of the hold, and his pupils contracted sharply!

He saw several of the Liu family’s trusted men stealthily prying open tea crates marked with the Jin family’s seal.

They pushed aside the top layer of tea, carefully scooped out handfuls of snow-white powder from sacks nearby, poured it all in, covered it back up with the tea, and resealed the crates.

The powder shimmered with a crystalline luster in the dim light.

*Salt!*

*It’s illicit salt!*

According to the laws of the Great Jing, those who traffic in illicit salt are treated as traitors, a crime punishable by the execution of one's entire clan!

*What a vicious scheme!*

Chen Yinyu felt a chill shoot from the soles of his feet to the top of his head; his blood felt as if it were about to freeze.

He could already see the image of Jin Yu wearing prison garb and being dragged to the execution ground.

*No! Absolutely not!*

His gaze swept rapidly across the hold and settled on the sacks containing the illicit salt.

In the bottom right corner of each sack was a faint, branded emblem—the internal mark of the Liu family’s trading firm!

He quickly pulled a piece of thin paper and an ink stick from his robe, pressed the paper firmly against the wooden slats of the vent, and, relying on his photographic memory, traced the shape of the emblem in the dim light.

After doing this, he saw a shipping logbook in the corner. A man who looked like a foreman was checking things off in it and finally signed his name.

That book recorded which crates they had tampered with!

*I must get it!*

Chen Yinyu’s brain raced, his eyes landing on a pile of debris nearby.

He picked up a pebble and flicked it with his finger.

*Clack!*

The pebble hit an empty wooden barrel in the distance with a crisp sound.

"Who's there?!"

The people in the hold grew tense. The foreman immediately tucked the logbook into his waistband and rushed out with two men.

*Now!*

Chen Yinyu darted out from the shadows like a ghost, snatched the real shipping logbook that had fallen to the ground, and quickly grabbed a handful of the illicit salt, wrapping it in oil paper.

*Got it!*

His heart leaped with joy, and he prepared to retreat the way he came.

However, at that very moment, an unexpected turn of events occurred!

A large rat darted out from somewhere, and in its panic, it slammed into a precarious oil lamp nearby!

*Crash!*

The oil lamp hit the ground and shattered. A flame roared to life, instantly illuminating the dark corner!

"Fire! There's someone over there!"

The foreman, who had just gone out to investigate, happened to return and roared at the sight.

Almost at the same time, a flurry of hurried footsteps sounded nearby.

A gloomy, familiar voice rang out: "What’s going on? Why all the shouting?"

*It’s Xun An!*

Chen Yinyu’s heart skipped a beat, and he instinctively shrank back into the shadows of the cargo crates.

Xun An walked over quickly with a few men. Seeing that the small fire had already been stamped out by the thugs, he frowned in dissatisfaction.

His gaze scanned the surroundings, inadvertently sweeping over the corner where Chen Yinyu was hiding.

In the darkness, although the face of the hunched figure in the accountant’s clothes could not be seen clearly, the thin, slender silhouette felt strangely familiar to Xun An for some reason.

An inexplicable irritation welled up in his heart.

He narrowed his eyes, staring fixedly at the figure like a viper that had spotted its prey.

"Stop!"

Chen Yinyu’s feet froze in place.

Xun An approached step by step, the scrutiny and suspicion in his eyes growing more intense.

He barked sharply: "You there, look up!"

**

chapters.title: Life-and-Death Pursuit, the Scholar Leaps into the River
chapters.content:
The air seemed to solidify at that moment. The "crackling" of the burning torches and the "patter" of the falling rain became exceptionally clear.

Chen Yinyu’s spine was as stiff as iron. He knew that if he looked up, everything would be over.

Even though his face was disguised with makeup, it was impossible to deceive Xun An; he would likely recognize him even if he were reduced to ashes.

Just as Xun An impatiently took another step closer, Chen Yinyu’s hunched body suddenly moved!

He didn't turn around or resist; instead, he kicked hard at a sack in the pile of debris beside him!

It was the final barrier he had prepared for himself—lime powder!

*Bang!* The sack burst open.

The white powder exploded like a dense fog, forming a choking curtain in the wind and rain, heading straight for Xun An and the oil lamp that had just been stamped out but still held embers!

"Cough, cough, cough! What is this!"

"My eyes!"

The thugs around Xun An were instantly blinded, howling in pain as they clutched their faces.

Xun An reacted the fastest, slamming his sleeve over his nose and mouth, but the pungent dust still made him cough violently, his eyes burning with intense pain.

*Now!*

In the chaotic white mist, Chen Yinyu’s figure shot out like an arrow from a bow!

"Stop! Stop him, damn it!"

Xun An’s voice came from behind, filled with the rage of one who had been played. "Catch him! Don't let him get away! He’s a spy for the Jin family!"

That shout was like a spark thrown into a vat of oil; the entire wharf exploded into chaos.

The soldiers and thugs who had been moving cargo turned in unison, countless fierce eyes locking onto the thin figure sprinting through the rainy night.

"Over there! Quick!"

"Surround him!"

Disorderly footsteps and curses rang out from all directions. A net made of blades, spears, and staves was tightening rapidly around Chen Yinyu.

Chen Yinyu’s heart pounded wildly in his chest, threatening to leap out of his throat.

Cold rain mixed with cold sweat blurred his vision; his lungs felt as if they were being scorched by fire, and every breath brought a tearing, agonizing pain.

But he dared not stop; he could not stop!

Only one thought remained in his mind—get out! Get out with this sole piece of evidence!

Jin Yu was still waiting for him.

His gaze swept rapidly across the chaotic wharf, his brain working at an unprecedented speed.

Ahead, several thugs were closing in on him with blades drawn.

Chen Yinyu’s eyes narrowed as he spotted the cables used for hoisting cargo.

Without hesitation, he pulled a short dagger he had prepared from his boot and, with a flick of his wrist, slashed hard at the taut hemp rope!

*Creak—*

After a harsh sound of friction, a massive bundle of fishing nets suspended in mid-air plummeted, landing squarely on the thugs charging in the front!

"Ouch!"

"Damn it!"

The men were instantly tangled tightly, rolling into a heap.

Chen Yinyu didn't even look back. He kept moving, turning into a narrow alley packed with cargo crates.

The pursuers behind him were surging forward, the distance closing.

Listening to the approaching footsteps, he gritted his teeth, turned around, and used all his strength to slam into a stack of wooden crates piled half a man’s height high.

*Rumble!*

The crates collapsed one after another like dominoes, instantly blocking the entire narrow passage.

"Damn it! The path is blocked! Go around!"

The pursuers were briefly obstructed, letting out frustrated roars. Chen Yinyu took this opportunity to sprint another few dozen paces.

The exit of the wharf was within reach; the familiar dense forest was not far away!

The dawn of victory seemed to be right before his eyes!

However, at that very moment, a lethal sense of crisis struck him from behind!

Chen Yinyu instinctively tried to dodge to the side; he heard it—the sound of a bowstring vibrating.

Behind the chaotic pursuers, Xun An snatched a heavy bow from a soldier, his eyes bloodshot.

He had no intention of taking a live captive; he only wanted the person who dared to play him and make him lose face in public to die!

"Go to hell!"

A savage sense of satisfaction flashed across Xun An’s face as his fingers suddenly released.

*Whoosh—!*

The arrow pierced the air, flying with lethal precision through the rainy night toward the center of Chen Yinyu’s back!

At the critical moment, relying on his instinct for survival, Chen Yinyu twisted his body sharply to the side!

*Thwack!*

The arrow missed his heart but buried itself deep into his left shoulder!

An agonizing pain exploded instantly, as if a red-hot branding iron had pierced through his flesh and into his marrow!

"Ugh!"

Chen Yinyu let out a muffled groan of pain. The immense force sent him stumbling forward, and he fell heavily to the ground.

Blood instantly stained the coarse cloth of his clothes on his back, blooming into a jarring, dark red blotch in the cold rain.

"Catch... catch him..."

He struggled to climb back up, but his left arm was completely devoid of strength. The piercing pain made his vision go black in waves.

The sound of footsteps behind him grew closer, and a flicker of despair crossed Chen Yinyu's eyes.

No!

He jerked his head up to look ahead. At the end of the pier lay the surging, black-waved river.

Pursuers behind, a dead end ahead!

Xun An's twisted, triumphant face flickered in the firelight.

Chen Yinyu felt as if he could already hear his mocking laughter after victory, as if he could already see the tragic scene of the entire Jin family being dragged to the execution grounds.

A surge of strength, from nowhere, flooded his limbs.

With his remaining functional right hand, he pressed the oil-paper-wrapped bundle of evidence tightly against his heart.

Inside were the rubbings of the Liu family firm's seal, that crucial ledger, and the fatal stash of illicit salt.

This was the Jin family's only path to survival!

"Jin Yu..."

Chen Yinyu whispered the name, and the last shred of hesitation in his eyes turned into resolve.

He pushed off the ground, used his last ounce of strength to stand up, and then, to the astonishment of his pursuers, turned without hesitation and leaped!

*Splash!*

His thin figure was like a drifting fallen leaf, instantly swallowed by the dark, icy river.

"He jumped into the river!"

"Quick! Fire arrows! Shoot! I want to see him alive, or see his corpse!"

Xun An rushed to the edge of the pier, roaring in a frenzy as he watched the ripples spreading outward.

*Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!*

Countless feathered arrows shot into the river, but they only stirred up futile splashes before quickly disappearing.

The river water was bone-chillingly cold, instantly stripping Chen Yinyu of all warmth and strength.

The wound on his left shoulder throbbed with a numbing, excruciating pain as it soaked in the river water, and his consciousness was fading rapidly.

But he dared not let go.

He guarded the oil-paper bundle against his chest with his right hand, letting the cold river carry him downstream, sinking into deeper darkness...

I do not know how much time had passed.

In a hidden reed marsh downstream, on an inconspicuous small boat, Steward Wang was as anxious as an ant on a hot pan.

"Why isn't he here yet... I hope nothing has happened to the son-in-law..."

As he muttered, his sharp eyes caught sight of a dark shadow floating on the river not far away.

Steward Wang's heart tightened, and he hurriedly poled the boat toward it.

When he got close, he looked by the faint light of a lantern, and his soul nearly left his body!

It was Chen Yinyu!

Steward Wang scrambled to haul the man onto the boat; his touch met with bone-deep coldness.

On the boat, Chen Yinyu's face was as pale as paper, his lips blue and purple, his body soaked through, and the clothes on his left shoulder were drenched in blood, a shocking sight.

He had completely lost consciousness and fallen into a deep coma.

Yet, even so, his right hand was still clutching the small oil-paper bundle against his chest, his knuckles white, as if it were his entire life.

Steward Wang checked his breath; there was still a faint trace of life.

He dared not delay, shivering as he squeezed a few words through his teeth.

"Back to the manor... hurry!"

chapters.title: Returning in Blood, A New Way to Eat Soft Rice
chapters.content:
Just past the hour of the Rat, all was silent.

The back door of the Jin manor was pounded with a "bang, bang, bang," the sound urgent and heavy, like a death knell.

"Open the door! Open the door quickly!"

Steward Wang's hoarse roar shattered the silence of the night.

As soon as the night watchman pulled back the bolt, a thick, heavy stench of blood mixed with the damp chill of the river rushed in, choking them to the point of nausea.

The next moment, they saw a sight they would never forget—

Steward Wang's tall frame was hunched over, and on his back was a man, soaked through and unconscious.

The coarse clothes on the man were torn to shreds, and his left shoulder was soaked through with dark red blood, congealed into a terrifying black-purple.

His pale cheeks had not a drop of blood, and beneath his closed eyes were dark, bruised sockets. Only that breathtakingly beautiful face, washed clean by the river, allowed them to recognize him as the Jin family's son-in-law, Chen Yinyu.

"Quick! Go fetch Doctor Zhang! Take all the best ginseng and snow lotus from the warehouse!" Steward Wang's eyes were bloodshot, his voice trembling uncontrollably. "Go, now!"

The entire Jin manor erupted in chaos.

Lamps were lit one after another, and the sound of messy footsteps and gasps filled the air.

A single lamp still burned in Jin Yu's bedroom. She had long been awake and knew of Chen Yinyu's mission.

She leaned against a daybed by the window, holding a cup of tea that had long since gone cold, listening to the sound of the rain outside with a restless heart.

He hadn't returned yet.

An unprecedented panic coiled around her heart like vines, making it hard for her to breathe.

Just then, the door was slammed open.

The maid Lianqiao rushed in, her face deathly pale, unable to speak clearly: "Miss! It... it's not good! The son-in-law, he..."

Jin Yu's heart sank, and she stood up abruptly.

Before she could ask, she saw Steward Wang stumbling into the courtyard, carrying that blood-soaked, mangled figure on his back.

*Clatter—*

The tea cup in her hand, a "sky-after-rain" celadon worth a hundred gold, fell to the floor, the delicate porcelain shattering into countless pieces, just like her heart at that moment.

Jin Yu's mind went blank.

She stared blankly at the person being carefully placed on the bed, at his paper-pale face, at his blood-soaked shoulder.

"What happened... how could it be like this..."

Her voice was as thin as a mosquito's, and her body began to tremble uncontrollably.

Doctor Zhang was quickly brought in by the servants, and upon seeing Chen Yinyu's injuries, he gasped.

"An arrow wound! And soaked in water! This... it's only by the grace of the ancestors that he's still alive!"

"Scissors! Strong spirits! Wound powder!"

The maids scrambled to prepare the items, but Jin Yu stood frozen like a puppet.

When Lianqiao handed her a bottle of high-quality wound powder, she reached out, but her hands shook so much she couldn't even hold the small porcelain bottle.

"Miss!" Lianqiao was on the verge of tears.

"Get out!"

Jin Yu shoved her aside, snatched the scissors, and began frantically cutting away the blood-matted fabric from Chen Yinyu's shoulder herself.

Her movements were urgent and chaotic, completely lacking her usual composure.

Tears fell like broken pearls, uncontrollably, landing on Chen Yinyu's cold hand.

"Who told you to go!"

"Who told you to be a hero! Chen Yinyu! You bastard!"

She cursed through gritted teeth while crying, her voice filled with a fear and despair she hadn't even realized herself.

"Don't you love money the most? Is it worth risking your life for that bit of evidence?"

"If you die! I'll buy ten or eight more tomorrow! Every one of them will be more obedient than you!"

As she cursed, her voice choked up, leaving only suppressed, helpless sobs.

She had never been so afraid.

Even when her father forced her to marry, even when Xun An broke off their engagement in public, she had never felt this pain of her heart being torn open.

So, unknowingly, this "ornament" she had bought had become a pain that breathed with her.

Under the dual stimulation of the strong spirits and the excruciating pain, the unconscious Chen Yinyu let out a muffled groan of pain, his long eyelashes fluttered, and he slowly opened his eyes.

What met his gaze was Jin Yu's tear-streaked face, filled with shock and rage.

"Wife..."

As he spoke, his voice was as raspy as if it had been rubbed with sandpaper. The movement pulled at his wound, and a fine layer of cold sweat instantly broke out on his forehead.

"Shut up! Don't speak!" Jin Yu roared, her eyes red.

Chen Yinyu acted as if he hadn't heard, just staring at her steadily.

He saw the panic in her eyes, saw the tears she shed for him, and a hard corner of his heart suddenly collapsed, turning soft.

He tugged at the corners of his mouth, trying to squeeze out a reassuring smile, but it only made him wince in pain.

Even so, he used his uninjured right hand to tremblingly fish out the small, oil-paper-wrapped bundle from his soaked chest.

The oil-paper was soaked through by the river, its edges badly worn, but he had guarded it well.

"Wife... why are you crying..."

He gasped for air, every word spoken with extreme difficulty. "Is this ledger... worth... worth the price of admission?"

He looked at Jin Yu, a hint of cunning, like someone seeking credit, in his eyes, as if waiting for her praise.

"This time... count it as a work-related injury... I... I need a raise..."

All of Jin Yu's anger and scolding were blocked in her throat at this moment.

She looked at his face, which was devoid of color from the pain, yet he was still stubbornly haggling over money with her. Her heart felt sour and swollen, and her tears flowed even more fiercely.

This fool.

The biggest fool under heaven.

She didn't scold him for being greedy, nor did she yell at him again.

Jin Yu leaned down, ignoring the astonished gazes in the room, and kissed his cold forehead gently.

Then she lifted her head, looked him straight in the eyes, and said word by word: "The money is yours, your life is mine. Chen Yinyu, listen well: no more getting hurt from now on."

Her gaze was fiercer than ever, like a lioness completely provoked, flashing with a bloodthirsty light.

"Since the Liu family is looking for death, I will grant their wish."

After saying this, she resolutely took the oil-paper bundle, still warm with his body heat and stained with his blood, turned abruptly, and strode out.

"Wang Quan!"

"I am here!"

"Prepare the sedan! Notify the magistrate, tell him the Jin Firm is going to strike the Dengwen Drum!"

Her clear, murderous voice echoed under the night sky, carrying a madness that would stop at nothing.

After Jin Yu left, the room fell silent.

The maids efficiently bandaged Chen Yinyu's wounds, fed him ginseng soup, and then quietly withdrew.

Chen Yinyu lay alone on the bed, the cool scent of Jin Yu's Hengwu fragrance still lingering in his nose, and the touch of her soft lips still remaining on his forehead.

He lifted his uninjured hand to touch his forehead gently, then looked at the thick bandages wrapped around his left shoulder.

The bright red bloodstains on it were slowly spreading, and his eyes grew deep and dark, bit by bit, like a deep sea hiding a storm.

He recalled the arrogant and overbearing faces of the officials and bailiffs at the pier.

He recalled the face of Xun An, twisted with jealousy, and the savage look on his face when he fired that arrow.

And he recalled even more vividly the helplessness and despair he felt in that split second before he threw himself into the river.

Jin Yu had money; the Jin family was the wealthiest in Jiangnan.

But so what?

In the face of true power, in the face of those who held the knives, the brushes, and the official seals, no amount of wealth was anything more than a fat sheep waiting to be slaughtered.

He had gambled his life to return with the evidence today.

But what about next time?

The Liu family had officials behind them; Xun An had powerful backers.

If they dared to kill to silence witnesses at the pier today, they would dare to fabricate charges tomorrow and drag the entire Jin family into an abyss from which there was no return.

What would Jin Yu do then?

Money alone could not protect her, and his own petty cleverness could not protect her either.

In this man-eating world, only power was the most indestructible shield.

Chen Yinyu’s gaze slowly shifted to the sandalwood bookshelf in the corner of the room.

On the bottom shelf, several dust-covered copies of the *Four Books and Five Classics* lay quietly, as if mocking his former humiliation.

They were among the few belongings he had brought with him when he married into the family.

After arriving at the Jin household, he had never touched them again. He had once thought that this was how his life would be—staying with his wealthy wife, living as a kept husband without a care in the world; that was fine, too.

But now he knew: it was not enough, nowhere near enough.

The pride and ambition of a scholar, suppressed for so long within his chest, were thoroughly ignited at this moment by that tearful kiss from Jin Yu.

Chen Yinyu gritted his teeth, enduring the tearing pain in his left shoulder, and used his right hand to push against the edge of the bed, struggling bit by bit to sit up.

Cold sweat instantly soaked his undergarments, but he paid it no mind.

Barefoot, he walked step by step toward the bookshelf.

His slender fingers brushed the dust off the spines, revealing the familiar gold-stamped characters.

He picked up the copy of the *Great Learning*, his fingertips gently stroking the yellowed pages, as if touching another life of his that had been abandoned.

After a long while, he let out a low laugh, the sound appearing exceptionally clear in the empty room.

"It seems..."

"I'll have to find a new way to eat this 'soft rice'."

chapters.title: The Dengwen Drum Resounds, a High-Stakes Gamble of Commoner Against Official
chapters.content:
Outside the room, Wang Quan felt a jolt at Jin Yu’s murderous words, but years of composure prevented him from rushing in immediately.

He stepped forward, lowered his voice, and reasoned clearly: "Miss! The sedan chair is already prepared, but it is the dead of night. The gates of the prefectural office are tightly shut; even if you beat the drum, the effect will be greatly diminished!"

"It would be better to wait until the third quarter of the Mao hour at dawn when the commoners are out on the streets. If you beat the drum then, the commotion will spread throughout the entire city! With everyone’s eyes on you, even the Prefect won't be able to suppress it!"

Wang Quan’s words were like a basin of ice water, extinguishing the flames of Jin Yu’s impulsiveness.

She slowly closed her eyes, and when she opened them again, the madness in her gaze had faded, leaving only a coldness and determination like a frozen pool.

She was Jin Yu, someone who had reached this point through calculation and courage. She could afford to lose money, but she could never afford to lose her head.

"You are right."

Her voice was hoarse. "I was too hasty. Pass on my orders: summon all the managers of the shops and estates in the city overnight. They must see me in the main hall before dawn! Also, go to the accounting office and withdraw one hundred thousand taels in silver notes; I have a use for them."

That night, Jin Yu did not sleep at all.

She did not return to her bedroom but sat in the study, with the ledger—the one bought with half of Chen Yinyu’s life and still stained with the scent of blood—spread out before her.

The flickering lamplight stretched her shadow long and thin, casting it onto the wall like a silent jade statue.

She did not cry, nor did she curse again.

She simply looked quietly at the shocking names and numbers on the pages, the temperature in her eyes cooling inch by inch until it froze over.

Daylight broke, and the morning mist appeared.

In the main hall of the Jin residence, a dozen managers stood in terrified silence, not daring to breathe loudly.

Everyone knew about the young master’s ambush and the blood spilled at the gate last night, and they could all feel the oppressive atmosphere of a storm about to break.

Jin Yu walked in, step by step.

Though she had not slept all night, there was no sign of fatigue on her face, only a calmness as if she were prepared to perish together with her enemies.

"Everyone." She stood still, her gaze as sharp as a knife, slowly sweeping over each person.

"From today on, all businesses under the Jin firm—the rice shops, cloth stores, restaurants, pawnshops... all are to be suspended."

"All liquid assets, land deeds, and property titles are to be concentrated in my hands."

As soon as she finished speaking, the hall was in an uproar!

An old manager stood up, trembling: "Miss, this must not be! If the business stops, the daily losses will be more than a thousand gold pieces! This is... this is cutting off your own meridians!"

"Cutting them off?" Jin Yu sneered.

"That is exactly what I intend to do! I want the people of this entire city to see what they will eat without the Jin family’s rice! What they will wear without the Jin family’s cloth!"

"This lawsuit is about injustice and it is fueled by silver. I want the Liu family, I want this Prefect, and I want everyone in this city to know that Jin Yu’s money is too hot to handle! And that my people are not to be touched!"

Her words were resonant and firm, and the madness of her willingness to pay any price made everyone shudder.

Returning to her bedroom, the maids had already prepared her attire.

It was not plain clothing, nor was it everyday wear.

It was a dark red palace-style ceremonial gown, kept at the bottom of the Jin family’s chest, modeled after the regulations for a first-rank noble lady, embroidered with a "hundred birds paying homage to the phoenix" pattern in pure gold thread.

This outfit exceeded her station and was ostentatious; it was the ultimate display of the Jin family’s wealth and status, a dowry that Jin Wansan had spent his entire fortune to create for his daughter, which had been buried at the bottom of a chest for three full years.

Today, it became Jin Yu’s battle armor.

The complex layers of the gown were piled high, the heavy gold and jade phoenix crown pressed down on her hair, and the cold tassels hung by her cheeks.

Jin Yu looked at herself in the bronze mirror—her face cold and glamorous, exuding an imposing nobility, yet carrying an aura of slaughter—and her eyes remained without a ripple.

She said calmly to Wang Quan, who stood to the side: "Uncle Wang, you have been with me the longest and are the most steady."

"If I do not return today..."

She paused, her tone as calm as if she were speaking of someone else’s affairs.

"Distribute the family property among the servants in the house and let them find their own way to make a living. Don't let a single copper fall into the hands of the Liu family or those jackals."

Wang Quan’s heart gave a violent tug, and his eyes instantly turned red; the girl he had watched grow up was going to risk her life.

He knelt down heavily and kowtowed: "Rest assured, Miss! This old servant will wait for you outside the prefectural office! If you do not come out, this old servant will not leave, even in death!"

Jinling Prefectural Office.

Beneath the solemn and majestic stone lions, commoners had already gathered early on.

The Jin family’s luxurious carriage, drawn by four fine horses and inlaid with gold and jade, stopped arrogantly right at the front gate of the office; it was hard not to attract attention.

Jin Yu stepped down from the carriage, escorted by a group of servants.

Dressed in her finery, her gait was steady, and every step seemed to fall upon the heartbeats of all those watching.

"Who goes there! Step back from the front of the prefectural office!" the bailiffs at the gate shouted.

Jin Yu did not even glance at them, walking straight toward the giant, dust-covered drum on the side.

The Dengwen Drum!

Established by the Taizu Emperor of the Great Jing Dynasty, it could not be struck unless there was a grievance of heaven-shaking proportions. Once struck, it reached the ears of the Emperor, and the case had to be recorded, reported through the layers of bureaucracy, and sent all the way to the Ministry of Justice.

However, regardless of whether the striker was in the right or wrong, they would first have to endure the "killing-power rods" or the "nail board" to demonstrate the gravity of their words—it was no trivial matter.

Jin Yu stood before the drum, her slender, fair hands gripping the drumstick, which was thicker than her own arm.

She took a deep breath and, using all her strength, struck it with a heavy blow!

"Dong—!"

A dull, heavy, and massive sound, carrying endless grievance and fury, shattered the silence of the Jinling morning.

The sound seemed not to come from the surface of the drum, but from the depths of the earth, shaking the hearts of all who heard it.

The surrounding crowd instantly exploded into chaos!

"Heavens! It’s the Dengwen Drum!"

"Is that... the eldest daughter of the Jin family?"

"The Jin family is wealthy enough to rival a nation; what grievance could they have that requires beating this life-risking drum?"

"Dong—!"

"Dong—!"

Jin Yu ignored everything, using all her might to strike it twice more in succession.

Three drum beats, the sound shaking the entire city—it could not be revoked!

In the back hall of the prefectural office, Prefect Zhang Dechang was holding a bowl of ginseng tea, leisurely listening to a small tune.

The Liu family had already sent generous gifts last night, promising to double them once the matter was settled.

He was just calculating how to suppress this minor affair when the highly penetrating sound of the drum reached him.

"Dong—!"

His hand shook, and the scalding tea spilled onto his hand, causing him to yelp in pain.

"Is... is that the Dengwen Drum?"

The leisure on his face was instantly replaced by panic. "Who? Who is so bold?!"

The secretary ran in, stumbling and crawling, his face deathly pale: "My Lord! It’s bad! It’s Jin Yu of the Jin firm! She... she has struck the Dengwen Drum!"

Zhang Dechang’s face turned livid. That mad woman! How dare she!

He had intended to drag things out for ten days or a half-month, until Chen Yinyu’s body had rotted in the river, and then close the case as an "accidental drowning."

But by striking the drum, she had brought the matter completely into the open, right under the watchful eyes of the Ministry of Justice!

"Open the court!" Zhang Dechang gritted his teeth, squeezing the words out from between them.

He slammed the gavel down heavily!

"Wei—Wu—"

Zhang Dechang sat on the high bench, looking at the woman below who was dressed in finery and standing with her back straight, a flash of malice in his eyes.

He decided to give her a show of force first to dampen her spirit.

"Who is it below, and why do you beat the drum?" he asked, knowing the answer perfectly well, his official authority on full display.

"Commoner Jin Yu, accusing the Liu firm of colluding with officials to commit murder for wealth!" Jin Yu’s voice was clear and firm.

"Presumptuous!"

Zhang Dechang slammed the gavel again and shouted sternly, "Bold, insolent woman! Why do you not kneel before this official?"

"Furthermore, do you know the rules of striking the Dengwen Drum? Regardless of right or wrong, you must first receive thirty 'killing-power rods'! Do you know your crime?!"

The commoners outside the hall gasped; thirty rods would strip the skin off a person, if not kill them outright!

Everyone’s eyes were fixed on Jin Yu, waiting to see how she would respond.

But Jin Yu showed not the slightest fear; instead, she straightened her neck, which was aching slightly from the weight of the phoenix crown, and stared directly at Zhang Dechang.

Her voice was not loud, yet it carried clearly throughout the courtroom and beyond.

“This commoner knows her crime, but she knows even better that she has been wronged!”

She suddenly raised her volume, every word dripping with blood: “As long as Your Honor dares to preside over this trial! Dares to grant the Jin family justice! Then I, Jin Yu, shall take these disciplinary beatings on behalf of my husband, whose life hangs in the balance!”

As the words fell, the perspective shifted abruptly back to the Jin manor, where Chen Yinyu awoke amidst a tearing, agonizing pain.

What met his eyes was the familiar canopy of the bed, the air thick with the heavy scent of medicine.

“My lady…” he called out instinctively, his voice hoarse and dry.

The answer was the panicked sobbing of the maid, Lianqiao.

“Master, you’re awake? My lady… my lady has gone to the magistrate’s office!”

“She… she went to strike the Dengwen Drum!”

The three words “Dengwen Drum” exploded in Chen Yinyu’s mind like a thunderclap!

His handsome face, pale from blood loss, instantly drained of all color, and a raging storm churned within his peach-blossom eyes.

That fool!

He struggled to sit up, but the movement was too sudden; the stitches on his left shoulder burst open instantly, and bright red blood quickly seeped through the thick bandages.

“Master, you mustn’t!” The physician guarding him was horrified and rushed forward to hold him down. “Your injuries are extremely severe; you absolutely cannot move!”

Chen Yinyu, however, seemed not to feel the pain and shoved the physician aside.

He panted heavily, growling at the terrified maid nearby: “Go! Bring me that copy of the *Great Jing Code*, and my blood-stained green robe!”

The maid dared not delay and scrambled to fetch them.

Ignoring the horrified gazes of everyone present, Chen Yinyu used his one good hand to tremble, yet firmly, pull on the blood-soaked garment.

The scent of blood mixed with the cold fragrance of medicine, shrouding him in an aura of grim determination.

Clutching the heavy legal code in one hand and bracing himself against the bed with the other, he stood up unsteadily.

He walked barefoot across the cold floor, stepping toward the door, leaving a faint bloody footprint with every step.

“Prepare the carriage.”

His voice was cold as ice. “To the magistrate’s office. Whoever dares to touch her, I will destroy them.”

###

chapters.title: Under the Disciplinary Rod, the Ailing Husband’s Legal Suppression
chapters.content:
Inside the magistrate’s office, Zhang Dechang was so furious he laughed. He had not expected this woman to be so unyielding, willing to be flayed alive just to escalate the matter.

He slammed the gavel down heavily, the malice in his eyes no longer concealed.

“I shall grant you your martyrdom!”

“Men! Drag this unruly woman down and give her thirty disciplinary strokes!”

At the command, two rows of bailiffs holding water-and-fire staves swarmed in like wolves and tigers.

The staves were thicker than a woman’s arm, soaked in tung oil, dark and gleaming with a cold light. The tips were wrapped in iron, studded with barbs; a single strike would surely tear skin and mangle flesh.

The commoners outside the court gasped, and many timid women covered their eyes, unable to bear the sight.

Jin Yu, however, did not even blink.

She knelt straight on the cold bluestone floor, her gorgeous, eye-catching ceremonial dress looking completely out of place in the grim courtroom.

As long as she could obtain justice, let alone thirty strokes, she would even endure a bed of nails!

The bailiffs’ sneers grew louder in her ears. The staves were raised high, whistling through the air, and brought down fiercely toward Jin Yu’s slender yet straight back!

Just at this critical moment—

“Stop!”

A hoarse, weak, yet piercing cry came from the entrance of the magistrate’s office.

Everyone looked toward the sound to see a figure, supported by Wang Quan, stumbling into the courtroom.

The man wore a green robe, already stained a shocking dark red by dried blood.

His face was as pale as gold leaf, his lips devoid of color, his black hair disheveled.

It was Chen Yinyu!

Jin Yu’s pupils contracted sharply; her heart felt as if it were being squeezed by an invisible hand, causing her such pain she could barely breathe.

That fool! Was he throwing his life away? Hadn’t she told Wang Quan to watch him!

Chen Yinyu saw no one else but the woman in red kneeling in the hall, about to be struck by the staves.

He shook off Wang Quan’s support and, using the last ounce of his strength, stumbled and lunged toward Jin Yu.

*Thump.*

He did not stand; he collapsed with his entire weight, landing perfectly to shield Jin Yu’s petite frame beneath his own body.

His thin, frail back was bared directly to the descending staves.

“…”

The entire courtroom fell into a deathly silence.

The raised staves hung in mid-air. The bailiffs’ arms froze; looking at the blood-stained green robe and the frail back of the man, no one dared to deliver the first blow.

Beating the wife of a wealthy merchant was following orders.

But beating the plaintiff of the case, a severely injured man who looked like he might stop breathing at any second… if they beat him to death, they could not bear the consequences!

“Cough… cough, cough, cough!”

Chen Yinyu lay over Jin Yu’s back, coughing violently. Every spasm seemed to tear at his heart and lungs, his spine heaving with the effort, and fresh blood seeped from beneath the bandages, staining the green robe further.

Jin Yu could clearly feel his burning body temperature and his uncontrollable trembling. Her eyes turned red instantly.

“Chen Yinyu…” her voice trembled.

“My lady, do not fear.”

Chen Yinyu’s face was buried in the crook of her neck, his voice low and hoarse, carrying a reassuring steadiness.

He slowly raised his head. Those peach-blossom eyes, which should have been filled with soft spring water, were now like ice-tempered blades, staring fixedly at Zhang Dechang on the high bench.

“Your Honor…”

He gasped for breath, using his uninjured hand to point tremblingly at the gorgeous ceremonial dress Jin Yu wore.

“If Your Honor must beat… then beat this commoner. My life is cheap and not worth mourning.”

His voice was so weak it seemed it might snap at any moment, but the content of his words made everyone prick up their ears.

“It is just that… the cloud-brocade dress my wife wears was commissioned by the Jin family from the best embroiderer in Jiangnan, modeled after the ‘Hundred Birds Paying Homage to the Phoenix’ pattern made by the Imperial Weaving Bureau for the Empress Dowager’s birthday. It took three years to weave…”

He paused deliberately, and amidst the collective intake of breath, he slowly delivered the second half:

“This commoner only fears that the disciplinary rod has no eyes. If this garment is ruined, and this ‘Phoenix Dignity’ is defiled… if word gets out, I fear it may be labeled by those with ill intent as a grave disrespect toward the Empress Dowager!”

*Boom!*

With this heavy accusation leveled against him, Zhang Dechang’s face turned green!

He knew Chen Yinyu was twisting logic and arguing sophistry!

How could a replica dress have anything to do with the palace?

But the “Hundred Birds Paying Homage to the Phoenix” pattern was indeed imperial property, especially when linked to the “Empress Dowager.” He wouldn’t dare gamble on that possibility even if he had a hundred times his current courage!

If the matter escalated and the censors in the capital submitted a memorial accusing him, the Governor of Jinling, of allowing his subordinates to destroy imperial dignity and show contempt for the royal family, would his official cap still be on his head?!

This Chen Yinyu, who looked like a scholar without the strength to truss a chicken—how could he have more schemes than a beehive!

“Bastard!”

Zhang Dechang cursed inwardly, but could only swallow his fury and wave his hand impatiently: “All of you, stand down!”

The bailiffs, as if granted amnesty, quickly withdrew the staves and retreated to the sides.

The crisis was temporarily averted.

Jin Yu’s tightly wound nerves relaxed slightly, only to feel the body shielding her sway, as if it might collapse at any moment.

She reached back to support him, but Chen Yinyu did not give her a chance to catch her breath.

He braced himself against Jin Yu’s shoulders, using the leverage to force himself into a kneeling position, and then pulled a book from his robes.

It was the *Great Jing Code*!

Before Zhang Dechang could make another move, he spoke first:

“Reporting to Your Honor, this commoner has read a few volumes and recalls that in the ‘Great Jing Code: Household Law: Tax Regulations,’ it is clearly recorded—”

“‘Any merchant family that pays over ten thousand taels in taxes in one region may be treated as gentry. Their head of household and his legal wife are exempt from kneeling before officials. Unless they have committed the ten heinous crimes of treason, colluding with the enemy, or rebellion, no state or prefectural office shall subject them to interrogation by torture!’”

With every word he recited, Zhang Dechang’s face grew uglier.

After finishing, Chen Yinyu raised his bloodshot eyes, staring straight at him, and asked word by word:

“May I ask Your Honor, since my Jin family moved to Jinling, for ten years, we have paid over one hundred thousand taels in taxes annually, far exceeding the ‘ten thousand tael’ threshold.”

“My wife has neither rebelled nor colluded with the enemy; she has only come to seek justice for her husband. Why does Your Honor wish to use the ‘disciplinary rod’—a form of torture—on her?”

“This… exactly which law is this based on?!”

This series of questions was like a string of loud slaps across Zhang Dechang’s face.

The commoners outside the court were stunned at first, then erupted into thunderous applause!

“Well said! There is a law to follow, why beat people indiscriminately!”

“So our Great Jing Dynasty has this law! The Jin family is our great benefactor, supporting so many people; why should they suffer this indignity!”

“That young master… cough, that husband is truly a scholar! He has talent!”

Public opinion had completely shifted to the Jin family.

Zhang Dechang’s face turned the color of a pig’s liver. Sitting on the high bench, he felt the gazes of everyone below piercing him like needles.

He knew the intimidation tactic had failed, and if he continued to press the issue, he would only lose more face.

“Hmph! Since that is the case, I shall waive your disciplinary strokes!”

Zhang Dechang slammed the gavel with feigned severity, forcing the page to be turned.

“Resume the trial—!”

He practically spat the words out through gritted teeth. “Summon the plaintiff, Jin Yu; the aggrieved party, Chen Yinyu; the defendant, Liu Fugui of the Liu Firm; and the witness, Xun An!”

Following the bailiffs’ summons, a middle-aged man in brocade, with a stout figure, was brought in—it was the head of the Liu family, Liu Fugui.

Behind him followed a young scholar in a moon-white brocade robe, wearing a jade crown, looking exceptionally polished and bright.

It was Xun An.

As soon as Xun An entered, his gaze fell upon the disheveled Chen Yinyu.

When he saw Chen Yinyu’s blood-stained robe and pale face, a flash of imperceptible satisfaction crossed his eyes.

Then, seeing Chen Yinyu leaning weakly in Jin Yu’s arms, and Jin Yu protecting him with a look of heartache, that satisfaction instantly turned into poison-tipped jealousy.

He bowed respectfully to Zhang Dechang with a graceful posture, forming a sharp contrast with the two people kneeling on the ground.

Then, he turned around and looked down at Chen Yinyu, a hypocritical and compassionate smile curling at the corners of his lips.

"Brother Yinyu, you... why must you suffer like this?"

chapters.title: Meteorological Evidence, a Dimensional Strike by a Logical Genius
chapters.content:
How intimate, yet how hypocritical, that "Brother Yinyu" sounded.

Chen Yinyu seemed not to hear the thorns in his words; he did not even lift his eyelids.

He simply leaned quietly against Jin Yu, like an injured young beast that had found a sanctuary, exposing all his weakness and reliance before her without reservation.

Jin Yu’s heart felt both soft and pained. She tightened her grip on Chen Yinyu’s arm, raised those phoenix eyes tempered with ice, and gave Xun An a cold, scathing look.

That gaze seemed to say: What kind of thing are you to even be worthy of calling him "brother"?

The smile on Xun An’s face stiffened for a moment. What he hated most was this look from Jin Yu.

It was the contempt of a superior—a look that looked down on him and couldn't even be bothered to speak more to him.

He took a deep breath, suppressed the surging jealousy and resentment in his heart, and put back on that hypocritical, compassionate mask.

Zhang Dechang, on the bench, had long since lost his patience. He slammed the gavel down hard and shouted sternly, "Silence!"

"Witness Xun An, step forward to be heard!"

Xun An smoothed his bright, magnificent robes and walked leisurely to the front of the court.

"Commoner Xun An, greetings to your Honor." He bowed deeply, his posture graceful, fully displaying the elegance of a scholar.

Zhang Dechang nodded with satisfaction. This was the kind of witness he wanted: well-mannered and possessing integrity.

"Xun An, I ask you: on the night of the fourteenth of April, did you see the Jin family's boatmen smuggling official salt at the pier outside the city?"

Xun An straightened up, his gaze sweeping over Chen Yinyu’s paper-white face, and a nearly imperceptible arc curled at the corner of his mouth.

He replied loudly, "In reply to your Honor, I saw it with my own eyes. Every word is true!"

"That night, I had just composed a fine line for an essay and was feeling inspired, so I went out for a night stroll and walked near the pier."

"I happened to see the Jin family's boat docking, and a group of boatmen were acting suspiciously, moving bags of cargo off the boat."

"Feeling suspicious, I crept closer to take a look."

He paused, deliberately holding back, and only continued after everyone’s heart was in their throat: "By the bright moonlight, I saw clearly that the sacks were stamped with a vermilion character for 'Private'!"

"Not only that, I heard them whispering, saying things like, 'Once this batch of goods is sold, we won't have to worry about food or drink for the rest of our lives!'"

"With both human and material evidence present, the Jin family’s smuggling of official salt is an ironclad fact!"

Xun An spoke with resounding force and full of detail, as if he had truly been at the scene.

The commoners outside the court began to whisper, and many changed the way they looked at Jin Yu.

The Jin family had always had a good reputation; who would have thought they were doing such head-chopping business behind the scenes?

Liu Fugui stood to the side, a smug smile appearing on his fat face.

It was done!

With a "scholar" like Xun An as a witness, the credibility was far higher than if he had just found a few thugs!

Jin Yu was trembling with rage, her fingernails digging deep into her palms.

Nonsense!

The Jin family’s salt bags were always stamped with the Jin family’s "Jin" emblem; when had there ever been a "Private" character!

This was clearly a malicious slander!

Just as she was about to speak up to refute him, she felt her hand being patted gently.

It was Chen Yinyu.

He was still leaning against her, his breath weak, as if a gust of wind could blow him over, but those pitch-black eyes were startlingly bright.

Jin Yu looked at him, and the raging fire in her heart miraculously calmed down.

She chose to believe him.

Chen Yinyu coughed twice softly and spoke slowly.

"Brother... Brother Xun..."

This call seemed to exhaust all his strength, making one's heart tremble.

Xun An looked down at him, a trace of contempt flashing in his eyes: "Does Brother Yinyu have any advice?"

"I wouldn't dare..."

Chen Yinyu coughed a few more times, caught his breath, and asked in a tone of almost naive curiosity: "I am just... a bit curious."

"Since Brother Xun could see so clearly, you must have... been very close at the time, right?"

Xun An was stunned. He hadn't expected him to ask this. Wasn't that obvious? How could he have seen it clearly if he wasn't close?

He said proudly, "Naturally, I was no more than ten paces from that boat."

Chen Yinyu nodded, like a student thirsty for knowledge, and continued to ask: "Then... the moonlight that night must have been excellent?"

This question hit the nail on the head for Xun An!

He had been worrying about how to emphasize the truthfulness of his testimony, and Chen Yinyu had handed him the ladder himself.

What a fool!

Xun An sneered inwardly, but on the surface, he feigned a look of recollection and said loudly, "More than excellent! The moonlight that night was bright, clear as a silver plate, illuminating the entire pier as if it were broad daylight! Otherwise, how could I have seen the writing on the sacks?"

To make his story more credible, he added a superfluous detail.

"And the night was clear and breezy, with a gentle river breeze blowing on my face. It was very pleasant; I remember it clearly!"

After he finished speaking, he looked at Chen Yinyu triumphantly, his eyes full of intellectual superiority.

Look, this is the gap between you and me.

You can only survive by relying on a face and a woman's protection, while I, with a flick of my tongue, can cast you and the Jin family behind you into an abyss of no return!

The commoners outside the court nodded one after another, feeling that what Xun An said was reasonable.

Yes, if it were dark and one couldn't see, there would be no point in testifying.

However, after hearing his detailed description, a strange smile slowly bloomed on Chen Yinyu’s pale face.

The smile was very faint, but it made Xun An’s heart skip a beat for no reason.

"So... that’s how it was."

Chen Yinyu murmured, and then, to the astonishment of everyone, he tremblingly pulled a rolled-up document from his blood-stained sleeve.

The paper of the document was slightly yellow, and it was stamped with a bright red, square official seal that ordinary people could not understand.

"Your Honor."

Chen Yinyu raised his head, his gaze passing over Xun An and shooting straight at Zhang Dechang on the high bench. "I happen to have a piece of material evidence here as well."

Zhang Dechang frowned: "Present it!"

The bailiff took the document and presented it to Zhang Dechang. Zhang Dechang only glanced at the red official seal, and his pupils shrank violently!

—The Seal of the Imperial Observatory!

This... this is an official document from the Jinling branch of the Imperial Observatory! Where did this son-in-law get such a thing?!

Chen Yinyu seemed to see through his thoughts and smiled weakly:

"I know that my words are light and carry little weight, and I feared no one would believe me."

"So, before coming to the yamen, I specifically had my steward go to the Jinling branch of the Imperial Observatory and spent one hundred taels of silver to purchase the Jinling meteorological records for the night of April 14th."

Boom!

As soon as these words were spoken, the whole hall was shocked!

Meteorological records? What was that? And you could buy it with money?

The Jin family... was just too rich!

Xun An’s face turned white in a flash, and an ominous premonition rose in his heart.

Chen Yinyu ignored the shock of the crowd. Relying on his memory, he recited the contents word for word.

"Jinghe Year 7, April 14th, night."

"Starting at the Hour of the Bo (9-11 PM), dark clouds obscured the moon, with lightning and thunder."

"From the Hour of the Zi (11 PM) to the end of the Hour of the Chou (1-3 AM), there was a torrential downpour, rain falling like a waterfall, with gale-force winds blowing from the northwest, and water spouts visible on the river."

"That night, there was no moon, no stars, and one could not see one's own fingers."

"..."

The entire courtroom was deathly silent.

With every word Chen Yinyu spoke, Xun An’s face turned a shade paler.

When he finished the last sentence, "one could not see one's own fingers," Xun An’s body began to tremble violently and uncontrollably.

The silence lasted for three breaths.

"Pfft—"

In the crowd outside the court, someone couldn't help but laugh out loud.

This laugh was like lighting a powder keg, instantly igniting the entire audience!

"Hahahaha! So Young Master Xun has night vision! He could see writing ten paces away in a torrential rainstorm!"

"What night vision, I think it's the Heavenly Eye! He could see as clearly as day without a moon!"

"Clear breeze and bright moon? Gentle river breeze? Bah! The wind that night almost blew the roof off my house! He must be living in a dream!"

"This lie is too outrageous! Does he think we, the people of Jinling, are all fools?!"

The mockery, the laughter, and the contempt pierced into Xun An’s ears.

His face turned the color of a pig's liver, and sweat poured down, soaking his temples.

"No... that's not it!"

He shouted in a panic, trying to defend himself, "I... I used a lantern! Yes! I saw it by the light of the lanterns at the pier!"

He thought he had grabbed a straw, but Chen Yinyu just looked at him coldly, as if looking at a clown.

"Lanterns?"

He asked softly, his voice tinged with a hint of pity.

"Brother Xun, you have studied the books of the sages for so many years; do you not even understand the principle of 'a cup of water on a cartload of burning firewood'?"

"In the midst of a gale and torrential rain, let alone a small lantern, I fear even a sky full of bonfires wouldn't last a single breath, would it?"

"Or perhaps... Brother Xun, you were using the Lotus Lantern that only the immortals in heaven can light, which the wind cannot blow out and the rain cannot extinguish?"

These piercing words completely shattered Xun An’s last line of psychological defense.

His legs went weak, and with a "thud," he collapsed to the ground in a sorry state, his face ashen.

Chen Yinyu couldn't be bothered to look at him again. He turned to Zhang Dechang, whose face was already as dark as water, and delivered the most fatal blow.

"Your Honor, I also remember that the 'Criminal Law: Litigation' section of the *Great Jing Code* states—"

"'Anyone who gives false testimony without cause, confuses the public, or obstructs justice shall, depending on the severity of the circumstances, be punished with eighty strokes of the heavy staff or exiled three thousand li.'"

"May I ask your Honor, Xun An has lied in court, fabricated false evidence, and intended to frame my Jin family. What punishment should this conduct receive?!"

chapters.title: Micro-Identification, the Killing Blow in the Stitches
chapters.content:
The articles of the *Great Jing Code* were like a loud slap across Zhang Dechang’s face, which was full of official arrogance.

He, the dignified Prefect of Jinling, had actually been rebuffed in his own courtroom by a mere matrilocal son-in-law using the law.

What was even worse was that the person Chen Yinyu had questioned was none other than Xun An, the "irrefutable witness" he had personally selected.

To punish Xun An would be equivalent to admitting his own incompetence, acknowledging that this trial had been a farce from the very beginning.

Yet, if he did not punish him, where would the dignity of the law be? Where would the credibility of his office remain?

Zhang Dechang’s face turned from blue to white, the veins on the back of his hand, gripping the gavel, bulging with tension.

He could not fathom how a man who relied on his looks to climb the social ladder could recite the *Great Jing Code* by heart, and be even more proficient in it than he, the presiding judge!

As the stalemate persisted, Liu Fugui, who had been silent until now, could no longer sit still.

He squeezed his obese frame forward, cupped his hands toward the bench, his voice dripping with a slick, self-assured confidence.

"My Lord, calm your anger! This matter of perjury is indeed detestable, but it is merely a trivial detail!"

"The human witness may be flawed, but the material evidence is absolutely certain!"

Liu Fugui pointed at the bulging sacks on the courtroom floor, his voice rising sharply.

"Prefect, these bags of illicit salt were seized by the bailiffs themselves from the Jin family’s cargo ship. It was witnessed by all—the culprit and the stolen goods were caught together!"

"Jin Yu, Chen Yinyu, this is ironclad evidence you cannot deny!"

His words were like a lifeline, instantly snapping Zhang Dechang out of his predicament.

Right! Even if the human witness had collapsed, there was still the material evidence!

As long as it was confirmed that this salt was seized from the Jin family’s ship, the charges would still stand!

Zhang Dechang’s eyes turned fierce. He slammed the gavel down, attempting to regain control over the rhythm of the court.

"Guards! Bring the evidence forward!"

Several bailiffs immediately stepped up and laboriously hauled the heavy sacks to the center of the courtroom.

The openings of the sacks were tightly bound with thick hemp rope, appearing perfectly normal.

Liu Fugui stood to the side, his mouth curling into a greasy, triumphant smile.

He didn't believe these inanimate objects could grow mouths and overturn the case for the Jin family.

Jin Yu supported Chen Yinyu, feeling the slight tremor in his body, and her heart ached beyond measure.

She was about to tell Wang Quan to inspect them, but she saw Chen Yinyu shake his head at her gently.

He struggled, seemingly trying to stand up.

"What are you doing?" Jin Yu hurriedly held him down.

Chen Yinyu did not explain, only looking at her and saying, "Yu'er, help me over."

Jin Yu looked into his ink-black eyes, which held not a shred of retreat, only a calm sense of strategic mastery.

As if under a spell, she nodded and helped him walk toward the lethal "material evidence."

The eyes of everyone outside the court were focused on the couple, watching the beauty who seemed ready to shatter at any moment endure his pain, stubbornly walking toward the bags of illicit salt.

Xun An, slumped on the ground, saw this scene and a flash of malicious glee crossed his eyes.

*Putting on a show! Even if I let you see it, so what? Can you stare at it until it turns into a flower?*

Finally, the two reached the sacks.

Chen Yinyu did not look at the bags themselves but slowly crouched down—a movement that drained the last bit of color from his already pale face.

Jin Yu’s heart tightened; she longed to pull him back into her arms immediately.

Chen Yinyu, however, seemed not to feel the pain. He reached out his slender, knobby fingers and gently stroked the rough stitching at the opening of the sack.

Time seemed to stand still at that moment.

Everyone held their breath.

After a long while, Chen Yinyu slowly raised his head, his gaze like a torch, staring directly at Zhang Dechang on the high bench.

"My Lord, may this commoner speak?"

Zhang Dechang frowned and waved his hand impatiently: "Speak!"

Chen Yinyu pointed to the unremarkable seam, his voice not loud, yet clearly audible throughout the entire courtroom.

"My Lord, please look. The stitching technique used at the opening of these salt bags is dense and the thread is tucked inward. It is the 'reverse stitch' method from 'Su embroidery'."

*Su embroidery? Reverse stitch?*

The crowd looked at each other, completely bewildered. How did a case about smuggling salt get involved with embroidery?

Even Jin Yu was stunned. Chen Yinyu... how did he know these things?

Liu Fugui sneered, thinking Chen Yinyu was truly desperate and had started babbling nonsense.

Chen Yinyu ignored the crowd's reaction. He continued to explain unhurriedly, like a patient schoolteacher.

"The Jin family’s trading firm also has an embroidery workshop. To please my wife, I once learned a little about it."

With one light sentence, he explained the source of his knowledge while simultaneously showing off their affection.

Jin Yu’s cheeks flushed slightly, but a sweet, indescribable feeling welled up in her heart.

"Our Jin family embroidery workshop has a huge output. To rush production, all our goods are sealed using the simplest and fastest 'flat stitch' method—the stitches are coarse and sparse, with thread ends exposed."

He paused, then shifted his tone to look at Liu Fugui.

"But this 'reverse stitch' hides the stitches inside, making the exterior smooth. While it is sturdier and more beautiful, it is extremely time-consuming and laborious."

"As far as this commoner knows, in the entire city of Jinling, there is only one embroidery workshop that uses this technique on its goods—"

"And that is the Liu family’s trading firm, used only for their high-end silk goods destined for overseas export!"

*Boom!*

The moment these words were spoken, it was like a thunderclap on a clear day!

Liu Fugui’s smile froze on his face, and his fleshy cheeks began to twitch visibly.

*This... how is this possible!*

*How could he know so clearly! He even knows what kind of goods their workshop uses it for!*

Jin Yu instantly reacted. Her shrewd merchant’s mind immediately grasped the key point.

Without waiting for Zhang Dechang to speak, she raised her voice and shouted to Wang Quan outside the court: "Steward Wang!"

"Go! Go to the shop opposite us immediately, and send someone to the Liu family’s shop. Bring back one sample of the cloth bags we and the Liu family use for packing goods!"

"Yes, Miss!" Wang Quan took the order and bolted away.

Jin Yu’s command was decisive and imposing; this was the true master of the Jin family!

In less time than it takes to drink a cup of tea, Wang Quan ran back, gasping for air, holding two brand-new hemp bags high in his hands.

"My Lord! The samples have been retrieved!"

The bailiffs presented the two samples, placing them side-by-side with the "evidence" on the floor.

One bag’s opening was coarse, with thread ends clearly visible; the other had dense, smooth stitching.

And those sacks containing the illicit salt had a stitching technique identical to the samples from the Liu family’s shop—there was no difference at all!

"Hiss—"

The commoners outside the court gasped.

"My God! They really are exactly the same!"

"So, these bags containing the illicit salt belong to the Liu family after all!"

"What a clever trick, a thief crying 'stop thief'! How sinister!"

All eyes instantly shifted from suspicion of the Jin family to contempt and anger, all directed at Liu Fugui!

Liu Fugui felt the blood drain from his body, a chill shooting from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.

*It’s over!*

He had calculated everything—the human witnesses, the location of the frame-up—but he had never imagined the problem would arise from a tiny, inconspicuous stitch!

Just as he was teetering, Chen Yinyu’s cold voice drifted into his ears.

"Master Liu,"

Chen Yinyu slowly stood up, looking down at him, "How did the specialized bags from your own embroidery workshop travel across the sea and end up on our Jin family’s ship?"

He tilted his head slightly, a purely harmless smile curling his lips, but his words were piercing.

"Could it be... that these bags full of illicit salt grew legs of their own?"

"No! No—!"

Liu Fugui could no longer hold on; his psychological defenses had completely collapsed.

However, the final straw that broke him came from his own camp.

The bribed boatmen, seeing that the situation was lost and that Liu Fugui could not save himself, cared nothing for underworld loyalty if it meant a lighter sentence!

With a "thud," the men knelt in unison, kowtowing frantically toward Zhang Dechang.

"My Lord, spare us! My Lord, have mercy!"

The lead boatman cried, tears and snot streaming down his face: "We were forced into this!"

"It was Steward Liu of the Liu family! He gave us a large sum of money and told us to take advantage of the dark, rainy night to sneak these bags onto the Jin family’s ship!"

"He gave us the bags too! He said he would ensure we never had to worry about food or clothing for the rest of our lives if we succeeded! We were just momentarily foolish, My Lord!"

All the evidence formed a perfect closed loop at this moment, and all fingers pointed to the same person.

*Clang!*

Liu Fugui’s legs gave way, his obese body collapsing like mud, his face ashen.

In the corner, Xun An, long forgotten by the crowd, watched this shocking reversal. His body trembled like chaff, and his eyes held only endless fear and despair.

***

**

chapters.title: Abandoning the Pawn to Save the Knight, Victory Under the Rain of Money
chapters.content:
The evidence was as solid as a mountain, and the witnesses had defected.

The entire courtroom was deathly silent.

All eyes converged on the high bench, on Zhang Dechang, the Prefect of Jinling, who held the gavel but could not bring it down.

Fine cold sweat seeped from his temples, and his official robes were soaked through at the back.

Protect Liu Fugui?

He glanced at the crowd outside the court, who were seething with righteous indignation, looking as if they wanted to rush in and tear Liu Fugui apart. His heart trembled.

Public opinion is like water; it can carry a boat, but it can also capsize it.

If he forcibly protected the Liu family today, his official hat as Prefect would likely be overturned by this tidal wave of public outrage tomorrow!

He looked at the slumped, mud-like Liu Fugui—stupid as a pig, failing at everything he touched!

Finally, his gaze fell on Xun An, who was in a state of despair in the corner.

He must have been blind to have believed such a hypocritical, sanctimonious man!

One thought after another flashed through his mind, and Zhang Dechang’s pale, strained face finally hardened into a look of ruthless determination.

*Abandon the pawn to save the knight!*

At this point, it was the only way!

*Bang—!*

With a thunderous sound, he slammed the gavel onto the desk with such force that the teacup jumped.

"Audacious Liu Fugui!"

Zhang Dechang’s voice was booming, filled with righteous fury, as if he had been a clear-eyed, impartial judge from the very beginning.

"You dared to collude with boatmen to forge evidence and frame the Jin trading firm!"

"Disregarding the law, framing the loyal and righteous—your crimes are heinous!"

He rebuked them with stern, thunderous words, distancing himself completely from the matter.

Liu Fugui suddenly lifted his head, his face filled with disbelief.

He opened his mouth, wanting to say something, but only a desperate, rattling sound emerged.

Zhang Dechang gave him no chance to speak, delivering the verdict like a barrage of cannon fire.

"This official hereby pronounces judgment!"

"The Liu Family Trading Firm shall immediately compensate the Jin Family Trading Firm for all losses incurred due to this case, including but not limited to cargo delays and damage to business reputation, totaling a tenfold fine!"

"The principal offender, Liu Fugui, is to be imprisoned and await further sentencing!"

"The accomplices, several boatmen, are to receive twenty strokes of the cane and be exiled to the frontier as a warning to others!"

Once the verdict was delivered, the entire courtroom erupted in an uproar!

A tenfold fine!

That was practically the death knell for the Liu Family Trading Firm!

Everything went black before Liu Fugui’s eyes, and he fainted dead away.

The bailiffs immediately stepped forward and dragged him out like a dead dog.

As for Xun An, he was so terrified by this display of thunderous authority that he shuddered, and the stench of urine began to emanate from beneath him.

He was finished...

Zhang Dechang’s gaze finally landed on him, filled with undisguised disgust and contempt.

"As for you, Xun An!"

"As a scholar, you do not contemplate the ways of the sages, but instead willingly act as a lackey for merchants, twisting black and white and providing false testimony!"

"Although you did not directly participate in the framing, your character is corrupt, and you are unworthy of your position!"

"Guards!"

Zhang Dechang shouted sternly: "Expel this degenerate from the courtroom! I shall immediately draft a letter to the Ministry of Rites to have his scholar status revoked!"

Revoke his status!

These four words were more painful to Xun An than death itself!

Everything he took pride in, the haughtiness he relied upon to survive, was crushed to dust in this moment.

"No... My Lord... I... I was deceived..."

Xun An finally found his voice, crawling and scrambling as he tried to beg for mercy.

However, the bailiffs' staves had already fallen; without giving him any chance to argue, they dragged him out in a wretched state.

An earth-shattering frame-up case had been settled in a way no one had expected.

Jin Yu supported Chen Yinyu as they walked slowly out of the courtroom. The blinding sunlight poured down, dispelling the chill inside the yamen.

"We won! The Jin family won!"

"Miss Jin is mighty! The son-in-law, Chen, is a god-like man!"

Outside the yamen, the commoners who had been waiting for a long time erupted into thunderous cheers.

They had witnessed a spectacular, earth-shattering reversal and seen how justice had triumphed over a despicable conspiracy.

Jin Yu stood on the high steps, looking at the simple, excited faces below, and the pent-up frustration in her heart vanished.

She glanced back at the man beside her.

Chen Yinyu’s face was still as pale as paper, beads of cold sweat on his forehead, his lips so faint they were nearly transparent; he looked as if a gust of wind could blow him over.

Yet he stood straight, his beautiful peach-blossom eyes shining brilliantly in the sunlight, looking at her with a smile.

This battle had been won beautifully, and he was the greatest contributor.

Jin Yu’s heart was filled with an indescribable emotion—sour, soft, and tinged with a hint of pride.

She suddenly let go of the hand supporting him and turned to shout to Wang Quan behind her: "Steward Wang!"

"I am here, Miss!"

"Bring a chest of money." Jin Yu’s voice was clear and commanding, carrying across the entire street corner.

Wang Quan was stunned, but he reacted immediately and sprinted back to the shop across the street.

Soon, several clerks came running over, panting as they carried a heavy camphor wood chest.

The lid was opened, revealing a chest full of copper coins, shimmering with an alluring luster in the sunlight.

The commoners were stunned, not knowing what the eldest miss of the Jin family was planning to do.

Jin Yu stepped forward, grabbed a handful of copper coins herself, and with a sweep of her arm, a brilliant "rain of money" began to fall from the sky.

*Clatter, clatter—*

The coins hit the bluestone pavement, making a crisp, pleasant sound.

"For today’s events, many thanks to all the fellow townsfolk for speaking up for justice!"

Jin Yu’s voice was filled with laughter, ringing out to the heavens. "This is just a small token of my appreciation! Consider it my treat for everyone to have some tea!"

"Reward them!"

Following her order, the clerks tossed the entire chest of copper coins into the crowd.

The crowd instantly boiled over!

"Long live Miss Jin!"

"No! She is Jin the Upright!"

"Jin the Upright is here; I kowtow to you!"

The commoners cheered and scrambled; the entire long street turned into an ocean of joy.

They weren't just scrambling for money; they were scrambling for the joy of vindication and admiration for the Jin family's generosity!

Jin Yu stood on the steps, the sunlight gilding her edges. With a confident and flamboyant smile on her bright, beautiful face, she looked like a radiant Goddess of Wealth.

Chen Yinyu stood quietly behind her, watching her high-spirited appearance, a satisfied and doting smile tugging at his pale lips.

Deep in the shadows of the courtroom, Prefect Zhang Dechang squinted as he watched the bustling scene outside.

Buying people's hearts—what a grand gesture.

His gaze finally settled on the slender figure beside Jin Yu.

That man appeared frail, yet he possessed eyes that could see through everything and a mind more intricate than a nine-curved labyrinth.

"My Lord, this..." the secretary approached, still feeling a lingering fear.

Zhang Dechang’s eyes were terrifyingly sinister, and he slowly spat out a sentence.

"This son-in-law cannot be kept; he is too uncanny."

...

The carriage returning to the manor isolated them from all the noise of the outside world.

The radiant eldest miss of the Jin family was now knitting her brows tightly, carefully rolling up Chen Yinyu’s sleeves.

On his originally fair arms, hideous bloody scratches crisscrossed, caused by the splinters of the wooden boards.

Some wounds were still oozing blood, looking shocking to the eye.

Jin Yu’s heart felt as if it had been pricked by a needle—pained and angry.

"Does it hurt?" She took out the medicine she carried with her, dipped her fingertips into it, and gently applied it to his wounds.

Her movements were as gentle as if she were handling a priceless treasure.

"It hurts."

Chen Yinyu leaned against the soft brocade cushions, his whole being exuding a fragile vulnerability.

He lowered his eyes slightly, his long lashes casting shadows on his eyelids, his voice soft and light.

"If my wife blows on it, it won't hurt anymore."

Jin Yu’s cheeks grew hot, and she glared at him, but her movements became even gentler.

The guy was hurt this badly, yet he still didn't forget to flirt with her.

As she applied the medicine, she asked huffily: "When did you learn the Su embroidery technique? How come I didn't know?"

Chen Yinyu let out a low laugh, leaning weakly against her shoulder, entrusting most of his weight to her.

"To win my wife's favor, I naturally have to learn more about the things my wife likes."

His breath brushed against her neck, carrying a warm, ticklish sensation.

Jin Yu’s heart skipped a beat, but she didn't let him off the hook: "Smooth-tongued."

The carriage fell silent, with only the slight swaying sound of the carriage in motion.

Chen Yinyu leaned on her shoulder, eyes closed, appearing exhausted.

After a long while, he spoke softly, his voice carrying a trace of imperceptible seriousness.

"Wife."

"Hmm?"

"The Prefect sentenced the Liu family to tenfold compensation."

His voice was very light, as if he were talking in his sleep. "Is this money enough... to buy me for a lifetime?"
