Jin Yu’s hand, applying the medicine, paused. She turned her head, seeing only his beautifully defined jawline and his slightly bobbing Adam's apple.

Was this guy settling accounts with her?

Using an earth-shattering victory to trade for a lifetime promise?

Jin Yu’s heart felt as if it had been heavily struck by something.

She didn't answer his question, but instead took the compensation verdict stamped with the official seal from her sleeve.

She looked at the massive amount written on it, her red lips curling into a cold arc.

"Compensation?"

Her voice carried a chilling sneer. "Is that enough?"

Chen Yinyu slowly opened his eyes and looked at her.

He saw that Jin Yu’s eyes were burning with unprecedented ambition and murderous intent. "What I want is for the Liu family to completely disappear from Jinling City."

She didn't just want compensation; she wanted annexation! She wanted to wipe them out!

Chen Yinyu looked at the cold light flashing in her eyes; far from being afraid, he found her breathtakingly beautiful in this moment.

Although he was exhausted to the extreme, too lazy to even move a fingertip, a light identical to hers flashed in his dark pupils.

"My wife is right."

"Then we... must put on a good show."

chapters.title: The Liu Family’s Chaos, The Art of Profiteering from Misfortune
chapters.content:
When the carriage returned to the Jin manor, the entire residence was in a state of jubilation.

The servants ran to tell each other the news, their faces beaming with vindication, looking at Jin Yu as if they were gazing upon a deity.

And when their eyes swept over Chen Yinyu, who was being personally supported by Jin Yu as he stepped out of the carriage, their expressions became even more complex.

Before, it was contempt; later, it was awe; now, it carried a trace of heartfelt fanaticism.

The son-in-law is truly a god-like man!

Wang Quan came trotting up to greet them, his face blooming like a chrysanthemum: "Eldest Miss, you're back! The Prefect’s yamen sent over the verdict documents!"

Jin Yu helped Chen Yinyu sit down on a sandalwood chair cushioned with thick pads before taking the tea Wang Quan handed her, giving a faint "Hmm."

"What is the situation with the Liu family now?" she asked casually.

"It’s a complete mess!" Wang Quan’s tone was full of schadenfreude.

"Liu Fugui was beaten and thrown straight into the dungeon; they say it's uncertain if he'll even live until the autumn executions. With that tenfold fine, all the Liu family's liquid assets became empty shells overnight! Now that the wall is collapsing, everyone is pushing it; those who used to suck up to them are all showing up to demand their debts!"

Wang Quan paused, lowering his voice with a hint of contempt.

"The one in charge of the Liu family now is that Xun An."

"Him?" Jin Yu raised an eyebrow, a mocking sneer curling her lips. "What does he know about business?"

"Of course he doesn't know!"

Wang Quan slapped his thigh. "He’s like a headless fly right now. I heard that for the past two days, he’s been selling off family property, trying to scrape together money to pull strings and get Liu Fugui out."

Jin Yu’s gaze flickered slightly.

Sure enough, Wang Quan continued: "I just received news that Xun An has already spread the word that in three days, he will publicly auction off the five most valuable shops under the Liu family name at Jinling's largest 'Four Seas Auction House'!"

"Those five shops are all located on Zhuque Street, the most prosperous area in our Jinling City. Two of them are directly opposite our 'Jinxiu Pavilion.' The location is absolutely prime!"

Jin Yu paced slowly to the window, looking at the century-old osmanthus tree in the courtyard, its branches lush and full. In her mind, the commercial map of Jinling City had already taken shape.

Those five shops were like five nails, perfectly positioned to wedge into the gaps of the Jin family's commercial territory, linking their influence in Jinling into one cohesive whole.

She wanted them, and she was determined to have them.

"The starting price Xun An has set is not low," Wang Quan added with some concern. "He is likely a cornered dog, trying to make a killing while the location is still desirable. I heard that many wealthy merchants from other regions have received the news and are already rushing to Jinling."

Jin Yu sneered: "I never stop those who want to be suckers."

She turned around and looked at the man who was resting with his eyes closed.

Chen Yinyu had recovered somewhat by now and was leisurely peeling a crystal-clear purple jade grape.

His fingers were slender and fair, his movements elegant, as if he were not peeling a grape, but sculpting a work of art.

Once peeled, he removed the seeds, leaving only the sweetest, most tender flesh, and held the grape to Jin Yu's lips.

Jin Yu naturally opened her mouth to take it, the sweetness filling her palate.

"My lady," Chen Yinyu finally spoke, his voice still carrying a hint of the hoarseness of illness, yet every word was clear. "These shops must be bought, but they must be bought at our price."

He smiled slightly, like ice melting at the first touch of spring.

"Not only must we buy the shops, but I also want you, my lady, to pocket the 'foundation' the Liu family has accumulated over the years."

"'Foundation'?" Jin Yu chewed on the word.

"The Liu family's shopkeepers, clerks, procurement channels, shipping partnerships, and even the skilled embroiderers and dyers in their back courtyard," Chen Yinyu explained softly. "These are the roots of the Liu family's long-standing dominance in Jinling. Shops can be rebuilt if lost, but if the people are gone, that is the true way to pull the firewood from under the cauldron."

Jin Yu's eyes lit up instantly.

She had only thought of annexing assets, while Chen Yinyu was thinking of uprooting the entire tree and turning everything the opponent had into his own!

This method of killing the person and then destroying their spirit was simply... too much to her liking!

"What do you want to do?" Jin Yu pressed.

Chen Yinyu only gave a mysterious smile and beckoned to Wang Quan, who was waiting outside the door.

Wang Quan immediately leaned in.

Chen Yinyu leaned to his ear and whispered instructions in a voice only the two of them could hear.

At first, Wang Quan was confused, but as Chen Yinyu spoke, his eyes grew wider and wider. The expression on his face shifted from bewilderment to shock, finally settling into an irrepressible, extremely "insidious" smirk.

"Understood, Young Master!" Wang Quan slapped his chest and left to carry out the orders.

Meanwhile, at the Liu residence.

Xun An was sitting in the empty accounting room, worrying over a pile of deficit-ridden ledgers.

Prefect Zhang Dechang had already sent word that there was no room for negotiation regarding the stripping of his scholarly status; he was now a commoner.

His only hope was the auction three days later.

"Keep a close watch for me!"

His eyes bloodshot, he said viciously to the servants in front of him, "Especially the Jin family! On the day of the auction, if anyone from the Jin family dares to cause trouble, beat them out for me!"

He was fully convinced that Jin Yu would use commercial tactics to suppress the price, and he had made thorough preparations, even sparing no expense to hire shills to drive the price up.

However, he did not know that an invisible net had already quietly descended over the Liu family.

The next day, strange rumors began to circulate in the teahouses and taverns of Jinling City.

"Have you heard? The feng shui of those Liu family shops on Zhuque Street is bad!" A storyteller lowered his voice, acting mysterious.

"How so?"

"That area used to be a mass grave! I heard that back then, to occupy that land, the Liu family leveled people's graves! At night, people always hear crying coming from the shops!"

"That's not all! I also heard that Liu Fugui's downfall this time is because the evil energy is too heavy, clashing with the family head's fortune! Whoever takes over will be cursed with bad luck!"

The rumors grew wings, spreading through every street and alley of Jinling overnight.

Those wealthy merchants from out of town who had originally set their sights on the location started to have second thoughts.

Businessmen, above all, believe in these things.

Listening to Wang Quan's report, Jin Yu laughed until she shook.

She looked at the instigator in the study who was reading leisurely. Chen Yinyu noticed her gaze, looked up from behind the scroll, and gave her an extremely innocent smile.

He shook a small porcelain bottle by his hand.

Jin Yu took it curiously, opened it, and sniffed. A faint scent, similar to a mixture of sulfur and phosphorus powder, wafted out.

"This is?"

"Just some 'props' to liven things up," Chen Yinyu slowly closed his book, stood up, and walked to her side.

"My lady, tomorrow is a good day."

"We must go and 'help' Brother Xun An; we cannot let his auction... fall flat."

chapters.title: The Offensive of Rumors, the Feng Shui Master Shows His Power
chapters.content:
On the day of the auction.

Zhuque Street, the most prosperous street in Jinling City, was permeated with an eerie atmosphere.

At a time when it should have been bustling with traffic and noise, the five shops with vermilion lacquer and gold plaques belonging to the Liu family were surrounded by layers of people. They stretched their necks to look, yet kept their mouths tightly shut, as if afraid of disturbing something.

In the center of the crowd, an incense table had been set up.

Incense candles flickered on the table, blue smoke curled, and mixed with the charred smell of burning spirit money, emitting an ominous aura.

Three "masters" dressed in black Taoist robes were performing rituals around the incense table.

The one on the left held a compass, the needle spinning wildly, muttering: "...The dragon and tiger are at war, the white tiger raises its head; this is a sign of great misfortune, great misfortune indeed!"

The one on the right shook a copper bell, the sound shrill and piercing, as if it could penetrate the eardrums and stab directly into the soul: "The vengeful spirits will not disperse, the evil energy is entrenched; the living must not approach, for to approach is to die!"

The leader, with white hair and beard, looking every bit the immortal, held a peach-wood sword, stepping in ritual patterns, sighing toward the sky with tears in his eyes.

"Woe! Woe! This place was once a mass grave. The Liu family forcibly occupied the earth's veins, disturbing the dead, leading to the family head's imprisonment—this is heaven's retribution!"

He suddenly pointed the peach-wood sword at the shop door, his voice shaking the surroundings: "Now the evil energy has formed, the resentment is sky-high! This shop is no longer a dwelling for the living, but a 'White Tiger Curse' that devours human flesh and blood! Whoever buys it! Whoever lives in it! Whoever touches it! Will surely see their family destroyed and their lineage cut off!"

Every word was like a heavy hammer, smashing into the hearts of the onlookers.

Among the crowd, several wealthy merchants from other regions, dressed in finery and speaking with different accents, saw their complexions turn from curiosity to deathly pale.

They had heard the news released by Xun An and, seeing the prime location, had traveled thousands of miles to Jinling, prepared to spend a fortune at the auction.

But in business, the most important thing is auspiciousness!

Before they had even bought anything, a "procession of a hundred ghosts" was being performed at the doorstep. Who could stand that?

"Bad luck, truly bad luck!"

A fat merchant shook his head repeatedly and spat on the ground, "I wouldn't take these shops even if they were given to me for free!"

"Exactly, there's no point in risking one's life for this bit of business!"

"I don't think we need to go to this auction either, lest we get tainted with bad luck!"

The merchants discussed among themselves, looking at the five shops not as a piece of fat meat, but as a trap coated in deadly poison.

"Get out of here! A bunch of charlatans playing at gods and ghosts!"

A roar of exasperated fury exploded. Xun An pushed through the crowd, his face livid as he rushed out.

He had specially changed into a brand-new sky-blue scholar's robe today, attempting to keep up appearances, but his face was twisted with rage, looking even uglier than the evil ghosts the "masters" spoke of.

"They were sent by the Jin family! That poisonous woman Jin Yu sent them to cause trouble!"

Xun An pointed at the three "masters," his fingers trembling, "Don't believe them! This is all a conspiracy by the Jin family! They want to use these low-life tactics to drive down the price!"

He argued desperately, trying to awaken the crowd's reason.

However, before he could finish, the white-haired "master" leading them suddenly stopped his ritual.

He turned slowly, his cloudy old eyes fixed on Xun An, as if he could see through his very organs.

The "master" did not speak, but circled Xun An twice, shaking his head and sighing as he did so, his compassionate expression suggesting he had seen some unparalleled tragedy.

Xun An felt his skin crawl under the gaze and shouted sharply: "What are you looking at! If you don't leave, I'll report you to the authorities!"

"Sigh..."

The "master" sighed leisurely. He reached out a withered finger and pointed it directly at the center of Xun An's forehead.

"Young man, I see that your brow is darkened, black clouds hang over your head, and the aura of death is entwined between your eyebrows. This is... a sign of impending disaster!"

Xun An shuddered.

The "master's" voice grew even more mournful: "You once had scholarly status, but were stripped of it due to your crooked heart; you once had a great marriage, but were abandoned because you thought too highly of yourself!"

"Now you are aiding the tyrant, tainted by the overwhelming evil energy of this 'White Tiger Curse.' I predict that within three days, you will face imprisonment! At best, you will be exiled a thousand miles; at worst... your head will fall to the ground!"

These words were like claps of thunder, exploding in Xun An's mind!

Stripped of scholarly status! Abandoned!

Weren't these the most painful scars in his heart? How could this charlatan know?

The onlookers, however, were in an uproar!

"My god! That was too accurate!"

"I heard that this Young Master Xun was indeed a scholar and once had an engagement with the eldest lady of the Jin family!"

"Later, he was stripped of his status in court by the Prefect. The whole of Jinling City knows about that!"

"Miraculous! This master is truly a divine calculator!"

The crowd's discussion reached Xun An's ears. Looking at their expressions of both sympathy and contempt, he felt the world spinning, and a taste of blood surged into his throat.

"You... you are spouting nonsense!"

Xun An was trembling with rage. He pointed at the "master" wanting to curse, but he couldn't catch his breath. His whole body jerked backward, and he began to cough violently.

This appearance, in the eyes of the crowd, only served to confirm the "Master's" words—look, wasn't he just struck by his own guilty conscience, so enraged that he lost his composure?

The few wealthy merchants from out of town were so frightened that they retreated repeatedly, and without another word, turned and left.

This spectacle was not worth watching! And these shops were even less worth buying!

Whoever touched them would be doomed; this Young Master Xun was a living example!

Across from Suzaku Street, in a private room on the second floor of the "Zuixian Restaurant," by the railing.

Jin Yu leisurely picked up a Ru-ware sky-blue glazed teacup and took a light sip of the premium Biluochun tea. With the corner of her eye, she glanced at the farce downstairs, a look of comfortable amusement playing on her lips.

What a fine play of "Charlatan vs. Pedantic Scholar"—it truly made for a good appetite.

Beside her, Chen Yinyu kept his eyes lowered, his slender, fair fingers holding a small silver knife, focused on peeling a pear.

It was as if the farce downstairs, capable of stirring up the business world of Jinling, was to him merely a scene outside the window, far less important than the pear in his hand.

"The 'Masters' you invited are truly talented," Jin Yu chuckled. "It’s a pity they don't sing in the Pear Garden."

"You flatter me, my lady," Chen Yinyu said, cutting the peeled pear into small pieces. He speared one with a silver pick and held it to Jin Yu’s lips. "They are but minor tricks not fit for the main stage. If they can provide you with some amusement, then it is not a waste."

Jin Yu took the fruit into her mouth, the clear, sweet juice bursting forth, making her mood even more pleasant.

"This alone is not enough."

She watched the distraught figure of Xun An downstairs, her gaze turning cold. "Some people, if you don't push them to the edge, they will never give up."

Chen Yinyu smiled slightly, as if he had long expected her to say this.

He gave a subtle gesture to Wang Quan, who was standing guard outside the window. Wang Quan understood immediately, turned, and headed downstairs, blending into the crowd.

Before long, a new rumor began to spread quietly among the hesitant merchants.

"Hey, have you heard? The Jin family has sent word!"

"What did they say?"

"They say the Jin family has been paying court fines for their recent lawsuit, and their liquid cash is tight. They have absolutely no interest in these ill-omened shops of the Liu family!"

"What? The Jin family isn't buying?"

"Exactly! The eldest miss of the Jin family is such a shrewd person; if even she won't touch this mess, would we outsiders be fools to rush in and pick up the pieces?"

Once these words were out, the last shred of hope held by those merchants—who were still harboring thoughts of "seeking wealth in danger" and waiting to pick up bargains after the Jin family made their move—was completely extinguished.

If even the local snake, the Jin family, found these bones unpalatable, why should they, as visiting dragons, try to gnaw on them?

In an instant, the atmosphere of the entire auction plummeted to freezing point before it had even begun.

The "rare commodity" scene that Xun An had painstakingly crafted was shattered by the combination of Chen Yinyu's feints and strikes.

Jin Yu watched the crowd downstairs gradually disperse, leaving only Xun An’s lonely, swaying figure in the wind.

She set down her teacup, which made a crisp, light sound.

"The time is about right."

She rose slowly and smoothed the wide-sleeved silk robe embroidered with gold-threaded butterflies and floral cloud patterns.

"Let’s go, husband."

"It’s time to collect our spoils."

chapters.title: The Auction Site, A Double Act of Violent Debt Collection
chapters.content:
Chen Yinyu set down the silver pick, wiped his fingers carefully with a silk handkerchief, and then placed his slightly cool hand into Jin Yu’s warm palm.

He stood up obediently, his gaze lowered. "I listen to you, my lady."

The two walked out of the private room side by side. Wang Quan was already waiting downstairs, bowing in salute, his eyes filled with undisguised excitement and admiration.

The eldest miss's methods were as crisp and decisive as ever, and the young master's schemes were even more unfathomable, killing without drawing blood.

These two were truly a match made in heaven—a pair of banes!

Outside the Zuixian Restaurant, the crowd that had been packed tight moments ago had mostly dispersed.

The "Masters" who had been playing their charades were nowhere to be found, leaving behind only a mess of scattered spirit money and burnt incense ash.

Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu walked slowly toward the Liu family’s trading house opposite. The closer they got, the more intense the scent of decay became.

The vermilion gates of the trading house were left ajar, and someone had splashed thick ink across them, forming crooked characters: "Repay your debts."

On the threshold, a broken piece of the plaque lay alone, the characters "Liu Family" trampled into an unrecognizable blur.

However, when Jin Yu stepped into the trading house, she found it was not entirely empty.

In the vast hall, two or three merchants were still sitting scattered about.

They were dressed in fine attire, but their expressions were extremely tense, as if they were sitting on pins and needles, their eyes darting toward the door, looking ready to flee at any moment.

On the high platform, Xun An’s face was deathly pale, fine beads of cold sweat trickling down his temples, yet he still struggled to maintain the facade, attempting to continue this auction that had long since lost all meaning.

"Everyone, everyone, please be quiet!"

His voice was hoarse and dry, revealing a desperate madness.

"What happened just now was merely the Jin family using underhanded tactics to intentionally disrupt the proceedings! You are all discerning people; do not be deceived by such villains!"

"You all know the value of the location of these five shops! If you miss out today, you will surely regret it for the rest of your days!"

He was practically begging; the noble spirit of a scholar had been ground into dust by reality, leaving not even a scrap behind.

The merchants below looked at each other. One of them, slightly bolder, hesitated and raised his hand, seemingly wanting to wait and see.

A glimmer of hope ignited in Xun An’s eyes, and he was about to shout.

"BANG—!"

The already shaky doors of the trading house were kicked open from the outside!

Amidst flying wood splinters, a dozen burly men holding clubs and looking fierce charged in.

Leading them was none other than Wang Quan, who had changed into coarse linen clothes and had soot from a pot smeared across his face!

Behind him were a few agile guards from the Jin family, but more were the genuine beggars and thugs Wang Quan had hired from the dilapidated temple south of the city.

As soon as they rushed in, without a word, they raised their clubs and began smashing the tables and chairs in the hall!

"The Liu family refuses to pay their debts; it is intolerable!"

"Pay up! Pay up now!"

"Smash it! Smash this place to pay off the debt!"

The shouting was deafening, mixed with the "crack" of splintering wood and the "clatter" of porcelain hitting the floor. The entire hall instantly turned into a living hell.

The merchants, already terrified, had never seen such a scene!

The "creditors" brought by Wang Quan were very measured; the clubs never touched the people, but were aimed specifically at their feet.

A mahogany table was smashed to pieces in front of a fat merchant, the flying splinters tearing his robes.

A pot of boiling hot tea was "accidentally" knocked over, scalding the new official boots of another merchant.

"Ouch!"

"Murder! They're trying to kill us!"

The merchants were scared out of their wits, scrambling toward the door, no longer daring to think about buying shops.

In the blink of an eye, the hall was left in total disarray.

Xun An stood frozen on the high platform, watching helplessly as the last sparks of hope were completely extinguished by this group of thugs who had suddenly broken in.

He trembled all over, pointing at Wang Quan and the others, his lips quivering, but he couldn't utter a single word.

"Stop them! Servants! Where the hell are the servants?!"

He screamed at the top of his lungs.

A few Liu family servants rushed up timidly, but before they could get close, they were kicked to the ground by Wang Quan, wailing and crying for their parents.

These servants, who usually threw their weight around, were nothing but cowards in the face of real desperadoes.

In the chaos, no one noticed.

Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu were standing at the door, watching the play unfold with composure.

Jin Yu didn't speak; she just watched quietly as Xun An went from feigning calm to blustering, and finally to complete despair.

He collapsed on the platform, his eyes vacant, his face ashen.

All his calculations, all his struggles, had turned into bubbles at this moment.

The "creditors" causing the trouble gradually stopped their actions, but they still surrounded Xun An, eyeing him like tigers.

Wang Quan wiped the "soot" from his face and spat viciously.

"Xun, if you don't come up with the money today, don't think about walking out of this door!"

"That's right! Don't think about leaving!"

"Where is the money from selling the shops? Hand it over to pay the debt!"

Each demand was like a heavy hammer blow, striking Xun An’s collapsing nerves.

Just then, a crisp female voice, like jade striking jade, rang out leisurely.

"Oh my, what is happening here?"

Jin Yu walked into the hall, leaning on Chen Yinyu’s arm. She looked around, her delicate brows slightly furrowed, her face showing just the right amount of surprise and pity.

"Young Master Xun, why must it come to this?"

Xun An looked up abruptly. When he saw Jin Yu’s bright and beautiful face, a towering hatred ignited in his eyes.

"Jin Yu! It’s you! You designed all of this!"

Jin Yu seemed not to hear his accusation, only sighing softly, her tone filled with compassion.

"I was just passing by and wanted to see the excitement of the auction. Who would have thought..."

She shook her head, her gaze sweeping over the fierce "creditors" and finally landing on Xun An’s pale face.

"Forget it. For the sake of our acquaintance, if no one else wants these shops, I will reluctantly take them."

"Consider it an act of charity to help you pay off these debts."

"You..." Xun An was so angry that a mouthful of blood stuck in his throat.

An act of charity?

This was clearly robbery in the midst of a fire! This was kicking a man when he was down!

Chen Yinyu coughed lightly at her side, leaning weakly on Jin Yu’s shoulder, and whispered, "My lady is kind-hearted, but... for such a mess, it’s not worth dirtying your hands."

This back-and-forth completely trampled Xun An’s dignity into the dirt.

Wang Quan spat at the right moment and clamored, "Enough nonsense! Eldest Miss Jin, don't play the saint! These shops must be sold today to pay the debt! Whoever pays the money, they belong to!"

Jin Yu seemed moved by these words. She pondered for a moment and held up three slender fingers.

"In that case, I will make an offer."

Her voice was not loud, but it reached the ears of everyone present clearly. "Thirty thousand taels. For these five shops and everything inside, I offer thirty thousand taels of silver."

Thirty thousand taels!

Xun An’s eyes turned red in an instant!

The market value of the land deeds for these five shops alone was no less than one hundred thousand taels! Not to mention the high-quality shelving and furnishings inside!

Jin Yu’s price was not even thirty percent of the market value!

This was no longer price-gouging; this was cutting his flesh with a knife and drinking his blood!

He glared at Jin Yu, his teeth grinding together with a rattling sound, and squeezed a few words through his clenched teeth.

"You... are... dreaming!"

Upon hearing this, Jin Yu was not angry; instead, she smiled.

She withdrew her hand, shook her head with a look of regret, and turned to leave.

"Since Young Master Xun feels it isn't worth it, then so be it. Husband, let’s go; let’s not delay our return for dinner."

"Alright." Chen Yinyu nodded submissively and, supporting her, prepared to leave.

"Stop!"

Xun An looked at Jin Yu’s resolute back, then at the "creditors" surrounding him like wolves and tigers. A cold despair instantly drowned his last shred of reason.

He knew that if Jin Yu left today, not only would he not get a single cent, but he might actually be beaten to death here by this group of people.

His pride and his self-esteem were crushed to dust in the face of the instinct to survive.

Cold sweat slid down his temple and dripped into his eyes, stinging and painful.

He opened his mouth, but those two words felt as heavy as a thousand catties, exhausting every ounce of his strength.

chapters.title: Humiliating Contract, A Trap in Wordplay
chapters.content:
"...Fine."

Once the word was out, Xun An’s body swayed as if about to collapse; that "stop" had drained his final strength and dignity.

He stared fixedly at Jin Yu’s back, the luxurious cloud brocade stinging his eyes.

Jin Yu turned slowly, the look of regret on her face long gone, replaced by the scrutiny unique to a merchant.

"Has Young Master Xun thought it through?" she asked.

Xun An’s lips trembled. He wanted to say a few more face-saving words, wanted to curse her for being despicable and shameless, but facing Wang Quan and the fierce "creditors" behind him, all his words were stuck in his throat, turning into a humiliating silence.

He knew he had no choice.

Jin Yu’s gaze passed over him and swept across the chaotic hall, as if evaluating the residual value of a piece of cargo.

"Thirty thousand taels to buy these five shops, as well as all assets under the Liu family name. Money and goods cleared."

"You!" Xun An snapped his head up. This was different from what was just said! A moment ago, it was only the five shops!

"What?"

Jin Yu raised an eyebrow. "Does Young Master Xun think the Liu family only has these five shops of value? The detained goods, the outstanding debts, the bribes paid to officials—which of these doesn't require money?"

"My thirty thousand taels is to buy this mess for you, to let you escape from here. Otherwise..."

She didn't continue, but her gaze flicked toward the strong men holding clubs, the threat implied.

Xun An felt as if he had fallen into an ice cellar.

He understood now: Jin Yu didn't want just these few shops; she wanted the entire Liu family business. She wanted to pull the firewood from under the cauldron and root them out completely!

And he was merely the tool she used to pry open the rotten walnut that was the Liu family, to be discarded once used.

"Fine..." Xun An spoke again. This time, even the trace of unwilling hoarseness had vanished, leaving only a stagnant, numb silence. "I... I will sell."

A faint, imperceptible arc curled the corner of Jin Yu’s mouth before it vanished.

She gave Wang Quan a look.

Wang Quan understood immediately. He dragged a relatively intact low square table from the ruins and found two wobbly chairs from the corner, placing them heavily in the center of the hall.

"Bring the brush and ink!" Jin Yu said softly.

Immediately, a Jin family guard sprinted out, returning a moment later with a set of high-quality scholar's four treasures, which he respectfully spread out on the table.

The delicate rice paper and the lustrous Hui ink formed an ironic contrast with the broken walls and ruins surrounding them.

Jin Yu did not sit; she stood by the table and said softly to Chen Yinyu, "Husband, I must trouble you."

At this moment, everyone’s eyes were focused on Chen Yinyu.

He walked quietly to the table, rolled up his wide sleeves, and revealed a slender, fair wrist.

He picked up the purple-hair brush, dipped it fully in ink, and with his wrist suspended, the tip of the brush touched the paper.

The hall was deathly quiet, save for the "rustling" of the brush tip across the paper.

The sound was faint, yet like a small knife, slicing away at Xun An’s nerves one stroke at a time.

He stared fixedly at the thick stacks of silver notes on the table—those Jin Yu had prepared in advance, gleaming with an alluring luster.

They were his life-saving money, and also his blood money.

He couldn't understand what Chen Yinyu had written. He recognized the characters, but combined, they were as obscure as a heavenly book.

He only felt dizzy, his heart filled with the desire to end this public execution quickly.

Hurry!

Hurry and sign, press his thumbprint, take the money, and roll out of this place where he had lost all face!

Finally, Chen Yinyu stopped writing.

He placed the brush gently on the brush rest, picked up the contract filled with dense, small characters, brought it close to his lips, and blew gently on the wet ink.

His posture was elegant and composed, like an artist who had just finished a masterpiece.

"It is done, my lady." He handed the contract to Jin Yu, his voice as gentle and soft as before.

Jin Yu took it, not even glancing at it, and slapped the contract directly in front of Xun An.

"Young Master Xun, please take a look."

Xun An had no heart left to look; his eyes were already dazed by the thirty thousand taels of silver.

He scanned it haphazardly, seeing only glaring words like "Thirty thousand taels total" and "Five shopfronts," and grabbed the brush impatiently.

His hand shook violently; he could barely hold the brush.

"...Above this, all shops and auxiliary storage facilities under the Liu family business shall belong to the Jin family..."

He mumbled the words, thinking that terms like "auxiliary storage facilities" were merely the pedantic flourishes of a scholar trying to pad the word count, and he didn't give it a second thought.

Trembling, he used all his strength to write his name at the end of the contract.

The moment he pressed his bright red thumbprint, his entire body collapsed, as if his last bit of spirit had been drained away.

"Done." Jin Yu’s voice was crisp, signaling Wang Quan to push the silver notes over.

Xun An grabbed the silver notes like a drowning man clutching a straw, shoved them haphazardly into his robes, and turned to flee.

He didn't want to see the faces of Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu for one more second!

However, just as he took a step, Chen Yinyu’s unhurried, gentle voice came from behind him.

"Brother Xun, please stay a moment."

Xun An’s footsteps stiffened. With his back to him, he roared impatiently, "The contract is signed, money and goods cleared, what else is there?!"

Chen Yinyu chuckled, the sound ringing clearly in the empty hall.

"Nothing of great importance."

He leisurely took a bunch of messy keys from Jin Yu’s hand—the ones just found in the Liu family’s accounting room.

As he carelessly fiddled with the keys, making a "clinking" sound, he asked as if in passing:

"I just wanted to confirm with Brother Xun: the contract states that all Liu family shops and their 'auxiliary storage facilities' have been transferred."

"I recall... that abandoned warehouse at the charity cemetery next to the southern city graveyard was also a property the Liu family paid to renovate years ago, wasn't it?"

"I suppose that counts as an 'auxiliary facility' of the Liu family. Please hand over the keys to that place as well, Brother Xun."

"Boom—!"

Chen Yinyu’s words were not loud, but to Xun An, they were no less than a thunderbolt from a clear sky!

His body jolted violently, as if struck by lightning, and he turned around slowly.

Southern city... charity cemetery... warehouse!

That place!

That was the secret stronghold where Liu Fugui hid all his smuggled goods and private ledgers! Inside were not only illicit goods but also all the evidence of his years of collusion with officials, framing competitors, and keeping fake accounts!

That was Liu Fugui’s final trump card, and the last escape route Xun An had left for himself!

He had thought that even if the business was gone, as long as he had those ledgers, he could manipulate the officials who had colluded with the Liu family and make a comeback!

But now...

"You... how did you know?!" Xun An’s voice was hoarse and distorted, filled with unbelievable terror.

The smile on Chen Yinyu’s face grew more innocent. He gently shook the contract in his hand.

"I didn't know."

"It’s just written here in black and white: 'auxiliary storage facilities'."

He raised those beautiful peach-blossom eyes, his gaze shifting with a deadly chill.

"Brother Xun is well-read; surely you wouldn't want to say that the charity cemetery warehouse doesn't count as an 'auxiliary storage facility'?"

"Or is it..."

His voice turned cold abruptly.

"Does Brother Xun want to admit, in front of all these 'creditors', that what you just signed was a piece of waste paper, and you intend to... renege on the debt?"

"I..." Xun An opened his mouth, unable to utter a single word.

He looked at Chen Yinyu’s stunning yet incredibly vicious face, then at the strong men around him, who were once again eyeing him like predators.

Reneging?

He had no doubt that if he dared to say "no," he wouldn't walk out of this door in one piece today.

He wanted to go back on his word, to say that it was the Liu family’s private property and not part of this transaction.

But... "auxiliary storage facilities"!

Those words were like a death warrant, a trap already dug, waiting for him to jump in!

He thought he had only sold the empty shell of the business, never imagining that Chen Yinyu had calculated down to his very marrow!

Thirty thousand taels, indeed!

The value of those ledgers was far more than thirty thousand taels! They were earth-shattering secrets capable of shaking the entire capital’s officialdom and business world!

"Thump."

Xun An’s legs went weak, and he collapsed completely onto the floor, covered in dust and wood shavings.

The searingly hot silver notes in his robes now felt colder than ice.

With vacant eyes, he watched Jin Yu support Chen Yinyu, holding the keys that decided his fate, as they walked past him as if stepping over a pile of useless trash.

It was over.

Everything was over.

chapters.title: Changing the Name and Sign, Half the Empire is Yours
chapters.content:
Xun An was dragged out like a pile of mud.

Those thirty thousand taels of silver were his final shred of dignity, and also the nails for his coffin.

Jin Yu stood in the chaotic main hall of the Liu Family Trading House, not a trace of the joy of victory on her face.

She leaned on the arm of Chen Yinyu, who stood beside her, feeling the warmth of his palm, and the lingering hostility that had arisen from rooting out her enemies slowly subsided.

"Are you tired?" she asked.

Chen Yinyu shook his head, his beautiful peach-blossom eyes reflecting her image, a faint smile playing on his lips: "Doing things for my wife is not tiring."

He paused, his voice dropping lower, carrying a hint of playfulness that only Jin Yu could hear: "Besides, filling in the pit someone else dug with my own hands is actually quite interesting."

Jin Yu was amused by his fox-like demeanor and reached out to pinch his cheek: "You are such a rascal."

Wang Quan directed the servants to begin clearing the ruins. He walked up to Jin Yu, bowed, and said, "Miss, everything has been handled properly."

Jin Yu nodded, her gaze sweeping over the devastation, but her tone had already regained the boldness of the richest person in Jinling.

"Uncle Wang, pass on my word: find the best craftsmen in Jinling City and have them work through the night to forge me the largest golden signboard!"

"By tomorrow morning, I want the Liu family to be gone from the most prosperous street in Jinling, replaced only by my Jin family branch!"

Her voice was not loud, but it was firm and resonant, echoing through the empty hall.

**—**

The next day, the sky was bright.

Zhuque Avenue, the most prosperous street in Jinling City, was packed to the point of being impassable.

"Bang!"

One by one, the old plaques inscribed with "Liu Family Trading House" were rudely poked down by long poles, crashing heavily to the ground and breaking in two.

A ripple of murmurs and gasps broke out among the crowd.

Immediately after, amidst the deafening sound of firecrackers, a brand-new plaque was slowly hoisted up by four strong men working in unison.

The plaque was made of precious ebony, and the four large characters "Jin Family Branch" were crafted from pure gold, shimmering with a dazzling, mesmerizing light in the morning sun, almost blinding everyone who looked at it.

"My goodness! A pure gold signboard! Is the Jin family really that rich?"

"Is the Liu family completely finished? Did it change its name to Jin overnight?"

"Don't you know? I heard that yesterday, the Jin family's son-in-law used nothing but his tongue to take over the entire Liu business! That young master Xun An signed the contract in tears!"

Amidst the chatter, a window on the second floor was pushed open.

Jin Yu wore a long dress of cloud brocade patterned with red-gold intertwined flowers and a luxurious gold-woven cape, leaning lazily against the window frame.

She held a white jade teacup in her hand, gently blowing away the swirling steam, looking down at the clamor below and the prosperity of the street like a queen surveying her city.

Chen Yinyu, dressed in a green robe, stood quietly behind her, refilling her tea.

His gaze crossed over Jin Yu's shoulder and caught several familiar faces in the crowd—former classmates who had mocked and ostracized him at the academy were now looking up, their faces filled with shock as they stared at the gleaming golden signboard.

The smile on his lips deepened; this feeling was indeed quite good.

Jin Yu set down her teacup, turned her head, and met his gaze: "What is my husband smiling at?"

Chen Yinyu lowered his eyes, his long lashes concealing the sharp glint in his pupils, his voice soft and gentle: "I was just thinking that my wife looks truly beautiful standing here."

Jin Yu gave a light hum, though her mood was excellent.

She enjoyed this feeling of conquest, whether in the business world or with men.

**—**

In the afternoon, the noise subsided.

Chen Yinyu made an excuse about going to the study to review his books, but in reality, he left the Jin residence alone through the back door, hired an inconspicuous carriage, and headed straight for the south of the city.

The city's southern potter's field was adjacent to a mass grave, desolate and gloomy all year round.

The courtyard used as a warehouse was right next to the potter's field. Withered vines crawled over the dilapidated courtyard walls, the red lacquer on the main gate had long since peeled away, and a rusted copper lock hung on it, as if no one had been there for decades.

Chen Yinyu took out the key he had "requested" from Xun An and tried several times before the lock clicked open.

Pushing open the heavy wooden door, a strange odor mixed with dust, moldy wood, and rotting silk rushed out to meet him.

Sunlight squeezed through the cracks in the door, illuminating the countless dust motes dancing in the air.

The warehouse was filled with all sorts of crates, stacked in a disorderly fashion, many covered only by rough, rain-proof tarpaulins.

This was Liu Fugui's true treasury, and the location of the evidence of his illicit dealings with countless officials.

As for how Chen Yinyu knew about this place, it was thanks to the account book he had risked his life to seize from the cargo ship that day.

Although that account book hadn't been of much use in the magistrate's office, it had recorded other more important things, such as this place.

In other words, even if the lawsuit had failed that day, Chen Yinyu would have exposed the information about this place to bring the Liu family down with him.

Once inside the warehouse, Chen Yinyu did not rush to rummage through the obvious goods, but instead walked around the warehouse, his sharp gaze sweeping over every corner.

His memory was extraordinary; he had long since firmly memorized the Jin family's accounts and the distribution map of the shops in Jinling City.

Liu Fugui smuggled a wide variety of goods, from northern furs to southern spices, but the most profitable were illicit salt and ironware.

These items would never be left casually out in the open.

His gaze finally rested on the deepest part of the warehouse, on a pile of seemingly useless rotten wood and straw.

The dust there showed signs of having been disturbed.

He walked over, moved the rotting wood, and pushed aside the thick straw, revealing a bluestone slab underneath that was a slightly different color from the rest of the floor.

Chen Yinyu squatted down, pried the edge of the slab with his dagger, and gave it a hard heave; a pitch-black hole was suddenly revealed.

Lying quietly beneath the opening was a locked black-lacquered wooden box—this was the real prize.

He pulled the box up. Having no key, he simply used his dagger to pry open the lock.

With a "creak," the lid sprang open.

Inside, there were no gold, silver, jewelry, or land deeds as expected, but only a few thick account books and a letter sealed with wax that had not yet been opened.

Chen Yinyu picked up the account books and flipped through them rapidly.

Every page recorded shocking transactions, followed by names that were like thunder in the ears.

The Magistrate of Jinling, officials from the Provincial Administration Commission... almost the entire Jinling officialdom was involved in dirty dealings with the Liu family.

These account books were enough to cause a massive earthquake in the Jinling officialdom, but his true target was the letter.

He carefully picked up the envelope. It felt very light, as if it contained only a thin sheet of paper.

There was no signature on the envelope, no recipient, only a mark stamped in black wax.

It was not the emblem of any family, nor was it an official seal.

It was a totem.

A small black snake, head to tail, coiled into a circle, its mouth wide open as if to devour its own tail.

Chen Yinyu had seen this totem in a rare, obscure book at the academy; it was the personal seal of the current Grand Preceptor, Pang Wei.

Pang Wei, whose power shook the court, had students and subordinates all over the world; he was the leader of the aristocratic factions in the court and the official the Emperor feared most.

How could Liu Fugui, a mere wealthy merchant, be connected to the Grand Preceptor?

Chen Yinyu's expression instantly became incredibly grave.

He had originally thought this was just a trophy for toppling the Liu family, but he hadn't expected to accidentally hook a giant crocodile capable of overturning the imperial court.

This letter was meant for the capital.

The fact that it hadn't been sent meant that Liu Fugui's downfall had perhaps been faster than anyone imagined—so fast that he hadn't even had time to send this plea for help.

Chen Yinyu's heart beat slightly faster.

He put the account books back into the box, but he carefully and securely tucked the letter with the black snake totem into his robes, pressing it tightly against his chest.

This item was a hundred times more important than all those account books combined.

**—**

Night fell, the lanterns were lit, and a table of exquisite food and wine was set in the Lanyue Pavilion, the highest point of the Jin residence.

There were no guests, only Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu.

Jin Yu was clearly happy and had drunk a few too many cups. Two moving flushes of red rose on her fair cheeks, and even her eyes, which were always filled with shrewd calculation, held a bit of watery intoxication.

She stood leaning against the railing, the evening breeze blowing her hair and sleeves, making them snap in the wind.

"Yinyu, look."

She stretched out her slender fingers, pointing to the sea of brilliant lights below the pavilion. The ten thousand lights were like a flowing galaxy, covering the entire city of Jinling.

"I stood here the first time I took over the Jin family business. My father, and those uncles in the family, not one of them believed in me. They all said that a woman couldn't hold onto such a large family fortune."

Her voice carried a hint of tipsiness and a trace of imperceptible arrogance.

"Now, the Liu family has fallen, and my Jin family's banners are planted all over Jinling City. I told them: a woman can do it just the same!"

She turned back, looking at Chen Yinyu with blurred, drunken eyes, and suddenly grabbed his hand, pulling him to her side to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with her.

She pointed to the prosperous lights and said with great spirit: "Half of this empire belongs to you."

This was the empire Jin Yu had built—her business empire.

And she was willing to share half of it with him.

Chen Yinyu's heart was struck hard by those six words. He still had the letter that might relate to the true "empire" hidden in his robes.

He looked at Jin Yu's startlingly bright eyes, at the trust and openness in them, and suddenly felt that no court, no power, was as important as the radiance in her eyes at this moment.

He withdrew his gaze from the distance, reached out to take off his own cape, and gently draped it over Jin Yu's shoulders to shield her from the cool night breeze.

"My wife, the empire is too heavy; I don't want the empire."

He leaned close to her, his warm breath brushing against her ear, his voice low and lingering.

"I only want... this half of yours, that is enough."

Jin Yu's heart trembled violently, and her drunkenness vanished by more than half.

She looked at his handsome face close at hand, at the deep, inseparable affection in his eyes, and felt as if she were about to be swallowed by this gentle whirlpool.

Just as the atmosphere was enchanting and their affection was growing—

"Bang! Bang! Bang!"

A flurry of urgent knocking came from the direction of the back courtyard, shattering the tranquility of the garden!

Immediately after, a servant came scrambling up to the pavilion, his face deathly pale, his voice trembling:

"M-Miss! Sir! It's bad!"

"The... the yamen officials are here!"

The flush on Jin Yu’s face faded in an instant, her gaze turning suddenly sharp. Just as she was about to speak, she heard the servant continue, trembling:

“They say… they say the Prefect invites… invites Master Chen to the yamen to ‘have some tea’!”

chapters.title: A Sudden Turn at the Celebration Banquet, This Cup of Tea Is Hard to Swallow
chapters.content:
“The people from the yamen are here!”

The rosy flush on Jin Yu’s face vanished completely, and those eyes, shimmering with the effects of alcohol, turned suddenly piercing.

What invitation from the Prefect? What tea?

This was clearly a trap!

She had just acquired the Liu family estate, and she had forced Xun An to sign a deed that was little more than a contract of indenture. The Jinling Prefect had just ruled in her favor, and now, he was sending men to “invite” her husband?

What kind of scheme was this? It was as obvious as the intentions of Sima Zhao—known to everyone on the street!

Jin Yu shoved Chen Yinyu aside and turned to head downstairs.

“I’d like to see on what grounds he dares to take someone from my Jin household in the middle of the night!”

Her husband, her man—not even the King of Heaven would be allowed to touch a single hair on his head!

“My lady.”

A cool hand gently caught her sleeve from behind. It was Chen Yinyu.

There was not a trace of panic on his face, as if what the servant had just said was nothing more than an insignificant trifle.

“It is merely a matter of tying up loose ends.”

“The Liu family case has only just concluded, and the accounts are complex. Since I was the one handling them, it is only reasonable that the Prefect would want to close the case overnight and call me in to ask a few questions.”

Jin Yu whipped around, staring at him intensely. “Reasonable? Chen Yinyu, do you take me for a fool? Since when is there any reason to hold an interrogation in the dead of night!”

If he dared to go with those men today, tomorrow’s headline in Jinling City would be: “Jin Family’s Son-in-Law ‘Assists in Investigation’ and Fails to Return Overnight!”

What a heavy blow that would be to the prestige the Jin family had just established!

Seeing that she was truly angry, Chen Yinyu was not afraid; instead, his smile deepened.

He took the opportunity to hold Jin Yu’s hand, his fingertips gently stroking the back of her hand.

“My lady’s power is unparalleled. In a single day, you have uprooted the Liu family, who had entrenched themselves in Jinling for years. I am sure the Prefect has taken note of such thunderous methods.”

“He is in a hurry to close the case now simply to curry favor with you, to show that he has no intention of favoring the Liu family.”

He leaned in slightly, whispering into Jin Yu’s ear. His warm breath made her ear itch.

“If I do not go, it would make our Jin family look like we are in the wrong, throwing our weight around.”

His words were airtight; they both elevated Jin Yu and rationalized the Prefect’s behavior.

Jin Yu’s reason told her that things were never that simple.

But looking at Chen Yinyu’s beautiful face, which seemed to say, “Don’t worry, my lady,” and “I have everything under control,” the nameless fire in her heart was truly extinguished.

She admitted that she had once again been bewitched by his appearance—weak and innocent, yet seemingly capable of handling everything.

She scrutinized him suspiciously. “Is it really just for questioning?”

“Naturally.”

Chen Yinyu nodded, his long eyelashes drooping to hide the cold light that flashed in his eyes. “Do you still not trust me, my lady? I will go and return shortly; I still have to warm your bed when I get back.”

He said the last sentence so softly, like a feather, yet it precisely tickled the tip of Jin Yu’s heart.

Her cheeks flushed again, against her will. “…Nonsense!”

Jin Yu glared at him playfully, her tense shoulders finally slumping.

She reached into her sleeve, pulled out a small brocade pouch, and shoved it into his hand without a word.

“This is some hangover-curing plum I prepared for you. You drank quite a bit tonight, so this will keep you from losing your composure before the Prefect.”

Though she spoke of composure, she was thinking that if he really had to stay up all night, eating a plum would help keep him alert.

Chen Yinyu clutched the pouch, which still held her body heat, and nodded firmly. “Thank you, my lady.”

Watching him look so obedient, Jin Yu was still uneasy. She turned to Wang Quan, who was standing nearby, and ordered, “Uncle Wang, prepare a generous gift and accompany the son-in-law yourself. Remember, stay by his side at the yamen gate. If he hasn’t come out after an hour, you…”

Before she could finish, Chen Yinyu interrupted her with a smile.

“My lady, there is no need to make such a fuss.”

He took Jin Yu’s hand and led her to the railing of the pavilion, pointing to the brightly lit mansion below.

“Look, tonight is a great day of victory for our Jin family. The whole household is celebrating. If we disrupt everyone’s peace for a small matter like mine, wouldn’t that spoil your mood?”

“Just wait for me here and warm a pot of tea. I will be back soon.”

He looked at Jin Yu deeply, his gaze lingering and tender, as if he wanted to carve her image into his soul.

Then, he turned resolutely and walked toward the backyard, following the servant who had already grown impatient.

Jin Yu stood on the pavilion, watching his cyan robes gradually disappear into the layers of corridors and shadows.

As the night wind blew, she suddenly felt a chill.

…

Chen Yinyu followed the bailiffs, not leaving through the grand front gate of the Jin estate.

Like ghostly shadows, they bypassed the bustling front courtyard, crossed the silent back garden, and slipped out quietly through a side gate used only by servants.

A plain blue-cloth carriage with no markings was waiting at the gate. A bailiff lifted the curtain and gestured for him to enter, though his tone held no respect.

Chen Yinyu’s gaze fell on the bailiff’s waist, where a thick, dark red short club hung. It looked as if it had been soaked in countless bloodstains—it was the very club used in the yamen to intimidate prisoners.

His heart sank, inch by inch.

Once inside the carriage, he took one last look back.

In the night, the Jin estate was brilliantly lit, like a celestial palace standing in the mortal world—warm and bright.

He could even see the small, stubborn point of light at the highest point of Lanyue Pavilion; that was Jin Yu waiting for him.

Chen Yinyu slowly withdrew his gaze.

The moment the carriage curtain fell, all the soft smiles on his face and all the lingering tenderness in his eyes vanished without a trace.

On that incomparably handsome face, there remained only an ice-cold sternness and a bone-chilling coldness.

The carriage did not head toward the main gate of the yamen but stopped in a dark back alley.

This was the rear hall of the yamen, where they usually dealt with dirty, unspeakable business.

The air was filled with a damp, moldy smell and a faint scent of blood that made one want to retch.

Chen Yinyu was “sandwiched” between two bailiffs and brought into a dimly lit room.

In the center of the room, a middle-aged man in casual treasure-blue Hangzhou silk robes sat in a grand armchair, slowly scraping the foam off his tea with the lid of his cup.

The “shhh-shhh” sound was particularly harsh in the deathly silent room, like a dull knife scraping against one’s eardrums.

He was the Jinling Prefect, Zhang Dechang.

Standing around him were four or five burly men, all with malicious expressions, holding clubs and leather whips. They stared coldly at Chen Yinyu, their eyes like those of a butcher looking at a lamb waiting to be slaughtered.

There was no courtroom, no gavel, not even a cry of “Court is in session.”

This was not an interrogation; this was a private torture chamber.

Chen Yinyu understood perfectly, but he remained calm on the surface, standing quietly in the hall and bowing with cupped hands: “Student Chen Yinyu greets the Prefect.”

Zhang Dechang acted as if he hadn’t heard, keeping his head down and focusing on scraping his tea foam, leaving Chen Yinyu standing there for the time it takes to drink a cup of tea.

Only when he felt he had sufficiently intimidated him did he slowly raise his head.

He did not offer a seat; instead, he spoke with a mocking, insincere smile, his tone filled with undisguised sarcasm.

“Oh, isn’t this our famous Jieyuan of Jinling City?”

Before he finished speaking, his wrist suddenly flicked.

“Clatter—!”

With a crisp sound, the priceless Ru ware teacup hit the ground and shattered into pieces.

Scalding tea mixed with emerald tea leaves splashed everywhere, and a few shards of porcelain even bounced onto Chen Yinyu’s boots.

The air in the entire room seemed to freeze at that moment.

Zhang Dechang slowly stood up, looking down at Chen Yinyu from his height, a cruel sneer curling his lips.

He pointed a finger at the mess of broken porcelain on the floor.

“Oops, my hand slipped.”

“Trouble yourself, Jieyuan Chen, to pick up these fragments.”

He paused, his eyes turning suddenly vicious, and said word by word:

“Remember, you must pick them up while kneeling. That way… it will show your sincerity.”

chapters.title: The Pain of Shattered Porcelain, The Protective Talisman on the Wall
chapters.content:
As the words fell, the bailiffs holding the clubs immediately stepped forward, their fierce, murderous gazes locked onto Chen Yinyu, as if they would strike him down the moment he showed any hesitation.

The air was thick with the damp, moldy smell, mixed with the faint scent of iron-like blood.

Chen Yinyu’s long eyelashes trembled slightly, his gaze moving slowly from Zhang Dechang’s greasy, triumphant face to the ground.

It was a scene of utter ruin.

The sky-blue shards of Ru ware glinted with a cold, sharp light under the dim lamp, and the scalding tea had already lost its heat, leaving only a dark puddle.

The Prefect of Jinling was using such methods to humiliate a scholar who had not yet been convicted.

This was no longer intimidation; it was naked, cruel torture.

The color drained from Chen Yinyu’s face, yet there was no sign of panic or anger.

He simply stood there, his clean cyan robes looking so out of place in this filthy, vile spot.

Time seemed to stretch infinitely at this moment.

The sneer on Zhang Dechang’s lips widened. What he wanted to see was how the bones of this high-minded scholar would be crushed, inch by inch.

He wanted the entire city of Jinling to know the consequences of offending him—and those behind him!

However, to his surprise, Chen Yinyu did not hesitate in the slightest. He calmly lifted the hem of his cyan robes.

“Thump—!”

Chen Yinyu knelt down heavily.

A sharp pain, like a red-hot iron rod, pierced through his knees and instantly swept through his entire body!

His frame swayed violently, almost collapsing to the ground, but he steadied himself with the pride etched into his very bones.

Bright red blood seeped through the fabric almost immediately.

First a dot, then it quickly spread, like eerie red plum blossoms suddenly blooming on the cyan cloth.

Chen Yinyu’s face was as pale as paper, and a fine layer of cold sweat instantly beaded on his forehead, but he bit his lower lip so hard that he did not let out a single sound of pain.

This submissive, silent endurance gave Zhang Dechang a profound sense of sadistic pleasure.

"That’s more like it."

Zhang Dechang sat back down in his grand armchair, picked up the tea that his secretary had just served, and blew on it leisurely, his tone growing increasingly arrogant and overbearing.

"Jieyuan Chen is a smart man; he should know what it means to be a person who knows the times."

He glanced at the shocking bloodstains on the floor, his eyes devoid of pity, filled only with greed.

"I won't beat around the bush with you."

He took a sip of tea and said slowly, "Liu Fugui has accused your Jin family of maliciously swallowing his assets through improper means, leading to the collapse of his business. Although I ruled in your favor, this case is full of suspicious points. If I wanted to overturn the verdict, it would take nothing more than a single word."

Chen Yinyu knelt on the ground, the waves of excruciating pain from his knees threatening to swallow his consciousness.

Yet, he forced himself to ignore the agony that would have made an ordinary person faint, listening to every word clearly.

"I await the Prefect's wise judgment," he said. His voice was somewhat hoarse from the pain, but remained steady.

Zhang Dechang sneered and slammed his teacup onto the table.

"Wise judgment? I think your Jin family has grown quite bold!"

He leaned forward, emphasizing every word: "You annexed the Liu family; you must have made at least this much, right?"

He held up five fat fingers.

"I don't want much. Give me fifty percent, and this matter will be completely settled. Otherwise, don't just talk about a charge of 'malicious annexation'—I can also pin a major crime of 'hoarding and manipulating market prices' on your Jin family! By then, it won't be as simple as just kneeling here!"

Fifty percent!

He dared to open his mouth like a lion, demanding half of the family fortune that the Jin family had risked everything to win!

This was no Prefect; he was a bandit in official robes!

The pain in his knees and the surging hatred in his heart intertwined like two beasts tearing at his nerves.

Chen Yinyu dug his fingernails deep into his palms, using the new pain to maintain clarity of mind.

He could not collapse, and he certainly could not let anger cloud his judgment.

Jin Yu was still waiting for him to return.

He slowly raised his head, his gaze appearing unfocused due to the pain, while he actually scanned the study, which served as a private torture chamber.

Finally, his gaze fixed on the wall behind Zhang Dechang, where a beautifully framed "Painting of One Hundred Longevity Characters" hung.

One hundred "Shou" (Longevity) characters, each in a different style, were written in gold powder. The brushwork varied, appearing as if it were a celebratory gift, luxurious and festive.

But Chen Yinyu’s photographic memory instantly captured the strangeness within it.

These "Shou" characters were arranged without any pattern, and the flow of the brushstrokes betrayed a deliberate design.

His gaze continued to move, landing on a sandalwood bookshelf nearby.

The shelf was stuffed with files, but in one small compartment, the corners of several letters were inadvertently exposed.

The material of the envelopes was clearly a special supply from the "Gongxuan Paper Workshop" in the capital, and in the bottom right corner of the envelopes was a tiny, barely noticeable red seal with the character "Pang."

Pang!

It was the Grand Tutor of the current dynasty, Pang Wei!

In a flash of lightning, a horrifying thought exploded in his mind!

Enduring the waves of intense pain from his knees, he forced his extraordinary memory to look at the "Painting of One Hundred Longevity Characters" once more.

This was no celebratory painting!

Each "Shou" character was a homophone or a stand-in for a name! Their arrangement was a tangled web of corruption spanning the Jiangnan officialdom!

Zhang Dechang, Liu Fugui... name after name, official position after official position—through those golden "Shou" characters, they were all tightly linked to the name at the very top: Grand Tutor Pang!

This painting was Zhang Dechang’s protective talisman, and also his proof of allegiance!

Chen Yinyu’s breathing suddenly became rapid.

He forced his eyes wide open, carving those one hundred "Shou" characters, along with every name and every layer of connection they represented, deep into his mind!

Time passed slowly in the silent torture.

Half an hour went by.

The cold sweat on Chen Yinyu’s forehead flowed like rain down his pale cheeks, dripping into the pool of blood beneath him, splashing into tiny ripples.

The green robes at his knees were already soaked through with blood, becoming wet and sticky, clinging tightly to his lacerated wounds.

Zhang Dechang had long since lost patience and gone to the next room to handle other "matters," leaving him there like a worn-out torture device.

A secretary in a long gown walked in. Seeing Chen Yinyu’s miserable state, a flash of pity crossed his eyes, but he still advised, "Jieyuan Chen, why bother? All the Prefect wants is money. Why suffer like this? Just write the confession, admit the Jin family used improper means, and this matter..."

"A confession?"

Chen Yinyu slowly raised his head, his lips pale, and a weak smile curled at the corners of his mouth.

"This commoner is dull-witted," he said softly. "I only know I was ordered to come and pick up a teacup; I do not know what crime I have committed."

The secretary was choked by these words. Looking at those terrifyingly clear eyes, he was momentarily speechless.

There was no submission in that gaze, no pleading—only a bottomless, icy pool.

The secretary sighed, shook his head, and left.

Chen Yinyu lowered his head again, silently reciting in his heart, word by word.

Zhang Dechang, Grand Tutor Pang.

Today’s pain of shattered porcelain, the humiliation of bone-deep wounds.

In the days to come, I, Chen Yinyu, will make you... pay it back a thousand, ten thousand times over!

...

Meanwhile, at the Jin residence.

The banquet at Lanyue Pavilion had long since dispersed, and the maids were efficiently clearing away the leftovers.

The night breeze blew away the scent of wine and also awakened Jin Yu’s mind, which had been muddled by slight intoxication.

She sat by the window, supporting her chin with one hand, watching the courtyard below grow quiet, yet the inexplicable restlessness in her heart grew heavier.

It had been nearly an hour, and Chen Yinyu had not returned.

She poured herself a cup of cold tea and drank it in one gulp. The icy liquid slid down her throat, but it could not suppress the flame burning ever brighter in her heart.

"Uncle Wang!" she called out.

Wang Quan immediately trotted up from downstairs and bowed. "Eldest Miss, what are your orders?"

Jin Yu’s gaze was sharp. "The son-in-law still hasn't returned?"

Wang Quan’s body stiffened imperceptibly. His eyes darted away as he stammered, "The son-in-law... perhaps the Prefect had many questions, and he was delayed..."

"Delayed?"

Jin Yu stood up abruptly and grabbed Wang Quan’s arm with such force that the old steward gasped.

She stared at him fixedly. "I told you to stay at the entrance of the Yamen and never leave! Why are you back here?!"

Terrified by the murderous look in her eyes, Wang Quan’s legs went weak, and he nearly knelt, trembling, "Eldest Miss, please calm your anger! It is not that this old servant did not keep watch! The son-in-law... he didn't even enter through the main gate of the Yamen!"

"They... they took the son-in-law in through a side gate in the back alley! That is... that is where they interrogate prisoners!"

"Boom—!"

Jin Yu’s mind instantly went blank.

Back alley?

Side gate?

Interrogating prisoners?

He had lied to her!

That damned, self-righteous bastard actually dared to charge into a dragon’s den and tiger’s lair all by himself!

An unprecedented rage and panic instantly gripped her heart. Her husband was currently in the back hall of the Yamen, and she didn't know what inhuman treatment he was suffering!

A towering rage ignited in Jin Yu’s eyes, and her voice was as cold as icicles in the dead of winter.

"Wang Quan! Prepare the horses! Summon all the guards and have them bring their weapons!"

"I want to see who gave him the dog-guts to lay a hand on my, Jin Yu’s, person!"

chapters.title: Storming the Yamen, Opening Doors with Money
chapters.content:
Wang Quan’s old face lost all color, and he fell to his knees with a thud, clutching Jin Yu’s legs.

"Eldest Miss! You absolutely cannot!"

The old steward’s voice trembled, filled with tears.

"To storm the Yamen with weapons is a crime of rebellion! It will bring the disaster of extermination upon the Jin family!"

Rebellion?

Extermination?

These two words were like two basins of ice water poured over Jin Yu’s peak rage.

She was no impulsive, brainless brute; she was the head of the Jin family business. Behind her was a century-old foundation and the livelihoods of thousands of people.

Jin Yu’s bloodshot eyes stared fixedly in the direction of the Yamen. Her fingernails dug deep into her palms from the force, bringing a sharp pain that also brought back a sliver of cold reason.

To deal with a bottomless, hungry wolf like Zhang Dechang, using swords and blades was the worst strategy. That would be going head-to-head with the official powers behind him; it was like throwing an egg against a rock.

Jin Yu’s chest heaved violently. The rage and panic that threatened to tear her apart were forcibly suppressed, transforming into a more chilling, eerie calmness.

She suddenly laughed, a coldness in her laughter.

"Uncle Wang is right. Using blades and guns is too crude; it lowers the status of our Jin family."

She loosened her clenched fists and smoothed the wrinkles on her sleeves in a leisurely manner. The rage in her bright, beautiful eyes receded, leaving only a bottomless, icy pool.

"Go, open the warehouse."

Her voice was flat, yet more terrifying than her previous roar. "Load two chests of silver for me. Use the largest ingots, the kind filled so high the lids won't even close."

Wang Quan was stunned, unable to react for a moment.

Jin Yu glanced at him sideways, the corners of her mouth curling up. "What are you standing there for? My husband has been invited to have tea, and as his wife, I naturally must go and settle the bill."

"...Yes!"

Wang Quan shivered and scrambled to his feet. He understood.

The Eldest Miss wasn't going to reason; she was going to crush them with money!

...

Jingling Yamen, back alley.

A plain, unadorned carriage stopped at the alley entrance. Jin Yu stepped down in her magnificent robes, followed by four sturdy servants carrying two heavy, black-lacquered wooden chests.

"Bang!"

"Bang!"

The wooden chests were set down heavily, the dull thud echoing clearly in the deathly silent alley.

The two bailiffs guarding the side gate immediately stepped forward with their staves, looking fierce and menacing.

"Who goes there! This is a restricted area of the Yamen; no idlers allowed!"

Jin Yu couldn't be bothered to look at them.

Wang Quan stepped forward and slapped one of the chests, the heavy lid clattering open with a loud bang.

In an instant, a silvery-white radiance overflowed from the chest, illuminating the greedy and shocked faces of the two bailiffs!

It was a chest filled to the brim with fifty-tael silver ingots!

In the dim alley, this light was brighter than moonlight and more piercing than the gleam of a blade.

The two bailiffs’ breathing stopped instantly; their eyes bulged as if they were about to pop out of their sockets, and they could barely keep a grip on their wooden staves.

Jin Yu walked forward with elegant strides. She reached her slender, jade-like hand into the sea of silver and grabbed a handful—at least four or five ingots.

She weighed the heavy load in her hand, then swung it, slamming it straight into the chest of the lead bailiff!

"Thud! Thud!"

The dull sound of impact made the bailiff cry out in pain and stumble backward, yet he felt no resentment—he even looked as if he wanted to be hit a few more times.

"Get lost! Go tell that man surnamed Zhang that I, Jin Yu, have come to pay his tea bill. Tell him to crawl out here and count it himself!"

Jin Yu’s aura was so terrifying that the two bailiffs scrambled to their feet in a panic. One scurried inside to deliver the message, while the other tremblingly pulled open the heavy wooden door.

Dressed in a magnificent embroidered gown, Jin Yu stepped onto the filthy, damp flagstone path and marched straight inside.

In the back hall of the yamen.

Zhang Dechang was just changing out of his official robes, preparing to rest in the back courtyard, when he heard a commotion outside.

Before he could even open his mouth to curse, the door was smashed open from the outside with a "boom!"

Jin Yu appeared before him, wrapped in an air of chilling frost.

Zhang Dechang was startled. When he saw who it was, and then noticed the two large, silver-glowing chests behind her, a flash of greed and suspicion crossed his eyes.

"Miss... Miss Jin?"

He cleared his throat, feigning composure. "What is the meaning of you barging into my yamen in the middle of the night?"

Jin Yu’s gaze was like two sharp blades, scraping him from head to toe. Finally, she spoke coldly, asking only two words.

"Where is he?"

"Who?"

Zhang Dechang’s eyes darted around. He immediately put on a look of sudden realization and smiled greasily. "Oh, you mean Young Master Chen? The official and I hit it off immediately and had a pleasant conversation. I invited him for a cup of tea, and I already sent him home long ago."

Jin Yu looked at his hypocritical face, the murderous intent in her heart nearly impossible to suppress.

Sent him home long ago?

Did he take her for a three-year-old child!

She said nothing, her sharp gaze sweeping rapidly across the study.

The furnishings were elegant, but they could not mask a musty, decaying odor. Her eyes finally locked onto an inconspicuous side door on the side of the study.

Without waiting for Zhang Dechang to react, Jin Yu lunged forward and kicked it open!

"Bang—!"

The fragile door panel gave way with a crash!

Behind the door was a smaller, darker room—less of a side parlor and more of a storage closet.

By the light filtering in from the study, Jin Yu instantly caught sight of the figure that made her heart stop.

Chen Yinyu was facing away from the door, his green robes so stained by the darkness that their color was unrecognizable. He was bracing himself against the damp wall with one hand, his body trembling uncontrollably as if he were using every ounce of his strength to try and stand up from the floor.

Even from just his back, the sense of loneliness and fragility emanating from his very bones pierced Jin Yu’s eyes painfully.

"Chen Yinyu!"

She cried out, her voice trembling in a way she hadn't even realized.

Hearing her voice, the figure stiffened violently.

In the next second, he turned around with incredible speed.

The moment he turned, he instinctively straightened his robes, pulling his long hem down to hide his knees.

When he finally faced Jin Yu, a gentle, impeccable smile was already plastered on his face.

The smile was still faint and soft, but his complexion was as pale as transparent paper, and his lips were devoid of any color.

"My lady?"

He spoke softly, his tone carrying a hint of perfectly measured surprise and the relief of seeing a loved one.

"It’s late, why are you here?"

As he spoke, he tried to walk toward her, as if he had only been stopping by briefly and was just about to head home.

"I... I was just about to leave."

However, he had only taken one step when his body swayed violently, as if he had tripped over something, and he nearly collapsed to the ground.

Jin Yu lunged forward and caught him firmly.

Under her touch, his arms were ice-cold and rigid. Even through the fabric, she could feel his muscles tensing and trembling.

Jin Yu’s heart felt as if it were being gripped tightly by an invisible hand; it hurt so much she could barely breathe.

He was still acting!

Even at a time like this, this man was still acting in front of her!

Acting as if he were docile and harmless, acting as if he were safe and sound!

Her gaze moved uncontrollably downward, landing on the knees he had just desperately tried to cover.

On the clean green fabric, two dark red stains were silently spreading in the moonlight, like two eerie blood-red plum blossoms blooming in a desperate situation.

Those weren't water stains—that was blood!

Boom—!

Jin Yu’s mind completely exploded. Her hands, which were supporting him, tightened sharply, her fingertips turning white from the force.

An unprecedented emotion, a mixture of overwhelming rage and sharp, piercing heartbreak, instantly drowned out all her reason.

She slowly raised her head, looking past Chen Yinyu’s shoulder at the stunned Zhang Dechang by the door.

At this moment, there was no expression on Jin Yu’s face. All emotion had faded from her bright eyes, leaving only a deathly, freezing cold that could turn a person to ice.

She didn't look at Chen Yinyu again, but instead turned while supporting him, her gaze pinned directly onto Zhang Dechang.

"Magistrate Zhang."

She pointed to the two wide-open wooden chests outside, the silver light so bright it was blinding. "Consider these two chests of silver... the tea money I am paying on behalf of my husband."

Zhang Dechang’s Adam’s apple bobbed involuntarily; his greedy nature made it impossible for him to tear his eyes away from the two chests of gleaming silver.

A mocking smile curled the corners of Jin Yu’s lips.

"The Jin family always has plenty of tea. In the future, if you wish to have more, Magistrate, just send someone to the Jin residence to say the word. I will personally deliver it to your manor myself—I guarantee it will be a hundred times better than the tea served in this yamen."

Her tone shifted abruptly, dropping to freezing point.

"However..."

"If there is a next time, if you dare to touch even a single hair on his head..."

She did not finish the sentence, but the unfinished threat was more chilling than any vicious curse.

Her eyes were no longer the shrewdness of a merchant, nor the arrogance of a noblewoman, but the desperate, insane murderous intent of a beast guarding its young.

Meeting those eyes, Zhang Dechang felt a chill shoot from the soles of his feet to the top of his head, and he couldn't help but shiver.
