Jin Yu ignored him further, treating him as if he were already a dead man.

She draped one of Chen Yinyu’s arms over her shoulder, using her slender frame to support most of his weight.

"Let’s go home."

For the first time, her voice held a hint of imperceptible tenderness and tremor.

"Okay."

Chen Yinyu replied softly, leaning his entire weight onto her without reservation, as if she were his only piece of driftwood in this world.

He was a head taller than her, yet at this moment, he buried his face in the crook of her neck like a child.

chapters.title: Wounds Exposed, So You Can Feel Pain Too
chapters.content:
The carriage ride back to the Jin residence was deathly silent.

Inside the carriage, only a small lantern was lit. The dim, yellowish glow swayed gently with the jolting of the wheels, stretching and shrinking the shadows of the two.

Chen Yinyu leaned against the soft brocade cushions, his face still pale from excessive blood loss.

Yet he acted as if nothing were wrong, even pulling a faint smile to try and ease the frozen atmosphere.

"My lady, Magistrate Zhang didn't actually make things difficult for me."

"He just saw that my calligraphy was decent and insisted on challenging me to a game of chess. We played quite a few rounds."

His tone was light, as if he had truly just attended an elegant chess match.

Jin Yu said nothing. She simply reached out and gripped the hand he had resting on his knee.

Under her touch, it was bone-chillingly cold.

What was worse, that hand—which was usually steady and strong—was now trembling uncontrollably in the depths of her palm.

She said nothing, only gripping that cold hand tighter, as if trying to warm him with her own body heat.

The carriage pulled to a steady stop at the side gate of the Jin residence. Wang Quan was already waiting anxiously at the entrance with several trusted servants holding lanterns.

The carriage curtain was lifted, and Chen Yinyu leaned forward first, preparing to step out.

He maintained that same gentle, composed posture, a faint, reassuring smile still hanging on his lips.

However, the moment one foot touched the ground and the other was about to step off the carriage board, disaster struck!

His body swayed violently. His supporting leg seemed to have all its strength drained away; his knee buckled, and he fell forward, caught off guard, about to kneel onto the cold stone steps!

"Chen Yinyu!"

Jin Yu let out a sharp cry. Her reaction was astonishingly fast; almost the moment his body tilted, she lunged out of the carriage and caught his crumbling form, pulling him tightly into her arms.

The man’s lean body collided with her embrace—lighter and stiffer than she had imagined.

At that very moment, a faint, metallic scent of blood mixed with dust drifted into Jin Yu’s nostrils.

Her heart sank heavily.

In the bedroom, Jin Yu dismissed all the servants. The warm candlelight illuminated the room as brightly as day, also revealing Chen Yinyu’s bloodless face.

"Get on the bed." Jin Yu’s voice was hoarse, devoid of any emotion.

Chen Yinyu was being half-supported and half-carried by her. Hearing this, he instinctively took a step back, creating some distance.

His gaze darted away, his long eyelashes drooping to hide all the emotions in his eyes.

"My lady, don't..."

His voice was very soft, carrying a hint of imperceptible pleading. "I'm dirty, I haven't bathed yet. I'll soil your bed."

Again with this!

Even at a time like this, he was still thinking about these trivial, unimportant matters!

Did he have any idea that the more sensible he acted, the more it made her heart ache until she felt like she was going insane!

The fire that Jin Yu had been suppressing in her chest finally exploded at this moment.

She looked at him, her eyes reddening bit by bit, yet her voice was as cold as ice.

"I’ll say it one more time: get to the bed!"

Chen Yinyu shuddered at her shout, seemingly frightened by her current demeanor.

He bit his bloodless lower lip, and in the end, he obediently shuffled to the bedside and sat down stiffly.

Jinyu stepped forward, and before he could react, she grabbed his ankle!

"Wife!" Chen Yinyu exclaimed, instinctively trying to struggle.

Jinyu acted as if she hadn't heard him. With a force that was almost brutal, she yanked the leg of his green trousers upward!

But her movements froze completely the moment she saw the sight at his knees.

That... could no longer be called a knee.

It was a mass of mangled flesh, bruised and purple.

The fabric of his trousers had long been soaked through with blood, and upon drying, it had stuck fast to the exposed raw flesh.

Her movement just now was equivalent to tearing off a layer of his skin and flesh along with the fabric!

Embedded within that mess of gore were several sharp, glinting shards of porcelain.

The largest piece was nearly the size of a fingernail, driven deep into his kneecap, and the surrounding flesh had already begun to turn black.

So, that so-called "friendly chess match" meant making him kneel on broken porcelain to play?

In that instant, Jinyu felt as if her breath had been stolen away, and something scalding surged from her eyes without warning.

One drop, two drops...

Like beads from a broken string, they fell onto her luxurious cloud-brocade skirt, quickly blooming into small, dark water stains.

She was crying.

This female tycoon, who made ruthless decisions in the business world without batting an eye, was now like a helpless child, her tears flowing in an unstoppable torrent.

She wasn't crying because of lost money, nor because she herself was hurt.

It was because this man before her, this "ornament" she had bought with her money, had suffered such a grievous injury, yet he was still smiling at her, still telling her it "wasn't dirty."

So, he could feel pain too.

So, he wasn't truly invulnerable or unbreakable.

So, beneath that gentle, harmless exterior, he could also bleed and tremble in agony.

"Don't... don't cry..."

Chen Yinyu was completely panicked. He had never seen Jinyu cry. In his mind, she was always that radiant, omnipotent benefactor.

He subconsciously reached out to wipe the tears from her face.

But halfway there, seeing the dust and dried blood on his fingertips, he pulled his hand back as if electrocuted, hiding it behind his back in embarrassment.

He could only comfort her clumsily with his hoarse, trembling voice.

"Wife, don't cry... I'm fine..."

"Really... it doesn't hurt."

The more he said this, the harder Jinyu wept.

She wiped her face messily with her sleeve and took out the small silver tweezers she used for grooming her brows and the finest medicinal powder from her vanity case.

She knelt on the footstool before him, her hand trembling as she held the candle closer, while the other hand held the tweezers, carefully aiming for the shard embedded in his flesh.

"It might hurt a little, bear with it," she said through a thick, congested nose, gritting her teeth.

"Mm." Chen Yinyu squeezed out a syllable from his throat.

Jinyu took a deep breath, her fingertips turning white from the pressure on the tweezers.

She held her breath, steadied her mind, and the tip of the tweezers precisely gripped the largest porcelain shard.

Then, she yanked it out!

"Ugh!"

Chen Yinyu’s body arched like a bow in an instant, a stifled groan of extreme pain escaping his throat, and a fine layer of cold sweat broke out on his forehead.

A fresh stream of blood gushed from the wound.

Jinyu’s heart felt as if it had been gouged by those tweezers, the pain making her entire body convulse.

She looked at his handsome face twisted in agony, at his stubborn refusal to let out a cry of pain as he bit his lip, and an emotion mixed with monstrous rage and extreme heartbreak consumed her.

Why? Why should her person suffer such torment?

The person she held in the palm of her hand, the one she couldn't even bear to speak a harsh word to, why should he be so humiliated by a petty, insignificant official!

Jinyu threw the blood-stained porcelain shard into the tray with a sharp "clatter."

She raised her head, her eyes, washed by tears, shining with a terrifying intensity.

"Zhang Dechang... I have money!"

"I will buy the best assassins in the world! I will smash his yamen to the ground! I will have him hacked into a thousand pieces and his bones ground to dust!"

At this moment, she was no longer the calculating merchant.

She was like a lioness whose territory had been invaded and whose cub had been harmed, wanting only to tear her enemy to shreds in the most primitive, bloody way possible.

chapters.title: A Midnight Vow, I Will Be the One Who Holds the Blade
chapters.content:
However, just as Jinyu’s raging fury was about to burn away her reason, a hand suddenly grabbed her wrist.

The hand didn't use much force, but it carried an irresistible strength, like a basin of ice water poured over her head, bringing Jinyu’s madness to a sudden halt.

She whipped her head around and collided with a pair of bottomless eyes.

Those peach-blossom eyes, which were always filled with affection and gentle, spring-like smiles, were now filled with a dead, icy stillness.

There was no grievance, no pain—only a heart-stopping, near-cruel calmness.

"Wife."

Chen Yinyu spoke, his voice severely hoarse yet exceptionally clear. "Money cannot kill him."

Jinyu shuddered.

She saw Chen Yinyu’s gaze fall upon the blood-stained porcelain in the tray; there was not a ripple of emotion in his eyes, as if that object hadn't been pulled from his own flesh.

"Because he holds power."

His voice was very soft, yet it struck Jinyu’s heart like a heavy hammer.

"In the face of power, a vast fortune is nothing more than a fatted calf waiting to be slaughtered."

"Today he can make your person kneel on broken porcelain; tomorrow he can fabricate charges, raid your firm, and turn your century-old foundation into nothing in an instant."

"By then, your vast fortune will only be a new patch on someone else's official robe."

"And you—you won't even have a place to cry for justice."

Every word was cold and blunt, slicing open the powerful shell Jinyu had built with money, revealing the soft, helpless reality within.

It was true.

"The commoner does not fight the official"—this was a survival rule carved into the bones of every merchant.

She could bribe one official, but she couldn't bribe the entire bureaucracy.

She could buy an assassin, but she couldn't silence the masses or the crushing weight of the law.

Her rage, her money—in the true game of power, they were as fragile as a joke.

The fire in Jinyu’s eyes extinguished bit by bit, replaced by a deeper, colder despair.

She looked at Chen Yinyu’s face, pale to the point of transparency, and at the shocking mess of flesh on his knees. Her heart felt as if it were being gripped by an invisible hand, making it impossible to breathe.

For the first time, she felt her own powerlessness so clearly.

Just then, the hand gripping her wrist tightened slightly.

Chen Yinyu braced himself against the edge of the bed, using his uninjured leg to support himself, and slowly moved off the bed.

"Wife."

He spoke word by word, his voice not loud, yet as if he were using all his strength. "I must have this power, too."

Jinyu’s pupils contracted sharply; she heard the sound of her own heart beating like a drum.

Chen Yinyu gazed at her, and beneath the ice in his eyes, a small flame ignited—one strong enough to set the plains ablaze.

"I will take the imperial examinations. I will become an official. I will hold the blade that decides the life and death of others with my own hands."

"I will ensure that in this world, no one ever dares to make you suffer the slightest grievance again! I will ensure that in this world, no one ever dares to make you bow your head again!"

Boom!

It was as if thousands of thunderclaps had exploded in Jinyu’s mind simultaneously.

She was completely stunned, staring blankly at the man kneeling before her.

He was a mess, his clothes stained with blood and dust, his face as white as paper, and the wound on his knee still seeping blood.

Yet the words he spoke were more powerful than the hardest stone in the world.

Imperial examinations? Becoming an official?

She had always thought he only wanted to live a stable life as a kept man, to be the most beautiful canary hidden in her golden house.

She was happy to provide for him, to spoil him, and to protect him under her wings.

But she had never imagined that this man, who appeared so weak and helpless, would be willing to walk the most difficult, most dangerous path—the one where thousands of soldiers and horses cross a single-plank bridge—for her sake.

For a scholar to marry into a merchant's family was to cut himself off from the path to success.

If he were to pick up his books again, he would face the sneers and contempt of the entire scholar class, and thorns and obstacles a hundred, a thousand times greater than those of an ordinary student.

What was he doing this for?

Jinyu’s vision blurred.

Not for himself, not to bring honor to his ancestors, but simply so that... no one would ever dare make her bow her head again.

So, the "captivity" she thought she had imposed was, in his heart, a "treasure" worth protecting with his life and his future.

An indescribable, scalding warmth surged from the depths of her heart, instantly sweeping through her limbs and bones, dispelling all the cold and despair from moments ago.

Jinyu reached out with trembling hands and gently stroked his cold cheek. That handsome face, which could topple kingdoms, was now filled with a tenacity and stubbornness that did not belong to his age.

Her fingertips brushed his tightly pressed lips, her voice filled with unprecedented solemnity and tenderness.

"Good."

It was only one word, yet it weighed a thousand pounds.

"If you want to take the exams, I will pave a path to the heavens for you."

"If you want to be an official, I will smash open an indestructible Golden Throne for you."

"Chen Yinyu, remember this."

Jinyu leaned down, her forehead resting against his, their noses almost touching.

"From now on, we are one—husband and wife, sharing in honor and disgrace."

That night, Jinyu did not return to her own room.

After the wounds were carefully cleaned and re-dressed with medicine, Chen Yinyu was firmly pressed by her onto her own priceless agarwood bed.

The two slept in each other's arms.

There was no hint of passion, only the peace of having survived a disaster and two hearts pressed incredibly close together.

In the darkness, Jin Yu took the initiative to roll over and kissed Chen Yinyu’s lips.

This kiss held no lust, but it was a mark, a promise.

In his sleep, Chen Yinyu returned to that cold, damp back hall. Zhang Dechang’s nauseating face was right before him, and the floor was still covered in shards of porcelain glinting with a cold light.

He heard that arrogant voice command him: "Kneel!"

But this time, he did not move.

He only slowly raised his hand. Unbeknownst to him, he was holding a sword—a long, narrow, sharp blade that shone as clear as autumn water.

He did not draw it; he only tapped the hilt lightly with his finger.

That crisp sound made Zhang Dechang’s face turn deathly pale in an instant, and his entire body began to tremble like chaff in the wind.

The dream ended there.

The next morning, a ray of brilliant sunlight pierced through the lattice window, dancing playfully upon the brocade quilt.

Chen Yinyu slowly opened his eyes, the blinding light causing him to squint instinctively.

A strand of dark hair fell before his eyes, carrying a familiar, sweet fragrance.

He turned his head and saw Jin Yu’s magnified sleeping face.

She was sleeping soundly, her long eyelashes casting a quiet shadow beneath her lids. The brows and eyes that were usually sharp and assertive were now filled with a rare peace and softness.

The sunlight gilded her with a warm golden edge, making her look like a fragile statue of a glass deity.

Chen Yinyu’s heart softened abruptly. He reached out cautiously, wanting to brush away a stray lock of hair from her cheek.

Before his fingertips could touch her, Jin Yu’s eyelashes fluttered gently, and she slowly opened her eyes.

Their gazes met. There were no words, as if the bloodshed and vows of the previous night were merely a distant dream.

Looking at each other, they both curled the corners of their mouths in unison. This was a brand-new morning, one that belonged solely to the two of them.

However, this rare tranquility and tenderness were completely shattered by a sudden, panicked shout!

"Eldest Miss! Eldest Miss, it’s bad!"

Wang Quan’s voice came from behind the heavy door, laced with irrepressible anxiety.

"The Master and the Second Master are here!"

"They’re in the front hall! They say... they say they want an explanation from you!"

chapters.title: Forcing the Son-in-Law Out, a Backstab from Father
chapters.content:
The soft smile on Jin Yu’s face froze inch by inch, turning into a biting frost.

The vows of last night still echoed in her ears, and the warmth of this morning had yet to dissipate, yet her father and her own uncle were already so impatient to storm her home?

"Wife."

Chen Yinyu’s voice sounded by her side, carrying a hint of reassurance.

He had already braced himself against the edge of the bed to stand on one leg. The laziness was gone from his peach-blossom eyes, leaving only the stillness of a cold pool.

Jin Yu took a deep breath, suppressing the surging hostility in her heart.

She rose quickly, dressed with efficient movements, and personally walked over to support Chen Yinyu’s arm.

"I’ll help you."

Chen Yinyu did not refuse, obediently leaning most of his weight onto Jin Yu.

The two walked step by step, moving extremely slowly; the path from the inner chamber to the front hall had never felt so long.

Along the way, the servants of the manor kept their heads bowed, not daring to even breathe loudly. The air was thick with the oppressive tension of an impending storm.

Jin Yu’s expression grew colder and colder. Finally, they reached the front hall.

As soon as they stepped into the hall, a dull, stifling atmosphere rushed toward them.

Jin Yu raised her eyes.

She saw her father, Jin Wansan, sitting upright in the main seat, his old face pulled tight, his eyes filled with anxiety and fury.

Her second uncle, Jin Wansan, sat in the lower seat, a faint, gloating sneer playing on his lips.

In the center of the hall lay a mess of broken porcelain.

"So you finally show yourself!"

Seeing them enter, Jin Wansan seemed like a lit firecracker; he slammed the table and stood up abruptly.

His gaze passed over Jin Yu and fixed on Chen Yinyu like a knife.

"You jinx!"

Jin Wansan grabbed another teacup from the table and, without a second thought, hurled it fiercely toward Chen Yinyu!

Jin Yu’s pupils shrank, and she instinctively moved to shield Chen Yinyu behind her.

However, Chen Yinyu was faster. Almost the moment the teacup left the hand, he shifted his body imperceptibly, using his own back to block Jin Yu completely.

"Bang!"

The teacup smashed near Chen Yinyu’s feet and shattered.

Scalding tea splashed out, and a few drops even landed on his injured knee, immediately staining the wrapped gauze with a dark, wet patch.

Chen Yinyu didn’t even frown, only lowering his eyes as if he weren't the one who had been targeted.

But Jin Yu’s heart felt as if it had been scorched by that boiling tea.

She looked up abruptly, her eyes as cold as ice: "Father! What are you doing!"

"What am I doing? I should be asking you what good deeds you’ve done!"

Jin Wansan was trembling with rage, pointing at Jin Yu’s nose and cursing, "Look at the fine husband you’ve chosen! The Jin family’s century-old foundation is about to be destroyed by his hands!"

Jin Yu sneered: "I’d like to hear how the Jin family’s foundation is being destroyed by him?"

"You still dare to talk back!" Jin Wansan was incensed.

Seeing this, Jin Wansan (the uncle) spoke up slowly, his tone filled with hypocritical heartbreak: "Yu’er, it’s not that Second Uncle wants to lecture you, but you’ve truly brought disaster upon us this time."

He cleared his throat and recounted the story.

It turned out that early this morning, the Prefect’s yamen had suddenly sent men to seal off three of the Jin family’s shops in the most prosperous area of the East City, citing "poor management and suspicious goods" as the reason!

One of them was the Jin family’s largest silver shop!

This sudden, thunderous move caught the Jin family completely off guard.

Jin Wansan panicked and hurriedly sent men to smooth things over, but the money sent was returned untouched, bringing back only one message.

"The Prefect said," Jin Wansan (the uncle) paused deliberately, enjoying Jin Yu’s darkening expression, "that someone offended the yamen and the official’s dignity last night. His Honor is in a bad mood, so this business... had better stop for now."

"Unless..." Jin Wansan (the uncle) drew out his tone, his gaze scanning back and forth between Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu, "the Jin family can provide enough 'sincerity'."

Jin Yu’s heart sank straight to the bottom. She knew this was Zhang Dechang’s revenge.

She had made Zhang Dechang lose face yesterday, and today he was going to cut off the Jin family’s livelihood.

What a fine example of "the commoner cannot fight the official"!

"What sincerity?" Jin Yu’s voice was heavy.

Jin Wansan (the uncle) had finally waited for this moment. He sighed with feigned heaviness: "Prefect Zhang has a son, twenty years of age, not yet married..."

Alarm bells rang in Jin Yu’s heart.

She heard her uncle continue: "Prefect Zhang said he admires your ability to manage the household, Yu’er. If you... can divorce this Chen Yinyu and remarry the Prefect’s son as a secondary wife, then the Jin family and the Prefect’s yamen will be one family."

"By then, not to mention three shops, even if we want to expand business to the capital, Prefect Zhang will open the doors wide for our Jin family!"

As his words fell, the entire hall fell into a deathly silence.

Chen Yinyu kept his eyes lowered, as if he hadn't heard this absurd proposal, but the hand resting on Jin Yu’s arm tightened imperceptibly.

Jin Yu was stunned; she thought she had misheard.

She stared blankly at her father and her uncle, as if looking at two strangers she had never met before.

Ask her... to divorce Chen Yinyu and go be a secondary wife to the Prefect’s legendary idiot son, who supposedly couldn't even speak clearly and drooled all day?

This was the "solution" they had come up with?

To trade her entire life for three shops?

Absurd!

It was the most ridiculous thing under heaven!

A few seconds later, an irrepressible, light laugh escaped Jin Yu’s lips.

She laughed.

She laughed until her shoulders trembled, until tears were about to spill from her eyes.

"Father."

She looked up, her gaze fixed directly on Jin Wansan, "Are you senile? You want me to marry that drooling idiot? For the sake of those few 'broken shops' you speak of, you would sell your own daughter?"

Jin Wansan felt guilty under her laughter, and was further enraged by her calling them "broken shops." His old face turned the color of a pig’s liver.

He slammed the table and roared, his voice harsh but weak: "Insolent!"

"What do you mean by selling my daughter? This is for our Jin family! For our century-old foundation!"

"As long as the Jin family doesn't fall, you will still be the noble Eldest Miss. Which of your comforts will be lacking? Sacrificing one person’s marriage to preserve the entire family—what is wrong with that?!"

"What is wrong with that?" Jin Yu repeated these words, feeling a chill rise from the soles of her feet to the top of her head.

In this moment, she finally saw clearly.

In her father’s eyes, she, his daughter, was no different from the goods on the shelves.

She was merely a chip that could be sacrificed and traded for profit.

Just as she was trembling with rage, nearly losing control of her tongue, a cold, clear voice suddenly sounded before her.

"Father-in-law."

It was Chen Yinyu.

He had let go of Jin Yu’s arm at some point and stepped half a step forward, shielding Jin Yu behind him.

Although one of his legs was still injured and his stance was somewhat strained, his thin back stood like an insurmountable mountain.

"Jin Yu is a person, not merchandise."

"This Jin family foundation was earned by her, bit by bit. You... have no right to sell her."

Hearing Chen Yinyu’s words, Jin Wansan was completely enraged!

A live-in son-in-law who relied on a woman to get ahead, a pretty boy who had done nothing of note, dared to talk back to him to his face!

"You... you..." He pointed at Chen Yinyu, his fingers trembling, unable to utter a complete sentence for a long time.

"Rebellion! This is pure rebellion!"

Just then, a sudden change occurred!

Jin Wansan suddenly clutched his chest, his face turning deathly pale in an instant, his lips purple, and his entire body collapsed limply toward the floor!

"Father!" Jin Yu’s expression changed.

"Big Brother!"

Jin Wansan (the uncle) let out an exaggerated cry, lunging forward to catch Jin Wansan, then turned back to roar at Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu in grief and indignation, "You saw it! You saw it!"

"Unfilial daughter! The unfilial daughter has angered her own father to death! Quick! Call the physician!!"

chapters.title: House Arrest in the Embroidery Tower, the Humiliation of Fifty Taels
chapters.content:
The moment Jin Wansan collapsed, Jin Wans嗣’s cry of "unfilial daughter," filled with grief and indignation, fell upon Jin Yu like a heavy iron pot, pinning her down.

The servants scrambled to fetch a physician, who rushed in, breathless. After checking the pulse while stroking his beard, the physician concluded: the old master had suffered a surge of anger that caused his blood to rush to his head. Fortunately, there was no major damage, but he must not be subjected to any further agitation and required absolute rest.

Those six words, "must not be subjected to further agitation," became Jin Wans嗣’s most potent weapon.

In front of all the clan members and stewards, he pointed at Jin Yu with a look of profound heartbreak: "Your father has toiled for the Jin family his entire life, and now he has been driven to this state by you, an unfilial daughter! The physician said he cannot bear to see you again!"

"For the sake of your father’s health, from this day forward, Jin Yu, you are relieved of all duties regarding the family’s affairs."

He turned to the accountant, who was already pale with terror, and spoke with stern severity: "Hand over the keys and the seal of the accounting office. I, your second uncle, shall take custody of them for the time being!"

Jin Yu was trembling with rage, her phoenix eyes nearly spitting fire.

"Jin Wans嗣, by what right!"

"By the right of being your second uncle! By the right of being a man of the Jin family!"

Jin Wans嗣 straightened his back, as if holding a royal decree in his hand. "A woman like you, rebellious and unfilial, nearly causing your own father’s death—what face do you have left to manage the family business?!"

"Men!" With a wave of his hand, several burly servants, whom he had long since bought off, immediately surrounded her.

"‘Escort’ the eldest miss back to the embroidery tower in the backyard! Without my orders, she is not to step one foot outside her door!"

"Let’s see who dares!" Jin Yu’s voice was sharp and cold, her gaze sweeping over the servants like a blade.

Intimidated by her usual authority, the servants hesitated, not daring to step forward.

Jin Wans嗣 sneered, his voice drifting over languidly: "What? Do you want to watch the master be angered to death? If that happens, every one of you will be an accomplice!"

This sentence was the final straw.

With Jin Wansan’s life supposedly hanging in the balance, all of Jin Yu’s resistance appeared pale and weak, serving only as ironclad proof of her "unfilial" nature.

Wang Quan and other loyal servants tried to step forward, but they were blocked by the men Jin Wans嗣 had brought, unable to get anywhere near her.

Chen Yinyu was squeezed to the edge of the crowd. His injured leg made it impossible for him to move easily, and he could only watch helplessly as Jin Yu was half-pushed, half-dragged by the servants toward the backyard.

As she passed by him, Jin Yu turned her head abruptly and gave him a deep, lingering look.

In that gaze, there was no fear, no pleading, only a raging fire and a trace of... a request.

She trusted him, even in this desperate situation where heaven and earth seemed deaf to her cries.

Chen Yinyu met her gaze and gave a slight, almost imperceptible nod.

Jin Yu was taken away. The vast Jin estate was turned upside down overnight.

Having secured the keys to the accounting office, Jin Wans嗣 announced with the arrogance of a triumphant general that, while the master was recuperating, he would have full authority over all affairs in the household.

The servants, fickle as grass in the wind, immediately saw which way the wind was blowing.

They were as disdainful toward Chen Yinyu now as they had been fawning before.

Chen Yinyu was "settled" into the most remote guest room in the outer courtyard, without even a servant to attend to him.

At dusk, a young servant brought a food box, and too lazy to even knock, he kicked the door open.

With a loud "bang," the food box was slammed onto the table.

"Son-in-law, time to eat." The servant’s tone was full of contempt; he didn't even bother to call him "Master Chen."

Chen Yinyu opened the box.

Inside was only a bowl of cold rice that had congealed into a lump and a dish of leftovers that were unrecognizable, with disgusting congealed grease clinging to the vegetable leaves.

This swill, which even the lowest servants of the Jin household wouldn't eat, had been brazenly served to him, the "son-in-law."

Chen Yinyu looked at the bowl of rice quietly, his face expressionless, though the color in his peach-blossom eyes was colder than the night outside.

Seeing him motionless, the servant sneered: "What? Not good enough? You should be grateful to have anything at all. Do you still think you’re the pampered son-in-law you once were? Look at the eldest miss—she can’t even save herself!"

With that, he spat on the floor and turned to walk away.

The door remained wide open, letting in the cold wind that made the candle flame on the table flicker wildly, as if it might go out at any moment.

Chen Yinyu slowly closed the food box. He did not get angry; he simply braced himself against the table to stand up, walked to the window, and looked quietly toward the inner courtyard.

There, the tall embroidery tower stood dark and silent, like a giant cage.

Before long, a chaotic sound of footsteps approached. Jin Wans嗣 walked in, beaming with joy, accompanied by two servants.

As soon as he entered, he fanned his nose with his sleeve in disgust, as if the air in the room were filthy.

His gaze landed on Chen Yinyu, filled with condescending scrutiny and disdain.

"Chen Yinyu," he began slowly, pulling a piece of paper from his robe and tossing it onto the table. "This is a letter of divorce. I have already written it on Yu’er’s behalf."

The paper landed lightly beside the cold food, appearing particularly jarring.

Jin Wans嗣 fished a silver ingot from his sleeve and slapped it onto the table with a "clack." The ingot rolled twice and stopped next to the divorce letter.

"Here are fifty taels of silver. Sign it, take the money, and get out of Jinling City immediately."

His voice carried undisguised malice and threats: "I advise you to be sensible. Otherwise, when the magistrate’s office comes to arrest you... you might not even be able to save your own life."

In his eyes, a pampered gigolo had become nothing more than an ant to be crushed at will now that Jin Yu had lost her power.

Fifty taels was already a massive act of charity.

However, to his surprise, Chen Yinyu was neither angry nor pleading.

He simply turned around slowly, his gaze passing over the divorce letter and landing directly on the silver ingot.

He walked over, picked up the cold, gleaming silver with his slender fingers, and weighed it gently in his palm.

A moment later, Chen Yinyu raised his eyes, and a look of undisguised, almost greedy amusement appeared in those beautiful peach-blossom eyes.

"Second Uncle."

He spoke, his voice still cool and pleasant, but his words were extremely mercenary.

"Fifty taels? Are you trying to dismiss a beggar?"

Jin Wans嗣 was stunned; he had never expected such a reaction.

Chen Yinyu continued: "I, Chen Yinyu, am at least the number one matrilocal son-in-law in Jinling City with a clear market price. Now that I’m being kicked out, am I only worth a measly fifty taels?"

"If word gets out, wouldn't people laugh at the Jin family’s reputation for being so stingy with severance pay?"

He threw the silver back onto the table with a crisp "clink."

Then, he held up five fingers, the smile on his lips deepening.

"At least this much—five hundred taels. I won't sign for a penny less."

Jin Wans嗣 looked at his greedy, insatiable face. First came shock, then a wave of immense disdain and relief washed over him.

He knew it!

A poor scholar is just scum who only cares about money at heart!

All that integrity and aloofness was just a facade!

As soon as he heard there was money to be made, he abandoned even the dignity of being divorced.

"Hmph."

Jin Wans嗣 let out a disdainful snort through his nose. "As expected, a piece of trash that can't be propped up."

He was no longer in a hurry, feeling that everything was under control.

In his view, any problem that could be solved with money was no problem at all. The more greedy Chen Yinyu was, the easier he would be to handle.

"Five hundred taels?"

Jin Wans嗣 crossed his arms and mocked him from above. "You really have some nerve, but... very well."

He needed Chen Yinyu to leave as soon as possible to give the magistrate an explanation and to completely cut off any lingering hopes Jin Yu might have.

"Five hundred taels it is. But I control the cash in the estate, and I can't scrape that much together all at once."

He put on a charitable air: "Wait here. In two days at most, I will have the money. You sign the divorce letter, and then get out."

"Very well, I shall await Second Uncle’s good news." Chen Yinyu smiled, his eyes curving like a fox that had stolen a treat.

Jin Wans嗣 looked at him with disgust, as if looking at him for one second longer would dirty his own eyes, and turned to leave with his men.

The door was closed again, and silence returned to the room.

The smile on Chen Yinyu’s face vanished without a trace. He walked to the table, ignored the divorce letter, picked up the bowl of cold rice, and walked to the window.

Outside, the number of patrolling servants had more than doubled, all holding clubs and watching the surroundings vigilantly.

The Jin estate had become an impenetrable cage.

Chen Yinyu dumped the cold rice into the bushes outside the window and placed the empty bowl on the windowsill.

He took a very fine charcoal pencil from his sleeve and a small scrap of paper he had torn from somewhere.

By the dim candlelight, he quickly wrote a few characters on the paper, his handwriting small and clear.

After finishing, he folded the paper and hid it in his sleeve, then picked up the empty bowl and headed toward the kitchen.

The kitchen was brightly lit, and several cooks were whispering, talking of nothing but the Jin family’s change of fortune and the eldest miss’s downfall.

When they saw Chen Yinyu enter, their chatter stopped abruptly, and they all wore expressions of wanting to watch a show.

Just then, an anxious voice came from the kitchen doorway.

"Son-in-law!"

It was Wang Quan.

The loyal old steward had somehow gotten the news and rushed over, his face full of worry.

"Son-in-law, are... are you alright? The eldest miss, she..."

"Steward Wang."

Chen Yinyu interrupted him and handed over the empty bowl. "I’m hungry. Could you help me get something to eat?"

Wang Quan looked at the empty bowl in his hand and then at his pale face, his eyes instantly reddening.

He quickly took the bowl and choked out: "Wait here, Son-in-law, this old servant will go make something for you right now!"

At the very moment their hands met to exchange the bowl, Chen Yinyu’s fingers moved swiftly, and a small slip of paper slid silently and invisibly from his sleeve into Wang Quan’s broad palm.

Wang Quan’s body stiffened, and he instinctively gripped his hand shut.

Chen Yinyu acted as if nothing had happened, merely giving him a weak smile, a hint of pleading in his expression: "Steward Wang, please... let’s keep this quiet."

Wang Quan suddenly snapped back to his senses. Looking into Chen Yinyu’s calm, water-like eyes, he understood everything in an instant.

He nodded heavily, clutching the small slip of paper tightly in his hand.

On it rested the only hope for breaking the deadlock.

Late at night.

Chen Yinyu stood alone in the pitch-black courtyard, gazing into the distance at the embroidery tower swallowed by the night.

He knew that Jin Wansi and Zhang Dechang both thought of him as a toothless tiger, a chess piece that could be discarded at will.

They were all waiting to see him make a fool of himself.

But they didn't know that even a rabbit will bite when cornered, and he, Chen Yinyu, had never been a docile rabbit!

chapters.title: Turning the Physician, A Court Gazette Breaks the Deadlock
chapters.content:
The world was silent; at the hour of the Rat, the Jin residence was quieter than ever.

The patrolling servants’ clubs tapped against their palms, making dull "thwack" sounds.

Chen Yinyu pushed aside the food box Wang Quan had brought.

A bowl of steaming shredded chicken noodle soup with two golden poached eggs sat inside, accompanied by several exquisite side dishes.

Wang Quan had cooked this himself, risking discovery by Jin Wansi.

Chen Yinyu picked up his chopsticks but did not eat; he simply stared at the bowl, his eyes dark and deep.

Wang Quan lowered his voice, his aged face full of anxiety and worry: "Young Master, I have found out everything you asked me to inquire about. Physician Liu, who is treating the Master, has been placed in the guest room in the East Wing by the Second Master, with two of his own men guarding the door."

As he spoke, Wang Quan fished a ring of keys and a heavy money pouch from his robes.

"These are the keys to the various small gates of the estate that I secretly had made, and... this is a little bit of savings I’ve gathered over the years. Please take it, Young Master. In case... in case you need money to grease some palms, don't hold back!"

The old steward’s eyes turned red as he spoke.

In his heart, Chen Yinyu was currently fighting alone, which was no different from throwing an egg against a rock.

Chen Yinyu did not take the money pouch. Instead, he pulled the cold ingot of silver from his sleeve—the fifty taels of "severance pay" Jin Wansi had given him.

He placed the silver on the table with a crisp "clink."

"I have money."

Chen Yinyu raised his eyes. There was no trace of despair in his peach-blossom eyes; instead, they flickered with a cold light. "Steward Wang, I only need you to do one thing for me."

"Tell me, Young Master!"

"In the time it takes for a stick of incense to burn, go to the woodshed in the west and set a fire. You don't need to make it too big, just enough to draw the patrols away."

Wang Quan was stunned, then immediately realized the intent and nodded heavily: "This old servant understands!"

...

East Wing guest room.

Physician Liu was twisting his goat-like beard, pacing the room in agitation.

He had been dragged into this turmoil within the Jin family, and his heart was in his throat.

Jin Wansi had promised him a hundred taels of silver to insist that the old master had been made ill by the eldest daughter. As long as he was willing to testify, there would be a heavy reward afterward.

But he felt uneasy; Jin Wansi’s face didn't look like that of a man who could keep a promise.

Just as he was sitting in distress, the window suddenly creaked, and a slender figure slipped in silently.

"Who?" Physician Liu was scared out of his wits and nearly cried out.

The figure turned, and the moonlight illuminated a face that was excessively handsome.

It was Chen Yinyu.

He still walked with a slight limp, yet his gait was steady, and a gentle smile played on his lips.

But that smile sent a chill running up Physician Liu’s spine.

Chen Yinyu walked straight to the table and slammed the fifty-tael ingot onto it with a "thud," the silver light dazzling the physician.

"This is the bribe the Second Uncle gave me to get lost," Chen Yinyu sat down with a smile.

"Physician Liu, how much did the Second Uncle promise you? A hundred taels? Or two hundred?"

Physician Liu’s throat went dry, his lips trembling as he could not speak.

"Do you know," Chen Yinyu’s voice turned cold, "that a man like Jin Wansi is greedy, shortsighted, and narrow-minded? Burning bridges is his specialty."

"Today he uses you and me as his pawns, but have you considered that if the Jin family truly falls into his hands, and he hollows out the family and flees, what will be the fate of the only person who knows the truth?"

"He... he wouldn't dare!" Physician Liu shouted, his bravado failing.

"Why wouldn't he?" Chen Yinyu laughed. "A doctor dies suddenly at home, or slips and falls into the water—who would investigate the truth for you? As for me, the cast-off son-in-law, I would die without a sound."

"Do you think he would leave the two of us as living evidence just to keep a promise?"

Physician Liu was completely stunned. Every word Chen Yinyu said hit him like a heavy hammer.

Cold sweat rolled down his forehead in large beads. "I... I..."

"Right now, you have only one way to survive: help me, and you help yourself. If Jin Yu manages the family, the Jin family will remain a prosperous one, and she won't miss a single cent of your fees. If Jin Wansi manages it, you and I might end up as corpses on the street by tomorrow."

As he spoke, Chen Yinyu pushed the fifty taels of silver toward Physician Liu. "This is the deposit. Once it’s done, Jin Yu will give you another five hundred taels, enough for you to open the largest pharmacy in the capital."

The carrot and the stick.

On one side was a massive sum of five hundred taels and a bright future; on the other was Jin Wansi’s sinister face and the risk of being silenced at any moment.

This multiple-choice question was far too easy to answer.

Physician Liu fell to his knees with a "thud," his voice trembling: "Young Master... no, Master Chen, tell me, what do you want me to do? I will listen to everything you say!"

Chen Yinyu leaned down and whispered a few words in his ear.

Physician Liu’s eyes widened, shifting from terror to confusion, and finally to deep awe.

He looked at the seemingly frail young man before him, feeling he was a hundred times more terrifying than a villain like Jin Wansi, who was strong on the outside but weak on the inside.

...

The next morning.

Jin Wansan’s bedroom was crowded with the clansmen of the Jin family.

Jin Wansi sat by the bed, holding a bowl of ginseng soup, urging with a face full of "filial piety": "Big Brother, just set your mind at ease. I’ll handle the family matters; you just focus on recovering..."

"Get out!" When Jin Wansan spoke, his voice was as hoarse as a broken gong.

Jin Wansi’s face turned the color of a pig’s liver in an instant.

At this moment, Physician Liu walked in with his medicine chest, followed by an anxious-looking Wang Quan.

"Master, the physician is here!"

Physician Liu stepped forward, made a show of taking the pulse for a long time, then stood up, stroking his beard with a solemn expression.

Everyone’s heart jumped into their throats.

They heard Physician Liu sigh deeply and speak slowly: "The Master’s illness cannot be cured by medicine alone."

"What?!" Jin Wansi was the first to jump up. "You quack, what nonsense are you spouting! My brother is clearly..."

"Second Master, please remain calm."

Physician Liu interrupted him, neither humble nor arrogant. "The Master’s pulse is depressed and his blood flow is obstructed; this is caused by a heart ailment, and a heart ailment requires a heart cure!"

"A heart cure? What heart cure?" Jin Wansan asked, propping himself up.

Physician Liu bowed slightly, his voice carrying a mystical tone: "The Jin family is wealthy, but it has always been a family of merchants, and it lacks one thing."

He paused, then said word by word: "It lacks 'nobility'!"

"Now that the Master is consumed by inner fire and stagnation, it is this 'merchant air' suppressing your 'noble destiny.' If you want a complete cure, you must have the aura of great nobility to flush it out!"

"What is the aura of great nobility?" a clan uncle couldn't help but ask.

Physician Liu suddenly raised his voice, his eyes shining with a fanatical light: "A Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar)! If the family can produce a Zhuangyuan, with the Wenqu Star entering your destiny, purple clouds coming from the east, it will surely clear the Master’s stagnation and ensure you live to a hundred, blessing three generations!"

The word "Zhuangyuan" exploded in everyone’s ears like a thunderclap.

A brilliant light instantly erupted in Jin Wansan’s cloudy eyes!

The greatest regret of his life was bearing the title of a merchant, being looked down upon everywhere. He dreamed of changing the family’s status and entering the ranks of the "scholars."

A Zhuangyuan!

These three words spoke directly to his heart!

Jin Wansi’s expression, however, turned ugly to the extreme. He sneered: "A Zhuangyuan? Physician Liu, have you lost your mind? My Jin family has been in business for generations; where would we find a seed of scholarship? Don't tell me you're counting on..."

His gaze swept toward the door like a blade. Before he could finish, a cold voice drifted in.

"Who says the Jin family doesn't have one?"

Everyone turned in unison to see Chen Yinyu, supported by someone, walking in step by step.

He was still wearing that washed-out green robe, his face pale and his frame thin, but his eyes were startlingly bright.

In his hand, he held a scroll of paper.

"What are you doing here, you useless piece of trash?!"

Seeing him was like seeing a fly to Jin Wansi, who barked harshly, "Someone, throw him out!"

"Wait!" Jin Wansan spoke hoarsely, his eyes fixed on Chen Yinyu. "Let him speak!"

Jin Wansi was instantly choked into silence.

Chen Yinyu ignored his fury, walking straight to the bed and slowly unfolding the scroll in his hand.

It was a copy of the *Dajing Court Gazette*.

"Father-in-law, please look. In the third year of Jinghe, in the tenth month, His Majesty, in order to recruit talents from across the world and combat the monopoly of the great clans, specially initiated a new policy."

His slender finger pointed to a line in the Gazette, and he read aloud:

"'For all merchant families, their sons, grandsons, and sons-in-law, if they possess outstanding talent, a clean background, and the backing of their wife’s family, they may pay grain to enter the Imperial Academy, follow the customary procedures to participate in the Autumn and Spring examinations, and compete with the scholars of the world for the Dragon Gate!'"

Boom!

This new policy was like a bolt of lightning, splitting open Jin Wansan’s muddled brain!

A merchant’s son-in-law could participate in the imperial examinations. His gaze instantly shifted from the Gazette to Chen Yinyu’s face.

A Zhuangyuan son-in-law...

A Zhuangyuan son-in-law who could completely change the family’s status and bring honor to his ancestors!

This... this was a hundred, a thousand times more glorious than sending his daughter to be a concubine for that fool!

Jin Wansan’s cracked lips began to tremble. He looked at Chen Yinyu, then at Jin Wansi, whose face was livid, and the scales in his heart began to tilt violently.

He snatched the Gazette, his withered fingers rubbing repeatedly over the words "pay grain to enter the Imperial Academy," and a light erupted in his eyes that had never been seen before.

It was the greed and fanaticism of a merchant who had discovered a massive business opportunity!

chapters.title: Family Meeting, I Dare to Sign a Military Pledge
chapters.content:
"Absurd! This is absolutely absurd!"

Watching his elder brother’s reaction, Jin Wansi quickly snapped out of his shock.

He pointed a finger at Chen Yinyu’s nose, spittle flying as he shouted, "Brother, do not listen to this boy’s flowery lies! What kind of momentous event is the imperial examination? It is like thousands of troops crossing a single-plank bridge. He is a good-for-nothing who relies on a woman for his keep, spending his days painting his brows and powdering his face—and he wants to take the top scholar exam? This is treating the future of the Jin family like a child’s game!"

As soon as he said this, the several clan uncles who had been momentarily swayed by the word "top scholar" instantly calmed down.

Indeed, the imperial examination was far too ethereal and uncertain.

What if he failed? Wouldn't that be a total waste of money and time?

A clan uncle with a goat-like beard spoke up, filled with worry: "Brother, what the second brother says is not without reason. The path of the imperial examination is fraught with difficulties. If, by any chance... wouldn't we be sitting around eating away our savings for these few years?"

"Exactly! The Jin family is currently in a precarious state; how can we afford such a gamble? The Prefect is still watching us!"

"I think this boy is just using a delaying tactic so he can stay in our Jin family and not leave!"

In an instant, the situation that had just turned around shifted back in Jin Wansi's favor.

A triumphant, cold sneer appeared on Jin Wansi’s face. He looked at Chen Yinyu with the contempt one might show an ant: "Did you hear that? You waste, do you think you are worthy of talking about the imperial examinations? You can’t even hold a book steady, and you want to be the top scholar? Stop having your grand, delusional dreams!"

Chen Yinyu listened quietly, his face devoid of any anger at being humiliated. Those beautiful peach-blossom eyes remained calm and ripple-free, as if these people were discussing something that had absolutely nothing to do with him.

Just as Jin Wansi was about to wave his hand to have him dragged out, the bedroom door creaked open.

A slender yet upright figure walked in against the light.

Jin Yu!

Her face was pale, with dark circles under her eyes; it was clear that the past few days of being confined had not been easy.

But in those bright, phoenix eyes burned a terrifying flame, like a provoked leopard ready to unsheathe its claws at any moment.

The murmurs of the crowd ceased abruptly.

Jin Yu did not look at anyone; she walked straight to Chen Yinyu’s side and stood shoulder-to-shoulder with him.

This action silently declared her stance, and Jin Wansi’s expression turned incredibly ugly.

Old Master Jin looked at his daughter’s haggard appearance, his lips moving, but in the end, he could not bring himself to utter a word of reprimand.

Jin Yu’s gaze slowly swept over everyone present, finally landing on Jin Wansi. Her voice was hoarse yet cold: "Second Uncle, are you finished?"

Jin Wansi felt a chill under her gaze, but he braced himself and said, "Jin Yu, don't be fooled by this boy! This is the Jin family’s private business; you are a woman..."

"My father is still alive, and the Jin family’s seal of authority is still in my hands. Since when is it your turn to be the master of the house?" Jin Yu interrupted him without mercy.

She turned her head to look at Chen Yinyu, her eyes filled with a ferocity that masked a flicker of worry she hadn't even noticed herself.

Chen Yinyu gave her a reassuring smile, then turned to the others and bowed slightly.

"I understand the concerns of my uncles. The path of the imperial examination is indeed uncertain, and empty words are truly hard to trust."

As he spoke, he walked to a side desk and said to Wang Quan, "Steward Wang, please provide pen and ink."

Wang Quan was stunned for a moment before hurriedly fetching the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone.

Under the suspicious and uncertain gazes of everyone, Chen Yinyu picked up the brush and dipped it into the thick ink.

With his wrist suspended, his brush moved like a dragon or a snake, and lines of vigorous, powerful calligraphy leaped onto the paper.

After writing, he set down the brush, picked up the paper with the ink still wet, held it high, and read aloud:

"Let this be written as proof!"

"I, the son-in-law Chen Yinyu, having received the Jin family’s grace, am willing to commit to a three-year term to pursue the imperial examinations, to gain merit, and to protect my wife’s family."

"If, within three years, I fail to achieve merit and cannot ensure the safety of the Jin family, I shall voluntarily leave the family, depart with nothing, and spend the rest of my life as a beast of burden for the Jin family to compensate for all expenses and losses incurred during this period!"

"Let this be the proof, witnessed by heaven and earth!"

Boom!

This military order was like a thunderbolt, striking everyone on the crown of their heads!

Depart with nothing!

Compensate for all losses!

What kind of determination and courage was this!

This was no longer a gamble; this was betting his life and his entire future!

Even Jin Wansi was speechless for a moment, staring fixedly at the paper as if he wanted to see right through it.

However, it wasn't over yet.

Before anyone could recover from the massive shock, Chen Yinyu took a thick stack of papers from his sleeve and handed them to Old Master Jin.

"Father-in-law, uncles, I know that a single military order is not enough to put your minds at ease."

"This is a 'Five-Year Development Plan for the Jin Trading Firm' that I have drafted over the past two days."

"What... plan?" The uncles looked at each other, clearly having never heard the term.

Chen Yinyu explained calmly and unhurriedly: "The Prefect is currently eyeing our Jin family with hostility. It is not advisable to make big moves in local business in Jiangnan in the short term."

"My plan is to shrink our local front to avoid his blade, while simultaneously sending people north to open up markets in the capital and the Central Plains."

He pointed to one of the pages: "The Jin family’s greatest advantages are silk and tea, both of which are in high demand in the north. We can use water transport to open up north-south trade routes. Although the cost of water transport is high, as long as the volume of goods is large enough, the profits will cover all costs and even far exceed what we have now."

"Furthermore, I suggest that we should not only focus on high-end luxury goods but also expand into the mid-to-low-end market, such as launching affordable cotton cloth and tea bricks. We should follow the path of small profits but quick turnover, allowing the Jin family’s goods to enter every household in the Great Jing!"

Chen Yinyu spoke eloquently. Many of the old shopkeepers present were confused by the novel terms he used, such as "market expansion," "logistics costs," and "product line extension."

But the detailed analysis and cost accounting accurate to every single expenditure in that plan—these, they could understand!

How could this be a pedantic scholar? This was clearly a business genius more shrewd and far-sighted than any of them, the old veterans of the trade!

An old shopkeeper who managed the warehouse flipped through the plan with trembling hands, muttering to himself: "Heaven... a genius... using the empty boats on the return trip of the water transport to carry northern specialties back to Jiangnan to sell—earning money on both ends... how... how is this brain wired?"

Jin Wansi’s face had turned from liver-colored to deathly gray.

His business experience, which he was so proud of, was like child’s play in the face of this plan, which could be called a "dimensionality reduction strike."

He finally understood that he had lost. This "useless son-in-law" he had always looked down upon not only had the ambition of a top scholar but also the talent to rule the world!

In the bedroom, everyone’s breathing became heavy.

If the military order just now was a high-stakes gamble, then this business plan was a massive, visible, and tangible fortune!

Under the dual temptation of profit and prospects, the eyes of the clan relatives changed completely.

They looked at Chen Yinyu as if they were looking at a walking mountain of gold.

Just then, Jin Yu walked to the bedside and took the seal of the head of the family, which symbolized the highest authority of the Jin family, from Jin Wansan’s trembling hands.

Then, she returned to the table and slammed the heavy jade seal onto it with a loud "thud"!

The crisp sound made everyone shudder.

Jin Yu looked around at the crowd and said firmly:

"Father! Uncles!"

"Today, I will lay it out here! I, Jin Yu, am betting that he, Chen Yinyu, will win!"

"If he loses, this position of head of the Jin family, along with the entire Jin family, will be handed over to you to do as you please!"

"But if he wins..."

Her voice rose sharply, carrying an indisputable dominance and determination:

"From now on, I will be the one in charge of the Jin family! If anyone dares to gossip in front of me or mention the word 'divorce' even once, don't blame me, Jin Yu, for forgetting our family ties and enforcing the family rules!"

The room was dead silent.

Jin Wansan looked at his daughter’s resolute back, then at his son-in-law, who held the plan in his thin hands but seemed capable of holding up the sky. For the first time, a flame called "hope" ignited in his cloudy eyes.

After a long time, he spoke hoarsely, saying only one word.

"Good!"

Jin Wansi’s body went limp, as if he had lost his parents; he knew the situation was lost.

He glared at Chen Yinyu and Jin Yu with resentment, then turned and stumbled away without a word.

The remaining clan relatives looked at each other, then stepped forward one after another, offering fawning and flattering smiles to Jin Yu and Chen Yinyu.

"Eldest Miss is wise!"

"Son-in-law... son-in-law is truly a divine man!"
